また、全国的に住吉神を祀る神社に関して見た場合、『[[住吉大社神代記]]』や『[[延喜式]]』[[延喜式神名帳|神名帳]]（[[927年]]成立）において[[摂津国]]・[[播磨国]]・[[長門国]]・[[筑前国]]・[[壱岐国]]・[[対馬国]]にそれぞれ住吉神社の記載があることから、当社含めこれらの社には朝鮮航路の要所に配置する意図があったとする説もある{{Sfn|岡田精司|2011|pp=86-109}}。この中で、住吉神は神功皇后の征討伝承と不可分であることから国家的な航海守護神に位置づけられていたとし、[[5世紀]]の[[倭の五王]]の頃から[[ヤマト王権]]の軍事・外交に深く関わっていたとする説もある{{Sfn|岡田精司|2011|pp=86-109}}。 === 概史 === ==== 古代 ==== 『続日本紀』[[天平]]9年（[[737年]]）4月乙巳朔条にて、[[伊勢神宮]]などとともに「筑紫住吉」に[[新羅]]の無礼の報告と奉幣がなされた{{Sfn|住吉神社（角川）|1988}}。『[[新抄格勅符抄]]』『新抄格勅符抄』巻10（神事諸家封戸）大同元年（806年）牒（{{Harvnb|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。によれば、[[大同 (日本)|大同]]元年（[[806年]]）には「[[住吉神]]」に[[神封]]36戸が[[筑前国]]から充てられている{{Sfn|住吉神社（角川）|1988}}。また[[承和 (日本)|承和]]14年（[[847年]]）には僧[[円仁]]が、[[仁寿]]2年（[[852年]]）には僧[[円珍]]が入唐にあたって経典の読誦を行なっている{{Sfn|住吉神社（神々）|1984}}。 [[六国史|国史]]では、[[天安 (日本)|天安]]3年（[[859年]]）に筑前国の「住吉神」の[[神階]]が無位から従五位下に昇叙されたと見えるほか、[[元慶]]2年（[[878年]]）『日本三代実録』元慶2年（878年）12月24日条（{{Harvnb|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。には「新羅凶賊」を告げる[[香椎宮]]の託宣を受けて朝廷の奉幣に預かっている{{Sfn|住吉神社（角川）|1988}}。 [[延長 (元号)|延長]]5年（[[927年]]）成立の『[[延喜式]]』[[延喜式神名帳|神名帳]]では、筑前国[[那珂郡 (福岡県)|那珂郡]]に「住吉神社三座 並名神大」と記載され、3座が[[名神大社]]に列している{{Sfn|住吉神社（角川）|1988}}。また『住吉大社神代記』では、「筑前国那珂郡住吉社三前」や「筑前国那珂郡住吉荒魂社三前」の表記で記載されている{{Sfn|岡田精司|2011|pp=86-109}}{{Sfn|住吉神社（神々）|1984}}。[[寛仁]]元年（[[1019年]]）『左経記』寛仁元年（1019年）10月2日条。には[[後一条天皇]]の1代1度の奉幣に預かったほか、[[元永]]2年（[[1119年]]）『中右記』元永2年（1119年）4月26日条。にも住吉社遷宮の日時勘申がなされており、国家神的性格は[[平安時代]]末期にも継続する{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000|pp=576-577}}。 ==== 中世・近世 ==== [[中世]]以降は[[建武 (日本)|建武]]元年（[[1334年]]）の文書を初見として筑前国の[[一宮]]の位置づけにあったとされる{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000|pp=576-577}}。文献では筑前国の一宮として[[筥崎宮]]（福岡市[[東区 (福岡市)|東区]][[箱崎 (福岡市)|箱崎]]）も見られるが、中世以前の史料で一宮の記述が確認されているのは筑前国で住吉神社のみになる{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000|pp=576-577}}。この頃の[[竹崎季長]]の『[[蒙古襲来絵詞]]』では、住吉神社の朱塗りの鳥居が描かれている{{Sfn|住吉神社（式内社）|1978}}。また[[文明 (日本)|文明]]12年（[[1480年]]）には連歌師の[[宗祇]]が参詣しており、『筑紫道記』に戦乱による住吉神社荒廃の様子を記している{{sfn|住吉神社（平凡社）|2004}}。[[戦国時代 (日本)|戦国時代]]には、当社に伝わる古文書を山口の[[大内義隆]]のもとに上進していたところ、[[天文 (元号)|天文]]20年（[[1551年]]）の[[大寧寺の変]]に巻き込まれその一切を散逸したという{{sfn|住吉神社（平凡社）|2004}}。 [[File:Kuroda Nagamasa.jpg|thumb|160px|right|{{center|[[黒田長政]]}}{{small|[[福岡藩]]初代藩主。現在の本殿を再建。}}]] [[江戸時代]]、[[福岡藩|福岡藩主]]となった[[黒田長政]]が[[元和 (日本)|元和]]9年（[[1623年]]）に白銀2,000枚を下行して社殿を再興し、そのときの本殿が現在まで使用されている{{sfn|住吉神社（平凡社）|2004}}。[[天和 (日本)|天和]]3年（[[1683年]]）には3代藩主[[黒田光之]]が社領として30石を寄せ、[[文化 (元号)|文化]]13年（[[1816年]]）には10代藩主[[黒田斉清]]が20石を加増したことにより計50石を有した{{sfn|住吉神社（平凡社）|2004}}。この頃の[[別当寺]]は松花山円福寺であった{{Sfn|住吉神社（角川）|1988}}。 ==== 近代以降 ==== [[明治維新]]後、[[明治]]5年（[[1872年]]）に[[近代社格制度]]において[[県社]]に列し、[[大正]]14年（[[1925年]]）に[[官幣小社]]に昇格した{{Sfn|住吉神社（角川）|1988}}。戦後は[[神社本庁]]の[[別表神社]]に列している。 [[平成]]16年（[[2004年]]）からは境内域周辺（住吉神社遺跡）で発掘調査が開始されている{{Sfn|住吉神社遺跡第1次調査報告|2006|p=6}}。平成26年（[[2014年]]）までの計3次の調査では、中世-近世期の屋敷地の遺構が祭祀に関わる遺物を伴い検出されるとともに[http://bunkazai.city.fukuoka.lg.jp/excavation_news/detail/18/from_sp:1 博多区住吉で中世の屋敷跡を発見! -住吉神社遺跡第3次発掘調査について-]（福岡市ホームページ）。、屋敷地の方位が現在の本殿と一致し、この方位が中世前半まで遡ることも認められた{{Sfn|住吉神社遺跡第1次調査報告|2006|p=6}}。 === 神階 === * [[天安 (日本)|天安]]3年（[[859年]]）1月27日、無位から従五位下 （『[[日本三代実録]]』）『日本三代実録』貞観元年（859年）正月27日条（{{Harvnb|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 - 表記は「住吉神」。 === 神職・社領 === 神職は、『[[類聚符宣抄]]』の[[天元 (日本)|天元]]2年（[[979年]]）太政官符によると大宮司があったといい、『[[吾妻鏡]]』には[[源頼朝]]にも仕えた神官として佐伯氏の名が見え{{sfn|住吉神社（平凡社）|2004}}、その後は佐伯氏末裔の横田氏が代々担ったという{{Sfn|住吉神社（神々）|1984}}。社領は文献に「住吉庄」と見え、その所属は後白河院領、宣陽門院領、伏見院領、天皇家領と変遷しながら継続した{{Sfn|住吉神社（角川）|1988}}。 [[天保]]時代の大宮司・横田織江は、[[福岡藩]]に禁じられた神道式祭祀の復活を願い、[[筥崎宮]]や[[宇美八幡宮]]の大宮司らと[[京都]]の[[一条家]]に訴え出たところ、藩から帰郷命令が出て逮捕され、天保4年（1833年）、隠居と[[座敷牢]]での謹慎を命じられた『大三輪長兵衛の生涯』葦津泰国（葦津事務所、2008年）p42。 == 境内 == [[File:Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka), honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|本殿（重要文化財）}}{{small|社殿形式は「住吉造」である。}}]] 境内の広さは8,107坪（2.68ヘクタール）。博多が砂丘上に立地するのとは異なり、境内周辺は那珂川の沖積地に立地する。 境内社殿のうち[[神社建築#本殿|'''本殿''']]は、[[江戸時代]]前期の[[元和 (日本)|元和]]9年（[[1623年]]）の[[福岡藩|福岡藩主]][[黒田長政]]による造営。[[神明造]]・[[大社造]]と並んで、古い社殿形式とされる「'''[[住吉造]]'''」{{Sfn|稲垣|2000|p=174}}{{Sfn|米澤|2016|pp=112-113}}を採用する。桁行（奥行）4間・梁間（間口）2間の[[切妻造]]で、屋根は[[檜皮葺]]。屋根やそれに付す[[破風]]・[[千木・鰹木|千木・堅魚木]]3本が直線的である点は、古式建築を反映する。柱は朱色、板壁は白色で彩る。{{Sfn|岡田精司|2011|pp=86-109}}。国の[[重要文化財]]に指定されている[http://www.fsg.pref.fukuoka.jp/bunka/contents_detail.asp?table=t6&fields=f767&id=1307-4&bunrui=kuni_yuke_kenz_juyo 住吉神社本殿]（ふくおか社会教育ネットワーク「福岡県の文化財」）。[http://bunkazai.city.fukuoka.lg.jp/cultural_properties/detail/140 住吉神社本殿]（福岡市文化財保護課「福岡市の文化財」）。。 本殿前に建てられている[[神社建築#拝殿|'''拝殿''']]は、[[入母屋造]]で、屋根は銅板葺。また境内南側にある[[住吉神社能楽殿|能楽殿]]（のうがくでん）は、[[警固神社]]（福岡市中央区天神）能楽堂の老朽化に伴い[[昭和]]10年（[[1935年]]）から住吉神社内での造営が計画され、昭和13年（[[1938年]]）に完成したものになる。[[入母屋造]]の妻入りで、屋根は波子鉄板葺。この能楽殿は日本の伝統様式と洋風の様式を一体とした近代和風建築であり、福岡市指定文化財に指定されている[http://bunkazai.city.fukuoka.lg.jp/cultural_properties/detail/158 住吉神社能楽殿]（福岡市文化財保護課「福岡市の文化財」）。境内説明板。。 そのほか、境内には神楽殿・神門などの社殿がある。 ファイル:住吉大社 本殿平面図.tif|住吉造の平面図 File:Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka) nougakuden.JPG|能楽殿（福岡市指定文化財）の入る建物 File:Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka) shinmon.JPG|神門 File:Shimboku "Ichiya no Matsu" of Sumiyoshi Shrine.JPG|神木「一夜松」 File:Sumiyoshi Mikka Ebisu Jinja pond.JPG|功徳池
{{small|昔は放生会の神事が行われたという。}} File:Tenryu Ike Sumiyoshi.JPG|天竜池（汐入池） == 摂社 == 摂末社は、摂社2社・末社6社の計8社。 === 摂社 === [[File:Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka), Shiga-jinja and Funadama-jinja.JPG|thumb|230px|right|{{center|船玉神社（右）と志賀神社（左）}}]] * 船玉神社（ふなたまじんじゃ） - 祭神：[[サルタヒコ|猿田彦命]]。例祭：9月9日。 * 志賀神社（しがじんじゃ） - 祭神：[[ワタツミ|綿津見三神]]。例祭：6月1日。 === 末社 === * 少彦名神社 - 祭神：[[スクナビコナ|少彦名命]]。例祭：6月8日。 * 稲荷神社 - 祭神：[[ウカノミタマ|宇賀乃魂]]。例祭：10月10日。 * 恵比須神社 - 祭神：[[事代主|事代主命]]。例祭：1月3日。 * 菅原神社（天満宮） - 祭神：[[菅原道真]]。例祭：8月25日。 * 人丸神社 - 祭神：[[柿本人麻呂|柿本人麿]]。例祭：3月18日。 * 天津神社 - 西門外に鎮座。祭神：[[イザナギ|伊弉諾大神]]。例祭：4月22日。 そのほかに関係社として千代森神社（福岡市博多区千代）、下照姫神社（福岡市博多区祇園町）、[[鉄道神社 (福岡市)|鉄道神社]]（福岡市博多区博多駅中央街、[[JR博多シティ]]屋上）がある。 File:Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka), Sukunahikona-jinja.JPG|少彦名神社 File:Uga Shrine in Sumiyoshi Shrine.JPG|稲荷神社 File:住吉神社＿恵比須神社.jpg|恵比須神社 File:Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka), Sugawara-jinja and Hitomaru-jinja.JPG|菅原神社（左、天満宮）・人丸神社（右） File:Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka), Amatsu-jinja.JPG|天津神社 == 祭事 == === 年間祭事 ===
年間祭事一覧
住吉神社で年間に行われる祭事の一覧[http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/index.html 祭典・行事について]（公式サイト）。。 * 1月 ** 歳旦祭 （1月1日） ** 住吉三日恵比須神社例祭 （1月3日） ** 追儺祭 （1月7日） * 2月 ** 節分祭 （2月3日） ** 稲荷神社初午祭 （2月初午） ** 建国記念祭 （2月11日） * 3月 ** 御田祭 （3月7日） ** 人丸神社例祭 （3月18日） * 4月 ** 潮干祭 （4月3日） ** 天津神社例祭 （4月22日） *　6月 ** 船玉神社例祭 （6月1日） ** 少彦名神社例祭 （6月8日） ** 大祓式 （6月30日） * 7月 ** 名越大祭 （7月30日-8月1日） * 8月 ** 菅原神社例祭 （8月25日） * 9月 ** 早穂祭 （9月4日） ** 志賀神社例祭 （9月9日） * 10月 ** 稲荷神社例祭 （10月10日） ** '''例大祭'''（'''相撲会大祭'''/相撲会祭） （10月12日-14日） ** 神宮遙拝式 （10月17日） * 11月 ** 歩射祭 （11月7日） ** 稲荷神社鞴祭、少彦名神社例祭 （11月8日） ** 官幣社列格記念祭 （11月10日） ** 新穀感謝大祭 （11月23日） * 12月 ** 大祓式、除夜祭 （12月31日）
=== 主な祭事 === ; 追儺祭 : 「ついなさい」。1月7日。皇室・国家の繁栄祈願として、鬼すべ・鷽替え（うそ替え）神事を行う[http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/winter.html 冬の祭典・行事]（公式サイト）。 ; 御田祭 : 「おんださい」。3月7日。五穀豊穣祈願として、播種神事を行う[http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/spring.html 春の祭典・行事]（公式サイト）。 ; 潮干祭 : 「しおひさい」。4月3日。航海安全・豊漁祈願として神幸（神輿渡御）を行う。かつて門前に海が広がった頃には船での神幸であったというが、現在は陸上での神幸として行う。 ; 名越大祭 : 「なごしたいさい」。7月30日から8月1日。伊弉諾尊の禊で住吉神が生まれたことに関係する神事で、穢れ祓いとして茅の輪くぐりや人形流しの神事を行う[http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/summer.html 夏の祭典・行事]（公式サイト）。 ; 例大祭 : 「'''相撲会大祭'''（すもうえたいさい）」または単に「相撲会祭」とも。10月12日から14日。住吉神社で最も重要な祭。神功皇后が朝鮮から帰国したとき、住吉神に対して神恩感謝として相撲・[[流鏑馬]]を奉納したことに由来するという。祭事では、稚児行列のほか・流鏑馬・少年相撲が奉納される[http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/autumn.html 秋の祭典・行事]（公式サイト）。 ; 歩射祭 : 「ほしゃさい」。11月7日。元慶2年（878年）の[[陽成天皇]]の奉幣の際、住吉神の霊験により外賊の災いがなくなったことの謝礼として、[[大宰府]]役人が南西（裏鬼門）方向に歩射を行なったことが由来とされる神事。国家鎮護祈願として社前で歩射を行う。 == 文化財 == === 重要文化財（国指定） === * 本殿（建造物） - [[江戸時代]]前期。1922年（大正11年）4月13日指定{{国指定文化財等データベース|102|3464|住吉神社本殿}}。 === 福岡県指定文化財 === * 有形文化財[https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~ri5t-mk/itiran/koukosiryo.html 考古資料一覧]（福岡市の文化財<個人サイト>）。 ** 銅戈 6口（考古資料） **: [[弥生時代]]中期の[[銅戈]]。社殿裏から出土したと伝えるが、出土状態・位置は不明。中細型で、全長は34センチメートル前後。1958年（昭和33年）10月29日指定[http://www.fsg.pref.fukuoka.jp/bunka/contents_detail.asp?table=t61&fields=f2293&id=1307-112&bunrui=kenn_yuke_biju_koko 銅戈]（ふくおか社会教育ネットワーク「福岡県の文化財」）。。 ** 銅鉾 5口（考古資料） **: 弥生時代中期の[[銅矛|銅鉾（銅矛）]]。銅戈同様に社殿裏から出土したと伝えるが、出土状態・位置は不明。1958年（昭和33年）10月29日指定[http://www.fsg.pref.fukuoka.jp/bunka/contents_detail.asp?table=t61&fields=f2293&id=1307-113&bunrui=kenn_yuke_biju_koko 銅鉾]（ふくおか社会教育ネットワーク「福岡県の文化財」）。。 === 福岡市指定文化財 === * 有形文化財[https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~ri5t-mk/itiran/kenzoubutu.html 有形文化財 建造物一覧]（福岡市の文化財<個人サイト>）。[https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~ri5t-mk/itiran/komonjo.html 書籍・典籍・古書 一覧]（福岡市の文化財<個人サイト>）。 ** 能楽殿（建造物） - 昭和13年（1938年）造営。2000年（平成12年）3月23日指定。 ** 唐門（建造物） - 江戸時代の造営。2010（平成22年）3月18日指定。 ** 松花和歌集巻第五 1巻（書籍・典籍・古書） - [[鎌倉時代]]末の歌集。1987年（昭和62年）3月30日指定。 ** 住吉神社文書 27点（書籍・典籍・古書） - 鎌倉時代以降の文書。1987年（昭和62年）3月30日指定。 === その他 === * 博多古図 - 中世期の博多の様子を描いた絵図。 * 住吉大明神御縁起 - 17世紀末成立の縁起。 == 和歌 == * [[寛弘]]2年（[[1005年]]）、[[藤原高遠]]参詣時の歌{{Sfn|住吉神社（平凡社）|2004}} {{Cquote|すみよしと　思ふにはあらで　ちはやぶる　神のこころを　まつるなりけり|20px||大宰大弐[[藤原高遠]]、『大弐高遠集』}} == 現地情報 == '''所在地''' * [[福岡県]][[福岡市]][[博多区]][[住吉 {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q29682]] Wikidata name: Sumiyoshi Shrine [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:35, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Sumiyoshi Shrine
住吉神社 | image = Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka) haiden-1.JPG | caption = Haiden of Sumiyoshi Shrine {{Infobox mapframe|tyep=shape|zoom=14|frame-width=240}} | map_type = Japan Fukuoka Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|33|35|9.26|N|130|24|49.33|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title, inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = Sumiyoshi Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = Sumiyoshi | deity = [[Sumiyoshi sanjin]] | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = 3-1-51 Sumiyoshi, Hakata-ku, Fukuoka-shi, Fukuoka-ken | website = | architecture_style = Sumiyoshi-zukuri | festival = October 13 | leadership = | footnotes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=pink|text align=center|[[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]}} }} {{nihongo|'''Sumiyoshi Shrine'''|住吉神社}} is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] in the Sumiyoshi neighborhood of [[:en:Hakata-ku, Fukuoka|Hakata-ku, Fukuoka]] in [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]], [[:en:Japan|Japan]]. It is the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of former [[:en:Chikuzen Province|Chikuzen Province]]. The main festival of the shrine is held annually on October 13.{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}} Along with the more famous [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]] in [[:en:Osaka|Osaka]] and the [[Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shimonoseki)|Sumiyoshi Jinja]] in [[:en:Shimonoseki, Yamaguchi|Shimonoseki, Yamaguchi]], it is one of the "Three Great Sumiyoshi" shrines.{{cite encyclopedia|last=Yonei|first=Teruyoshi|title=Aramitama|url=http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=1180|encyclopedia=Encyclopedia of Shinto|publisher=Kokugakuin University|access-date=5 February 2011}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''[[kami]]'' enshrined at Sumiyoshi Jinja are: * {{nihongo|'''[[Sumiyoshi sanjin]]'''| 住吉三神|}} * {{nihongo|'''[[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]]'''| 神功皇后|}} * {{nihongo|'''[[Amaterasu]]'''|天照皇大神 |}} ==Origins== Per the shrine's legend (''Chikuzen Sumiyoshi Daimyojin Goengi''), the shrine is the birthplace of the Sumiyoshi cult and the origin for all Sumiyoshi shrines in the country. Unlike Hakata, which is located on sand dunes, the area surrounding the shrine grounds is located on the alluvial land of the Naka River, and topographically located on the cape of Reizeitsu, which juts out into the mouths of the Hie River and the Naka River. This was thought to be a suitable location for a place of worship for the guardian deity of navigation. Bronze spear and a bronze sword from the [[:en:Yayoi Period|Yayoi Period]] have been excavated from the shrine grounds, and it is theorized that this area was originally a sacred place for [[:en:Nakoku|Nakoku]] or the Amabe maritime tribe. ==History== The foundation of the Sumitomo Shrine in Hakozaki is unknown. It first appears in historical documentation in an entry in the ''[[Shoku Nihongi]]'' dated April 737, when it is recorded that offerings were made to "Chikushi Sumiyoshi" and to [[Ise Grand Shrine]] in response to disrespectful actions by the kingdom of [[:en:Silla|Silla]] in the [[:en:Korea|Korea]]. Per a survey dated 806, 36 shrines were dedicated to Sumiyoshi in Chikuzen Province, and in 847 the monk [[:en:Ennin|Ennin]] and in 852 the monk [[:en:Enchin|Enchin]] recited Buddhist sutras at the shrine on their return from [[:en:Tang China|Tang China]]. In 878, it was placed under the direct protection of the Imperial Court after an oracle at [[ Kashii-gū]] warned of a possible attack by Silla. In the ''[[Engishiki]]'', the shrine is listed as a ''Myojin Taisha'' and in 1019, the shrine was entrusted to [[:en:Emperor Go-Ichijō|Emperor Go-Ichijō]] as a "once-in-a-generation" offering. It has been regarded as the ''ichinomiya'' of Chikuzen Province since the late [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]]. [[:en:Takezaki Suenaga|Takezaki Suenaga]]'s ''[[Mōko Shūrai Ekotoba]]'' depicts the vermilion torii gate of Sumiyoshi Shrine. In 1480, the ''[[:en:Renga|Renga]]'' master [[:en:Sōgi|Sōgi]] visited the shrine, and wrote about the devastation of Sumiyoshi Shrine due to war in the "Tsukushi Doki". During the [[:en:Sengoku period|Sengoku period]], the shrine records and old documents were taken by [[:en:Ōuchi Yoshitaka|Ōuchi Yoshitaka]] to [[:en:Yamaguchi, Yamaguchi|Yamaguchi]] and were destroyed in the [[:en:Tainei-ji incident|Tainei-ji incident]] of 1551. The current shrine was restored by [[:en:Kuroda Nagamasa|Kuroda Nagamasa]], the first ''[[:en:Daimyō|Daimyō]]'' of [[:en:Fukuoka Domain|Fukuoka Domain]] in 1623. Subsequent rulers of the domain continued to support the shrine to the [[Meiji Restoration|Meiji restoration]]. Under the [[:en:Government of Meiji Japan|Government of Meiji Japan]]'s [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]]'s system of [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|Ranked Shinto shrines]], Sumiyoshi Shrine was Ranked as a Prefectural Shrine in 1872, and promoted to a {{nihongo|Imperial shrine, 3rd Rank|官幣小社|Kanpei-shōsha}} in 1925. In 2004, [[archaeological excavation]]s began around the precincts. In a total of three excavations up to 2014, the remains of a mansion from the medieval to early modern period were discovered along with artifacts related to rituals. ==Cultural Properties== *{{nihongo|'''Honden'''|本殿||}} - The main hall of the shrine was built by Kuroda Nagamasa in 1623 during the early Edo period. It is in the ''Sumiyoshi-zukuri'' style, which is considered to be an older form of shrine architecture. It is a gabled structure and the roof is thatched with cypress bark. The pillars are painted vermilion and the wooden walls are painted white. It was designated as a National [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1922.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/3464|title=住吉神社本殿|language=ja |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=December 20, 2023}} ==Gallery== Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka) torii.JPG|Torii Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka), honden.JPG|Honden (ICP) Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka) nougakuden.JPG|Noh Theatre ==See also== *[[Ichinomiya]] ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons Category|Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka)}} *[https://www.nihondaiichisumiyoshigu.jp Official home page]{{in lang|ja}} *[https://bunkazai.city.fukuoka.lg.jp/cultural_properties/detail/93 Cultural Properties of Fukuoka City]{{in lang|ja}} *[https://www.crossroadfukuoka.jp/spot/12552 Fukuoka Tourism Web]{{in lang|ja}} {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ {{Ichinomiya}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shinto shrines in Fukuoka Prefecture]] [[Category:Chikuzen Province]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Fukuoka]] [[Category:Ichinomiya]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Kanpei Shōsha]] [[Category:Sumiyoshi shrines]] [[sn:Sumiyoshi Shrine (Fukuoka)]]}} [[sn:Sumiyoshi Shrine (Fukuoka)]] [[en:Sumiyoshi Shrine (Fukuoka)]] [[sn:umiyoshi Shrine (Fukuoka)]] [[sn: failed]] [[Category:Pages without translation templates]] [[Category:pages with valid en interwikis 2]] {{Commons category|Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka)}} [[de:Sumiyoshi-Schrein (Fukuoka)]] [[fr:Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka)]] [[ja:住吉神社 (福岡市)]] [[Category:Pages with simple english wikipedia interwikis]]Sumiyoshi Shrine (Fukuoka)]] [[zh:住吉神社 (福岡市)]]

The main festival of the shrine is held annually on October 13.{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}} Along with the more famous [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]] in [[:en:Osaka|Osaka]] and the [[Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shimonoseki)|Sumiyoshi Jinja]] in [[:en:Shimonoseki, Yamaguchi|Shimonoseki, Yamaguchi]], it is one of the "Three Great Sumiyoshi" shrines.{{cite encyclopedia|last=Yonei|first=Teruyoshi|title=Aramitama|url=http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=1180|encyclopedia=Encyclopedia of Shinto|publisher=Kokugakuin University|access-date=5 February 2011}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''[[kami]]'' enshrined at Sumiyoshi Jinja are: * {{nihongo|'''[[Sumiyoshi sanjin]]'''| 住吉三神|}} * {{nihongo|'''[[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]]'''| 神功皇后|}} * {{nihongo|'''[[Amaterasu]]'''|天照皇大神 |}} ==Origins== Per the shrine's legend (''Chikuzen Sumiyoshi Daimyojin Goengi''), the shrine is the birthplace of the Sumiyoshi cult and the origin for all Sumiyoshi shrines in the country. Unlike Hakata, which is located on sand dunes, the area surrounding the shrine grounds is located on the alluvial land of the Naka River, and topographically located on the cape of Reizeitsu, which juts out into the mouths of the Hie River and the Naka River. This was thought to be a suitable location for a place of worship for the guardian deity of navigation. Bronze spear and a bronze sword from the [[:en:Yayoi Period|Yayoi Period]] have been excavated from the shrine grounds, and it is theorized that this area was originally a sacred place for [[:en:Nakoku|Nakoku]] or the Amabe maritime tribe. ==History== The foundation of the Sumitomo Shrine in Hakozaki is unknown. It first appears in historical documentation in an entry in the ''[[Shoku Nihongi]]'' dated April 737, when it is recorded that offerings were made to "Chikushi Sumiyoshi" and to [[Ise Grand Shrine]] in response to disrespectful actions by the kingdom of [[:en:Silla|Silla]] in the [[:en:Korea|Korea]]. Per a survey dated 806, 36 shrines were dedicated to Sumiyoshi in Chikuzen Province, and in 847 the monk [[:en:Ennin|Ennin]] and in 852 the monk [[:en:Enchin|Enchin]] recited Buddhist sutras at the shrine on their return from [[:en:Tang China|Tang China]]. In 878, it was placed under the direct protection of the Imperial Court after an oracle at [[ Kashii-gū]] warned of a possible attack by Silla. In the ''[[Engishiki]]'', the shrine is listed as a ''Myōjin Taisha'' and in 1019, the shrine was entrusted to [[:en:Emperor Go-Ichijō|Emperor Go-Ichijō]] as a "once-in-a-generation" offering. It has been regarded as the ''ichinomiya'' of Chikuzen Province since the late [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]]. [[:en:Takezaki Suenaga|Takezaki Suenaga]]'s ''[[Mōko Shūrai Ekotoba]]'' depicts the vermilion torii gate of Sumiyoshi Shrine. In 1480, the ''[[:en:Renga|Renga]]'' master [[:en:Sōgi|Sōgi]] visited the shrine, and wrote about the devastation of Sumiyoshi Shrine due to war in the "Tsukushi Doki". During the [[:en:Sengoku period|Sengoku period]], the shrine records and old documents were taken by [[:en:Ōuchi Yoshitaka|Ōuchi Yoshitaka]] to [[:en:Yamaguchi, Yamaguchi|Yamaguchi]] and were destroyed in the [[:en:Tainei-ji incident|Tainei-ji incident]] of 1551. The current shrine was restored by [[:en:Kuroda Nagamasa|Kuroda Nagamasa]], the first ''[[:en:Daimyō|Daimyō]]'' of [[:en:Fukuoka Domain|Fukuoka Domain]] in 1623. Subsequent rulers of the domain continued to support the shrine to the [[Meiji Restoration|Meiji restoration]]. Under the [[:en:Government of Meiji Japan|Government of Meiji Japan]]'s [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]]'s system of [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|Ranked Shinto shrines]], Sumiyoshi Shrine was Ranked as a Prefectural Shrine in 1872, and promoted to a {{nihongo|Imperial shrine, 3rd Rank|官幣小社|Kanpei-shōsha}} in 1925. In 2004, [[archaeological excavation]]s began around the precincts. In a total of three excavations up to 2014, the remains of a mansion from the medieval to early modern period were discovered along with artifacts related to rituals. ==Cultural Properties== *{{nihongo|'''Honden'''|本殿||}} - The main hall of the shrine was built by Kuroda Nagamasa in 1623 during the early Edo period. It is in the ''Sumiyoshi-zukuri'' style, which is considered to be an older form of shrine architecture. It is a gabled structure and the roof is thatched with cypress bark. The pillars are painted vermilion and the wooden walls are painted white. It was designated as a National [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1922.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/3464|title=住吉神社本殿|language=ja |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=December 20, 2023}} ==Gallery== Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka) torii.JPG|Torii Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka), honden.JPG|Honden (ICP) Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka) nougakuden.JPG|Noh Theatre ==See also== *[[Ichinomiya]] ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons Category|Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka)}} *[https://www.nihondaiichisumiyoshigu.jp Official home page]{{in lang|ja}} *[https://bunkazai.city.fukuoka.lg.jp/cultural_properties/detail/93 Cultural Properties of Fukuoka City]{{in lang|ja}} *[https://www.crossroadfukuoka.jp/spot/12552 Fukuoka Tourism Web]{{in lang|ja}} {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ {{Ichinomiya}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shinto shrines in Fukuoka Prefecture]] [[Category:Chikuzen Province]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Fukuoka]] [[Category:Ichinomiya]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Kanpei Shōsha]] [[Category:Sumiyoshi shrines]] [[sn:Sumiyoshi Shrine (Fukuoka)]]}} [[sn:Sumiyoshi Shrine (Fukuoka)]] [[en:Sumiyoshi Shrine (Fukuoka)]] [[sn:umiyoshi Shrine (Fukuoka)]] [[sn: failed]] [[Category:Pages without translation templates]] [[Category:pages with valid en interwikis 2]] {{Commons category|Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka)}} [[de:Sumiyoshi-Schrein (Fukuoka)]] [[fr:Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka)]] [[ja:住吉神社 (福岡市)]] [[Category:Pages with simple english wikipedia interwikis]][[simple:Sumiyoshi Shrine (Fukuoka)]] [[zh:住吉神社 (福岡市)]] {{wikidata link|Q29682}}

住吉神社 | image = Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka) haiden-1.JPG | caption = Haiden of Sumiyoshi Shrine {{Infobox mapframe|tyep=shape|zoom=14|frame-width=240}} | map_type = Japan Fukuoka Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|33|35|9.26|N|130|24|49.33|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title, inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = Sumiyoshi Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = Sumiyoshi | deity = [[Sumiyoshi sanjin]] | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = 3-1-51 Sumiyoshi, Hakata-ku, Fukuoka-shi, Fukuoka-ken | website = | architecture_style = Sumiyoshi-zukuri | festival = October 13 | leadership = | footnotes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=pink|text align=center|[[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]}} }} {{nihongo|'''Sumiyoshi Shrine'''|住吉神社}} is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] in the Sumiyoshi neighborhood of [[:en:Hakata-ku, Fukuoka|Hakata-ku, Fukuoka]] in [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]], [[:en:Japan|Japan]]. It is the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of former [[:en:Chikuzen Province|Chikuzen Province]]. The main festival of the shrine is held annually on October 13.{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}} Along with the more famous [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]] in [[:en:Osaka|Osaka]] and the [[Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shimonoseki)|Sumiyoshi Jinja]] in [[:en:Shimonoseki, Yamaguchi|Shimonoseki, Yamaguchi]], it is one of the "Three Great Sumiyoshi" shrines.{{cite encyclopedia|last=Yonei|first=Teruyoshi|title=Aramitama|url=http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=1180|encyclopedia=Encyclopedia of Shinto|publisher=Kokugakuin University|access-date=5 February 2011}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''[[kami]]'' enshrined at Sumiyoshi Jinja are: * {{nihongo|'''[[Sumiyoshi sanjin]]'''| 住吉三神|}} * {{nihongo|'''[[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]]'''| 神功皇后|}} * {{nihongo|'''[[Amaterasu]]'''|天照皇大神 |}} ==Origins== Per the shrine's legend (''Chikuzen Sumiyoshi Daimyojin Goengi''), the shrine is the birthplace of the Sumiyoshi cult and the origin for all Sumiyoshi shrines in the country. Unlike Hakata, which is located on sand dunes, the area surrounding the shrine grounds is located on the alluvial land of the Naka River, and topographically located on the cape of Reizeitsu, which juts out into the mouths of the Hie River and the Naka River. This was thought to be a suitable location for a place of worship for the guardian deity of navigation. Bronze spear and a bronze sword from the [[:en:Yayoi Period|Yayoi Period]] have been excavated from the shrine grounds, and it is theorized that this area was originally a sacred place for [[:en:Nakoku|Nakoku]] or the Amabe maritime tribe. ==History== The foundation of the Sumitomo Shrine in Hakozaki is unknown. It first appears in historical documentation in an entry in the ''[[Shoku Nihongi]]'' dated April 737, when it is recorded that offerings were made to "Chikushi Sumiyoshi" and to [[Ise Grand Shrine]] in response to disrespectful actions by the kingdom of [[:en:Silla|Silla]] in the [[:en:Korea|Korea]]. Per a survey dated 806, 36 shrines were dedicated to Sumiyoshi in Chikuzen Province, and in 847 the monk [[:en:Ennin|Ennin]] and in 852 the monk [[:en:Enchin|Enchin]] recited Buddhist sutras at the shrine on their return from [[:en:Tang China|Tang China]]. In 878, it was placed under the direct protection of the Imperial Court after an oracle at [[ Kashii-gū]] warned of a possible attack by Silla. In the ''[[Engishiki]]'', the shrine is listed as a ''Myōjin Taisha'' and in 1019, the shrine was entrusted to [[:en:Emperor Go-Ichijō|Emperor Go-Ichijō]] as a "once-in-a-generation" offering. It has been regarded as the ''ichinomiya'' of Chikuzen Province since the late [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]]. [[:en:Takezaki Suenaga|Takezaki Suenaga]]'s ''[[Mōko Shūrai Ekotoba]]'' depicts the vermilion torii gate of Sumiyoshi Shrine. In 1480, the ''[[:en:Renga|Renga]]'' master [[:en:Sōgi|Sōgi]] visited the shrine, and wrote about the devastation of Sumiyoshi Shrine due to war in the "Tsukushi Doki". During the [[:en:Sengoku period|Sengoku period]], the shrine records and old documents were taken by [[:en:Ōuchi Yoshitaka|Ōuchi Yoshitaka]] to [[:en:Yamaguchi, Yamaguchi|Yamaguchi]] and were destroyed in the [[:en:Tainei-ji incident|Tainei-ji incident]] of 1551. The current shrine was restored by [[:en:Kuroda Nagamasa|Kuroda Nagamasa]], the first ''[[:en:Daimyō|Daimyō]]'' of [[:en:Fukuoka Domain|Fukuoka Domain]] in 1623. Subsequent rulers of the domain continued to support the shrine to the [[Meiji Restoration|Meiji restoration]]. Under the [[:en:Government of Meiji Japan|Government of Meiji Japan]]'s [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]]'s system of [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|Ranked Shinto shrines]], Sumiyoshi Shrine was Ranked as a Prefectural Shrine in 1872, and promoted to a {{nihongo|Imperial shrine, 3rd Rank|官幣小社|Kanpei-shōsha}} in 1925. In 2004, [[archaeological excavation]]s began around the precincts. In a total of three excavations up to 2014, the remains of a mansion from the medieval to early modern period were discovered along with artifacts related to rituals. ==Cultural Properties== *{{nihongo|'''Honden'''|本殿||}} - The main hall of the shrine was built by Kuroda Nagamasa in 1623 during the early Edo period. It is in the ''Sumiyoshi-zukuri'' style, which is considered to be an older form of shrine architecture. It is a gabled structure and the roof is thatched with cypress bark. The pillars are painted vermilion and the wooden walls are painted white. It was designated as a National [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1922.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/3464|title=住吉神社本殿|language=ja |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=December 20, 2023}} ==Gallery== Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka) torii.JPG|Torii Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka), honden.JPG|Honden (ICP) Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka) nougakuden.JPG|Noh Theatre ==See also== *[[Ichinomiya]] ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons Category|Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka)}} *[https://www.nihondaiichisumiyoshigu.jp Official home page]{{in lang|ja}} *[https://bunkazai.city.fukuoka.lg.jp/cultural_properties/detail/93 Cultural Properties of Fukuoka City]{{in lang|ja}} *[https://www.crossroadfukuoka.jp/spot/12552 Fukuoka Tourism Web]{{in lang|ja}} {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ {{Ichinomiya}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shinto shrines in Fukuoka Prefecture]] [[Category:Chikuzen Province]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Fukuoka]] [[Category:Ichinomiya]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Kanpei Shōsha]] [[Category:Sumiyoshi shrines]] }} [[en:Sumiyoshi Shrine (Fukuoka)]] [[Category:Pages without translation templates]] [[Category:pages with valid en interwikis 2]] {{Commons category|Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka)}} [[de:Sumiyoshi-Schrein (Fukuoka)]] [[fr:Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka)]] [[ja:住吉神社 (福岡市)]] [[Category:Pages with simple english wikipedia interwikis]][[simple:Sumiyoshi Shrine (Fukuoka)]] [[zh:住吉神社 (福岡市)]] {{wikidata link|Q29682}}

住吉神社 | image = Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka) haiden-1.JPG | caption = Haiden of Sumiyoshi Shrine {{Infobox mapframe|tyep=shape|zoom=14|frame-width=240}} | map_type = Japan Fukuoka Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|33|35|9.26|N|130|24|49.33|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title, inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = Sumiyoshi Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = Sumiyoshi | deity = [[Sumiyoshi sanjin]] | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = 3-1-51 Sumiyoshi, Hakata-ku, Fukuoka-shi, Fukuoka-ken | website = | architecture_style = Sumiyoshi-zukuri | festival = October 13 | leadership = | footnotes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=pink|text align=center|[[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]}} }} {{nihongo|'''Sumiyoshi Shrine'''|住吉神社}} is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] in the Sumiyoshi neighborhood of [[:en:Hakata-ku, Fukuoka|Hakata-ku, Fukuoka]] in [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]], [[:en:Japan|Japan]]. It is the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of former [[:en:Chikuzen Province|Chikuzen Province]]. The main festival of the shrine is held annually on October 13.{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}} Along with the more famous [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]] in [[:en:Osaka|Osaka]] and the [[Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shimonoseki)|Sumiyoshi Jinja]] in [[:en:Shimonoseki, Yamaguchi|Shimonoseki, Yamaguchi]], it is one of the "Three Great Sumiyoshi" shrines.{{cite encyclopedia|last=Yonei|first=Teruyoshi|title=Aramitama|url=http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=1180|encyclopedia=Encyclopedia of Shinto|publisher=Kokugakuin University|access-date=5 February 2011}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''[[kami]]'' enshrined at Sumiyoshi Jinja are: * {{nihongo|'''[[Sumiyoshi sanjin]]'''| 住吉三神|}} * {{nihongo|'''[[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]]'''| 神功皇后|}} * {{nihongo|'''[[Amaterasu]]'''|天照皇大神 |}} ==Origins== Per the shrine's legend (''Chikuzen Sumiyoshi Daimyojin Goengi''), the shrine is the birthplace of the Sumiyoshi cult and the origin for all Sumiyoshi shrines in the country. Unlike Hakata, which is located on sand dunes, the area surrounding the shrine grounds is located on the alluvial land of the Naka River, and topographically located on the cape of Reizeitsu, which juts out into the mouths of the Hie River and the Naka River. This was thought to be a suitable location for a place of worship for the guardian deity of navigation. Bronze spear and a bronze sword from the [[:en:Yayoi Period|Yayoi Period]] have been excavated from the shrine grounds, and it is theorized that this area was originally a sacred place for [[:en:Nakoku|Nakoku]] or the Amabe maritime tribe. ==History== The foundation of the Sumitomo Shrine in Hakozaki is unknown. It first appears in historical documentation in an entry in the ''[[Shoku Nihongi]]'' dated April 737, when it is recorded that offerings were made to "Chikushi Sumiyoshi" and to [[Ise Grand Shrine]] in response to disrespectful actions by the kingdom of [[:en:Silla|Silla]] in the [[:en:Korea|Korea]]. Per a survey dated 806, 36 shrines were dedicated to Sumiyoshi in Chikuzen Province, and in 847 the monk [[:en:Ennin|Ennin]] and in 852 the monk [[:en:Enchin|Enchin]] recited Buddhist sutras at the shrine on their return from [[:en:Tang China|Tang China]]. In 878, it was placed under the direct protection of the Imperial Court after an oracle at [[ Kashii-gū]] warned of a possible attack by Silla. In the ''[[Engishiki]]'', the shrine is listed as a ''Myōjin Taisha'' and in 1019, the shrine was entrusted to [[:en:Emperor Go-Ichijō|Emperor Go-Ichijō]] as a "once-in-a-generation" offering. It has been regarded as the ''ichinomiya'' of Chikuzen Province since the late [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]]. [[:en:Takezaki Suenaga|Takezaki Suenaga]]'s ''[[Mōko Shūrai Ekotoba]]'' depicts the vermilion torii gate of Sumiyoshi Shrine. In 1480, the ''[[:en:Renga|Renga]]'' master [[:en:Sōgi|Sōgi]] visited the shrine, and wrote about the devastation of Sumiyoshi Shrine due to war in the "Tsukushi Doki". During the [[:en:Sengoku period|Sengoku period]], the shrine records and old documents were taken by [[:en:Ōuchi Yoshitaka|Ōuchi Yoshitaka]] to [[:en:Yamaguchi, Yamaguchi|Yamaguchi]] and were destroyed in the [[:en:Tainei-ji incident|Tainei-ji incident]] of 1551. The current shrine was restored by [[:en:Kuroda Nagamasa|Kuroda Nagamasa]], the first ''[[:en:Daimyō|Daimyō]]'' of [[:en:Fukuoka Domain|Fukuoka Domain]] in 1623. Subsequent rulers of the domain continued to support the shrine to the [[Meiji Restoration|Meiji restoration]]. Under the [[:en:Government of Meiji Japan|Government of Meiji Japan]]'s [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]]'s system of [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|Ranked Shinto shrines]], Sumiyoshi Shrine was Ranked as a Prefectural Shrine in 1872, and promoted to a {{nihongo|Imperial shrine, 3rd Rank|官幣小社|Kanpei-shōsha}} in 1925. In 2004, [[archaeological excavation]]s began around the precincts. In a total of three excavations up to 2014, the remains of a mansion from the medieval to early modern period were discovered along with artifacts related to rituals. ==Cultural Properties== *{{nihongo|'''Honden'''|本殿||}} - The main hall of the shrine was built by Kuroda Nagamasa in 1623 during the early Edo period. It is in the ''Sumiyoshi-zukuri'' style, which is considered to be an older form of shrine architecture. It is a gabled structure and the roof is thatched with cypress bark. The pillars are painted vermilion and the wooden walls are painted white. It was designated as a National [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1922.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/3464|title=住吉神社本殿|language=ja |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=December 20, 2023}} ==Gallery== Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka) torii.JPG|Torii Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka), honden.JPG|Honden (ICP) Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka) nougakuden.JPG|Noh Theatre ==See also== *[[Ichinomiya]] ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons Category|Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka)}} *[https://www.nihondaiichisumiyoshigu.jp Official home page]{{in lang|ja}} *[https://bunkazai.city.fukuoka.lg.jp/cultural_properties/detail/93 Cultural Properties of Fukuoka City]{{in lang|ja}} *[https://www.crossroadfukuoka.jp/spot/12552 Fukuoka Tourism Web]{{in lang|ja}} {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ {{Ichinomiya}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shinto shrines in Fukuoka Prefecture]] [[Category:Chikuzen Province]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Fukuoka]] [[Category:Ichinomiya]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Kanpei Shōsha]] [[Category:Sumiyoshi shrines]] }} [[en:Sumiyoshi Shrine (Fukuoka)]] [[Category:Pages without translation templates]] {{Commons category|Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka)}} [[de:Sumiyoshi-Schrein (Fukuoka)]] [[fr:Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka)]] [[ja:住吉神社 (福岡市)]] [[Category:Pages with simple english wikipedia interwikis]][[simple:Sumiyoshi Shrine (Fukuoka)]] [[zh:住吉神社 (福岡市)]] {{wikidata link|Q29682}} [[Category:Wikidata has short description]]

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Sumiyoshi Shrine
住吉神社 | image = Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka) haiden-1.JPG | caption = Haiden of Sumiyoshi Shrine {{Infobox mapframe|tyep=shape|zoom=14|frame-width=240}} | map_type = Japan Fukuoka Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|33|35|9.26|N|130|24|49.33|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title, inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = Sumiyoshi Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = Sumiyoshi | deity = [[Sumiyoshi sanjin]] | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = 3-1-51 Sumiyoshi, Hakata-ku, Fukuoka-shi, Fukuoka-ken | website = | architecture_style = Sumiyoshi-zukuri | festival = October 13 | leadership = | footnotes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=pink|text align=center|[[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]}} }} {{nihongo|'''Sumiyoshi Shrine'''|住吉神社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] in the Sumiyoshi neighborhood of [[Hakata-ku, Fukuoka]] in [[Fukuoka Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It is the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of former [[Chikuzen Province]]. The main festival of the shrine is held annually on October 13.{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}} Along with the more famous [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]] in [[Osaka]] and the [[Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shimonoseki)|Sumiyoshi Jinja]] in [[Shimonoseki, Yamaguchi]], it is one of the "Three Great Sumiyoshi" shrines.{{cite encyclopedia|last=Yonei|first=Teruyoshi|title=Aramitama|url=http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=1180|encyclopedia=Encyclopedia of Shinto|publisher=Kokugakuin University|access-date=5 February 2011}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''[[kami]]'' enshrined at Sumiyoshi Jinja are: * {{nihongo|'''[[Sumiyoshi sanjin]]'''| 住吉三神|}} * {{nihongo|'''[[Empress Jingū]]'''| 神功皇后|}} * {{nihongo|'''[[Amaterasu]]'''|天照皇大神 |}} ==Origins== Per the shrine's legend (''Chikuzen Sumiyoshi Daimyojin Goengi''), the shrine is the birthplace of the Sumiyoshi cult and the origin for all Sumiyoshi shrines in the country. Unlike Hakata, which is located on sand dunes, the area surrounding the shrine grounds is located on the alluvial land of the Naka River, and topographically located on the cape of Reizeitsu, which juts out into the mouths of the Hie River and the Naka River. This was thought to be a suitable location for a place of worship for the guardian deity of navigation. Bronze spear and a bronze sword from the [[Yayoi Period]] have been excavated from the shrine grounds, and it is theorized that this area was originally a sacred place for [[Nakoku]] or the Amabe maritime tribe. ==History== The foundation of the Sumitomo Shrine in Hakozaki is unknown. It first appears in historical documentation in an entry in the ''[[Shoku Nihongi]]'' dated April 737, when it is recorded that offerings were made to "Chikushi Sumiyoshi" and to [[Ise Grand Shrine]] in response to disrespectful actions by the kingdom of [[Silla]] in the [[Korean Peninsula]]. Per a survey dated 806, 36 shrines were dedicated to Sumiyoshi in Chikuzen Province, and in 847 the monk [[Ennin]] and in 852 the monk [[Enchin]] recited Buddhist sutras at the shrine on their return from [[Tang China]]. In 878, it was placed under the direct protection of the Imperial Court after an oracle at [[ Kashii-gū]] warned of a possible attack by Silla. In the ''[[Engishiki]]'', the shrine is listed as a ''Myojin Taisha'' and in 1019, the shrine was entrusted to [[Emperor Go-Ichijō]] as a "once-in-a-generation" offering. It has been regarded as the ''ichinomiya'' of Chikuzen Province since the late [[Heian period]]. [[Takezaki Suenaga]]'s ''[[Mōko Shūrai Ekotoba]]'' depicts the vermilion torii gate of Sumiyoshi Shrine. In 1480, the ''[[renga]]'' master [[Sōgi]] visited the shrine, and wrote about the devastation of Sumiyoshi Shrine due to war in the "Tsukushi Doki". During the [[Sengoku period]], the shrine records and old documents were taken by [[Ōuchi Yoshitaka]] to [[Yamaguchi, Yamaguchi|Yamaguchi]] and were destroyed in the [[Tainei-ji incident]] of 1551. The current shrine was restored by [[Kuroda Nagamasa]], the first ''[[daimyō]]'' of [[Fukuoka Domain]] in 1623. Subsequent rulers of the domain continued to support the shrine to the [[Meiji Restoration|Meiji restoration]]. Under the [[Meiji government]]'s [[State Shinto]]'s system of [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|Ranked Shinto shrines]], Sumiyoshi Shrine was Ranked as a Prefectural Shrine in 1872, and promoted to a {{nihongo|Imperial shrine, 3rd Rank|官幣小社|Kanpei-shōsha}} in 1925. In 2004, [[archaeological excavation]]s began around the precincts. In a total of three excavations up to 2014, the remains of a mansion from the medieval to early modern period were discovered along with artifacts related to rituals. ==Cultural Properties== *{{nihongo|'''Honden'''|本殿||}} - The main hall of the shrine was built by Kuroda Nagamasa in 1623 during the early Edo period. It is in the ''Sumiyoshi-zukuri'' style, which is considered to be an older form of shrine architecture. It is a gabled structure and the roof is thatched with cypress bark. The pillars are painted vermilion and the wooden walls are painted white. It was designated as a National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1922.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/3464|title=住吉神社本殿|language=ja |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=December 20, 2023}} ==Gallery== Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka) torii.JPG|Torii Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka), honden.JPG|Honden (ICP) Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka) nougakuden.JPG|Noh Theatre ==See also== *[[Ichinomiya]] ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons Category|Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka)}} *[https://www.nihondaiichisumiyoshigu.jp Official home page]{{in lang|ja}} *[https://bunkazai.city.fukuoka.lg.jp/cultural_properties/detail/93 Cultural Properties of Fukuoka City]{{in lang|ja}} *[https://www.crossroadfukuoka.jp/spot/12552 Fukuoka Tourism Web]{{in lang|ja}} {{Shinto shrine}} ]] {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ {{Ichinomiya}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shinto shrines in Fukuoka Prefecture]] [[Category:Chikuzen Province]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Fukuoka]] [[Category:Ichinomiya]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Kanpei Shōsha]] [[Category:Shrines dedicated to empress Jingū]] [[Category:Sumiyoshi shrines]] [[Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia 6]] [[Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia]] [[sn:Sumiyoshi Shrine (Fukuoka)]]}} [[sn:Sumiyoshi Shrine (Fukuoka)]] [[en:Sumiyoshi Shrine (Fukuoka)]] [[sn:umiyoshi Shrine (Fukuoka)]] [[sn: failed]] [[Category:Pages without translation templates]] [[Category:pages with valid en interwikis]] [[Category:pages that were shrank]] {{Commons category|Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka)}} [[de:Sumiyoshi-Schrein (Fukuoka)]] [[fr:Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka)]] [[ja:住吉神社 (福岡市)]] [[simple:Sumiyoshi Shrine (Fukuoka)]] [[zh:住吉神社 (福岡市)]]

The main festival of the shrine is held annually on October 13.{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}} Along with the more famous [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]] in [[Osaka]] and the [[Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shimonoseki)|Sumiyoshi Jinja]] in [[Shimonoseki, Yamaguchi]], it is one of the "Three Great Sumiyoshi" shrines.{{cite encyclopedia|last=Yonei|first=Teruyoshi|title=Aramitama|url=http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=1180|encyclopedia=Encyclopedia of Shinto|publisher=Kokugakuin University|access-date=5 February 2011}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''[[kami]]'' enshrined at Sumiyoshi Jinja are: * {{nihongo|'''[[Sumiyoshi sanjin]]'''| 住吉三神|}} * {{nihongo|'''[[Empress Jingū]]'''| 神功皇后|}} * {{nihongo|'''[[Amaterasu]]'''|天照皇大神 |}} ==Origins== Per the shrine's legend (''Chikuzen Sumiyoshi Daimyojin Goengi''), the shrine is the birthplace of the Sumiyoshi cult and the origin for all Sumiyoshi shrines in the country. Unlike Hakata, which is located on sand dunes, the area surrounding the shrine grounds is located on the alluvial land of the Naka River, and topographically located on the cape of Reizeitsu, which juts out into the mouths of the Hie River and the Naka River. This was thought to be a suitable location for a place of worship for the guardian deity of navigation. Bronze spear and a bronze sword from the [[Yayoi Period]] have been excavated from the shrine grounds, and it is theorized that this area was originally a sacred place for [[Nakoku]] or the Amabe maritime tribe. ==History== The foundation of the Sumitomo Shrine in Hakozaki is unknown. It first appears in historical documentation in an entry in the ''[[Shoku Nihongi]]'' dated April 737, when it is recorded that offerings were made to "Chikushi Sumiyoshi" and to [[Ise Grand Shrine]] in response to disrespectful actions by the kingdom of [[Silla]] in the [[Korean Peninsula]]. Per a survey dated 806, 36 shrines were dedicated to Sumiyoshi in Chikuzen Province, and in 847 the monk [[Ennin]] and in 852 the monk [[Enchin]] recited Buddhist sutras at the shrine on their return from [[Tang China]]. In 878, it was placed under the direct protection of the Imperial Court after an oracle at [[ Kashii-gū]] warned of a possible attack by Silla. In the ''[[Engishiki]]'', the shrine is listed as a ''Myojin Taisha'' and in 1019, the shrine was entrusted to [[Emperor Go-Ichijō]] as a "once-in-a-generation" offering. It has been regarded as the ''ichinomiya'' of Chikuzen Province since the late [[Heian period]]. [[Takezaki Suenaga]]'s ''[[Mōko Shūrai Ekotoba]]'' depicts the vermilion torii gate of Sumiyoshi Shrine. In 1480, the ''[[renga]]'' master [[Sōgi]] visited the shrine, and wrote about the devastation of Sumiyoshi Shrine due to war in the "Tsukushi Doki". During the [[Sengoku period]], the shrine records and old documents were taken by [[Ōuchi Yoshitaka]] to [[Yamaguchi, Yamaguchi|Yamaguchi]] and were destroyed in the [[Tainei-ji incident]] of 1551. The current shrine was restored by [[Kuroda Nagamasa]], the first ''[[daimyō]]'' of [[Fukuoka Domain]] in 1623. Subsequent rulers of the domain continued to support the shrine to the [[Meiji Restoration|Meiji restoration]]. Under the [[Meiji government]]'s [[State Shinto]]'s system of [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|Ranked Shinto shrines]], Sumiyoshi Shrine was Ranked as a Prefectural Shrine in 1872, and promoted to a {{nihongo|Imperial shrine, 3rd Rank|官幣小社|Kanpei-shōsha}} in 1925. In 2004, [[archaeological excavation]]s began around the precincts. In a total of three excavations up to 2014, the remains of a mansion from the medieval to early modern period were discovered along with artifacts related to rituals. ==Cultural Properties== *{{nihongo|'''Honden'''|本殿||}} - The main hall of the shrine was built by Kuroda Nagamasa in 1623 during the early Edo period. It is in the ''Sumiyoshi-zukuri'' style, which is considered to be an older form of shrine architecture. It is a gabled structure and the roof is thatched with cypress bark. The pillars are painted vermilion and the wooden walls are painted white. It was designated as a National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1922.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/3464|title=住吉神社本殿|language=ja |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=December 20, 2023}} ==Gallery== Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka) torii.JPG|Torii Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka), honden.JPG|Honden (ICP) Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka) nougakuden.JPG|Noh Theatre ==See also== *[[Ichinomiya]] ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons Category|Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka)}} *[https://www.nihondaiichisumiyoshigu.jp Official home page]{{in lang|ja}} *[https://bunkazai.city.fukuoka.lg.jp/cultural_properties/detail/93 Cultural Properties of Fukuoka City]{{in lang|ja}} *[https://www.crossroadfukuoka.jp/spot/12552 Fukuoka Tourism Web]{{in lang|ja}} {{Shinto shrine}} ]] {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ {{Ichinomiya}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shinto shrines in Fukuoka Prefecture]] [[Category:Chikuzen Province]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Fukuoka]] [[Category:Ichinomiya]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Kanpei Shōsha]] [[Category:Shrines dedicated to empress Jingū]] [[Category:Sumiyoshi shrines]] [[Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia 6]] [[Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia]] [[sn:Sumiyoshi Shrine (Fukuoka)]]}} [[sn:Sumiyoshi Shrine (Fukuoka)]] [[en:Sumiyoshi Shrine (Fukuoka)]] [[sn:umiyoshi Shrine (Fukuoka)]] [[sn: failed]] [[Category:Pages without translation templates]] [[Category:pages with valid en interwikis]] [[Category:pages that were shrank]] {{Commons category|Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka)}} [[de:Sumiyoshi-Schrein (Fukuoka)]] [[fr:Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka)]] [[ja:住吉神社 (福岡市)]] [[simple:Sumiyoshi Shrine (Fukuoka)]] [[zh:住吉神社 (福岡市)]][[Category:LINKED FROM WIKIDATA DO NOT OVERWRITE]][[Category:LINKED FROM WIKIDATA DO NOT OVERWRITE]][[Category:LINKED FROM WIKIDATA DO NOT OVERWRITE]]

住吉神社 | image = Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka) haiden-1.JPG | caption = Haiden of Sumiyoshi Shrine {{Infobox mapframe|tyep=shape|zoom=14|frame-width=240}} | map_type = Japan Fukuoka Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|33|35|9.26|N|130|24|49.33|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title, inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = Sumiyoshi Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = Sumiyoshi | deity = [[Sumiyoshi sanjin]] | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = 3-1-51 Sumiyoshi, Hakata-ku, Fukuoka-shi, Fukuoka-ken | website = | architecture_style = Sumiyoshi-zukuri | festival = October 13 | leadership = | footnotes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=pink|text align=center|[[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]}} }} {{nihongo|'''Sumiyoshi Shrine'''|住吉神社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] in the Sumiyoshi neighborhood of [[Hakata-ku, Fukuoka]] in [[Fukuoka Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It is the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of former [[Chikuzen Province]]. The main festival of the shrine is held annually on October 13.{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}} Along with the more famous [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]] in [[Osaka]] and the [[Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shimonoseki)|Sumiyoshi Jinja]] in [[Shimonoseki, Yamaguchi]], it is one of the "Three Great Sumiyoshi" shrines.{{cite encyclopedia|last=Yonei|first=Teruyoshi|title=Aramitama|url=http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=1180|encyclopedia=Encyclopedia of Shinto|publisher=Kokugakuin University|access-date=5 February 2011}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''[[kami]]'' enshrined at Sumiyoshi Jinja are: * {{nihongo|'''[[Sumiyoshi sanjin]]'''| 住吉三神|}} * {{nihongo|'''[[Empress Jingū]]'''| 神功皇后|}} * {{nihongo|'''[[Amaterasu]]'''|天照皇大神 |}} ==Origins== Per the shrine's legend (''Chikuzen Sumiyoshi Daimyojin Goengi''), the shrine is the birthplace of the Sumiyoshi cult and the origin for all Sumiyoshi shrines in the country. Unlike Hakata, which is located on sand dunes, the area surrounding the shrine grounds is located on the alluvial land of the Naka River, and topographically located on the cape of Reizeitsu, which juts out into the mouths of the Hie River and the Naka River. This was thought to be a suitable location for a place of worship for the guardian deity of navigation. Bronze spear and a bronze sword from the [[Yayoi Period]] have been excavated from the shrine grounds, and it is theorized that this area was originally a sacred place for [[Nakoku]] or the Amabe maritime tribe. ==History== The foundation of the Sumitomo Shrine in Hakozaki is unknown. It first appears in historical documentation in an entry in the ''[[Shoku Nihongi]]'' dated April 737, when it is recorded that offerings were made to "Chikushi Sumiyoshi" and to [[Ise Grand Shrine]] in response to disrespectful actions by the kingdom of [[Silla]] in the [[Korean Peninsula]]. Per a survey dated 806, 36 shrines were dedicated to Sumiyoshi in Chikuzen Province, and in 847 the monk [[Ennin]] and in 852 the monk [[Enchin]] recited Buddhist sutras at the shrine on their return from [[Tang China]]. In 878, it was placed under the direct protection of the Imperial Court after an oracle at [[ Kashii-gū]] warned of a possible attack by Silla. In the ''[[Engishiki]]'', the shrine is listed as a ''Myojin Taisha'' and in 1019, the shrine was entrusted to [[Emperor Go-Ichijō]] as a "once-in-a-generation" offering. It has been regarded as the ''ichinomiya'' of Chikuzen Province since the late [[Heian period]]. [[Takezaki Suenaga]]'s ''[[Mōko Shūrai Ekotoba]]'' depicts the vermilion torii gate of Sumiyoshi Shrine. In 1480, the ''[[renga]]'' master [[Sōgi]] visited the shrine, and wrote about the devastation of Sumiyoshi Shrine due to war in the "Tsukushi Doki". During the [[Sengoku period]], the shrine records and old documents were taken by [[Ōuchi Yoshitaka]] to [[Yamaguchi, Yamaguchi|Yamaguchi]] and were destroyed in the [[Tainei-ji incident]] of 1551. The current shrine was restored by [[Kuroda Nagamasa]], the first ''[[daimyō]]'' of [[Fukuoka Domain]] in 1623. Subsequent rulers of the domain continued to support the shrine to the [[Meiji Restoration|Meiji restoration]]. Under the [[Meiji government]]'s [[State Shinto]]'s system of [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|Ranked Shinto shrines]], Sumiyoshi Shrine was Ranked as a Prefectural Shrine in 1872, and promoted to a {{nihongo|Imperial shrine, 3rd Rank|官幣小社|Kanpei-shōsha}} in 1925. In 2004, [[archaeological excavation]]s began around the precincts. In a total of three excavations up to 2014, the remains of a mansion from the medieval to early modern period were discovered along with artifacts related to rituals. ==Cultural Properties== *{{nihongo|'''Honden'''|本殿||}} - The main hall of the shrine was built by Kuroda Nagamasa in 1623 during the early Edo period. It is in the ''Sumiyoshi-zukuri'' style, which is considered to be an older form of shrine architecture. It is a gabled structure and the roof is thatched with cypress bark. The pillars are painted vermilion and the wooden walls are painted white. It was designated as a National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1922.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/3464|title=住吉神社本殿|language=ja |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=December 20, 2023}} ==Gallery== Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka) torii.JPG|Torii Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka), honden.JPG|Honden (ICP) Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka) nougakuden.JPG|Noh Theatre ==See also== *[[Ichinomiya]] ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons Category|Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka)}} *[https://www.nihondaiichisumiyoshigu.jp Official home page]{{in lang|ja}} *[https://bunkazai.city.fukuoka.lg.jp/cultural_properties/detail/93 Cultural Properties of Fukuoka City]{{in lang|ja}} *[https://www.crossroadfukuoka.jp/spot/12552 Fukuoka Tourism Web]{{in lang|ja}} {{Shinto shrine}} ]] {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ {{Ichinomiya}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shinto shrines in Fukuoka Prefecture]] [[Category:Chikuzen Province]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Fukuoka]] [[Category:Ichinomiya]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Kanpei Shōsha]] [[Category:Shrines dedicated to empress Jingū]] [[Category:Sumiyoshi shrines]] [[Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia 6]] [[Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia]] [[sn:Sumiyoshi Shrine (Fukuoka)]]}} [[sn:Sumiyoshi Shrine (Fukuoka)]] [[en:Sumiyoshi Shrine (Fukuoka)]] [[sn:umiyoshi Shrine (Fukuoka)]] [[sn: failed]] [[Category:Pages without translation templates]] [[Category:pages with valid en interwikis]] [[Category:pages that were shrank]] {{Commons category|Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka)}} [[de:Sumiyoshi-Schrein (Fukuoka)]] [[fr:Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka)]] [[ja:住吉神社 (福岡市)]] [[simple:Sumiyoshi Shrine (Fukuoka)]] [[zh:住吉神社 (福岡市)]][[Category:LINKED FROM WIKIDATA DO NOT OVERWRITE]][[Category:LINKED FROM WIKIDATA DO NOT OVERWRITE]][[Category:LINKED FROM WIKIDATA DO NOT OVERWRITE]][[Category:LINKED FROM WIKIDATA DO NOT OVERWRITE]]

住吉神社 | image = Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka) haiden-1.JPG | caption = Haiden of Sumiyoshi Shrine {{Infobox mapframe|tyep=shape|zoom=14|frame-width=240}} | map_type = Japan Fukuoka Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|33|35|9.26|N|130|24|49.33|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title, inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = Sumiyoshi Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = Sumiyoshi | deity = [[Sumiyoshi sanjin]] | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = 3-1-51 Sumiyoshi, Hakata-ku, Fukuoka-shi, Fukuoka-ken | website = | architecture_style = Sumiyoshi-zukuri | festival = October 13 | leadership = | footnotes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=pink|text align=center|[[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]}} }} {{nihongo|'''Sumiyoshi Shrine'''|住吉神社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] in the Sumiyoshi neighborhood of [[Hakata-ku, Fukuoka]] in [[Fukuoka Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It is the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of former [[Chikuzen Province]]. The main festival of the shrine is held annually on October 13.{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}} Along with the more famous [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]] in [[Osaka]] and the [[Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shimonoseki)|Sumiyoshi Jinja]] in [[Shimonoseki, Yamaguchi]], it is one of the "Three Great Sumiyoshi" shrines.{{cite encyclopedia|last=Yonei|first=Teruyoshi|title=Aramitama|url=http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=1180|encyclopedia=Encyclopedia of Shinto|publisher=Kokugakuin University|access-date=5 February 2011}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''[[kami]]'' enshrined at Sumiyoshi Jinja are: * {{nihongo|'''[[Sumiyoshi sanjin]]'''| 住吉三神|}} * {{nihongo|'''[[Empress Jingū]]'''| 神功皇后|}} * {{nihongo|'''[[Amaterasu]]'''|天照皇大神 |}} ==Origins== Per the shrine's legend (''Chikuzen Sumiyoshi Daimyojin Goengi''), the shrine is the birthplace of the Sumiyoshi cult and the origin for all Sumiyoshi shrines in the country. Unlike Hakata, which is located on sand dunes, the area surrounding the shrine grounds is located on the alluvial land of the Naka River, and topographically located on the cape of Reizeitsu, which juts out into the mouths of the Hie River and the Naka River. This was thought to be a suitable location for a place of worship for the guardian deity of navigation. Bronze spear and a bronze sword from the [[Yayoi Period]] have been excavated from the shrine grounds, and it is theorized that this area was originally a sacred place for [[Nakoku]] or the Amabe maritime tribe. ==History== The foundation of the Sumitomo Shrine in Hakozaki is unknown. It first appears in historical documentation in an entry in the ''[[Shoku Nihongi]]'' dated April 737, when it is recorded that offerings were made to "Chikushi Sumiyoshi" and to [[Ise Grand Shrine]] in response to disrespectful actions by the kingdom of [[Silla]] in the [[Korean Peninsula]]. Per a survey dated 806, 36 shrines were dedicated to Sumiyoshi in Chikuzen Province, and in 847 the monk [[Ennin]] and in 852 the monk [[Enchin]] recited Buddhist sutras at the shrine on their return from [[Tang China]]. In 878, it was placed under the direct protection of the Imperial Court after an oracle at [[ Kashii-gū]] warned of a possible attack by Silla. In the ''[[Engishiki]]'', the shrine is listed as a ''Myojin Taisha'' and in 1019, the shrine was entrusted to [[Emperor Go-Ichijō]] as a "once-in-a-generation" offering. It has been regarded as the ''ichinomiya'' of Chikuzen Province since the late [[Heian period]]. [[Takezaki Suenaga]]'s ''[[Mōko Shūrai Ekotoba]]'' depicts the vermilion torii gate of Sumiyoshi Shrine. In 1480, the ''[[renga]]'' master [[Sōgi]] visited the shrine, and wrote about the devastation of Sumiyoshi Shrine due to war in the "Tsukushi Doki". During the [[Sengoku period]], the shrine records and old documents were taken by [[Ōuchi Yoshitaka]] to [[Yamaguchi, Yamaguchi|Yamaguchi]] and were destroyed in the [[Tainei-ji incident]] of 1551. The current shrine was restored by [[Kuroda Nagamasa]], the first ''[[daimyō]]'' of [[Fukuoka Domain]] in 1623. Subsequent rulers of the domain continued to support the shrine to the [[Meiji Restoration|Meiji restoration]]. Under the [[Meiji government]]'s [[State Shinto]]'s system of [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|Ranked Shinto shrines]], Sumiyoshi Shrine was Ranked as a Prefectural Shrine in 1872, and promoted to a {{nihongo|Imperial shrine, 3rd Rank|官幣小社|Kanpei-shōsha}} in 1925. In 2004, [[archaeological excavation]]s began around the precincts. In a total of three excavations up to 2014, the remains of a mansion from the medieval to early modern period were discovered along with artifacts related to rituals. ==Cultural Properties== *{{nihongo|'''Honden'''|本殿||}} - The main hall of the shrine was built by Kuroda Nagamasa in 1623 during the early Edo period. It is in the ''Sumiyoshi-zukuri'' style, which is considered to be an older form of shrine architecture. It is a gabled structure and the roof is thatched with cypress bark. The pillars are painted vermilion and the wooden walls are painted white. It was designated as a National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1922.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/3464|title=住吉神社本殿|language=ja |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=December 20, 2023}} ==Gallery== Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka) 住吉神社 | image = Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka) haiden-1.JPG | caption = Haiden of Sumiyoshi Shrine {{Infobox mapframe|tyep=shape|zoom=14|frame-width=240}} | map_type = Japan Fukuoka Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|33|35|9.26|N|130|24|49.33|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title, inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = Sumiyoshi Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = Sumiyoshi | deity = [[Sumiyoshi sanjin]] | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = 3-1-51 Sumiyoshi, Hakata-ku, Fukuoka-shi, Fukuoka-ken | website = | architecture_style = Sumiyoshi-zukuri | festival = October 13 | leadership = | footnotes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=pink|text align=center|[[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]}} }} {{nihongo|'''Sumiyoshi Shrine'''|住吉神社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] in the Sumiyoshi neighborhood of [[Hakata-ku, Fukuoka]] in [[Fukuoka Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It is the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of former [[Chikuzen Province]]. The main festival of the shrine is held annually on October 13.{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}} Along with the more famous [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]] in [[Osaka]] and the [[Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shimonoseki)|Sumiyoshi Jinja]] in [[Shimonoseki, Yamaguchi]], it is one of the "Three Great Sumiyoshi" shrines.{{cite encyclopedia|last=Yonei|first=Teruyoshi|title=Aramitama|url=http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=1180|encyclopedia=Encyclopedia of Shinto|publisher=Kokugakuin University|access-date=5 February 2011}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''[[kami]]'' enshrined at Sumiyoshi Jinja are: * {{nihongo|'''[[Sumiyoshi sanjin]]'''| 住吉三神|}} * {{nihongo|'''[[Empress Jingū]]'''| 神功皇后|}} * {{nihongo|'''[[Amaterasu]]'''|天照皇大神 |}} ==Origins== Per the shrine's legend (''Chikuzen Sumiyoshi Daimyojin Goengi''), the shrine is the birthplace of the Sumiyoshi cult and the origin for all Sumiyoshi shrines in the country. Unlike Hakata, which is located on sand dunes, the area surrounding the shrine grounds is located on the alluvial land of the Naka River, and topographically located on the cape of Reizeitsu, which juts out into the mouths of the Hie River and the Naka River. This was thought to be a suitable location for a place of worship for the guardian deity of navigation. Bronze spear and a bronze sword from the [[Yayoi Period]] have been excavated from the shrine grounds, and it is theorized that this area was originally a sacred place for [[Nakoku]] or the Amabe maritime tribe. ==History== The foundation of the Sumitomo Shrine in Hakozaki is unknown. It first appears in historical documentation in an entry in the ''[[Shoku Nihongi]]'' dated April 737, when it is recorded that offerings were made to "Chikushi Sumiyoshi" and to [[Ise Grand Shrine]] in response to disrespectful actions by the kingdom of [[Silla]] in the [[Korean Peninsula]]. Per a survey dated 806, 36 shrines were dedicated to Sumiyoshi in Chikuzen Province, and in 847 the monk [[Ennin]] and in 852 the monk [[Enchin]] recited Buddhist sutras at the shrine on their return from [[Tang China]]. In 878, it was placed under the direct protection of the Imperial Court after an oracle at [[ Kashii-gū]] warned of a possible attack by Silla. In the ''[[Engishiki]]'', the shrine is listed as a ''Myojin Taisha'' and in 1019, the shrine was entrusted to [[Emperor Go-Ichijō]] as a "once-in-a-generation" offering. It has been regarded as the ''ichinomiya'' of Chikuzen Province since the late [[Heian period]]. [[Takezaki Suenaga]]'s ''[[Mōko Shūrai Ekotoba]]'' depicts the vermilion torii gate of Sumiyoshi Shrine. In 1480, the ''[[renga]]'' master [[Sōgi]] visited the shrine, and wrote about the devastation of Sumiyoshi Shrine due to war in the "Tsukushi Doki". During the [[Sengoku period]], the shrine records and old documents were taken by [[Ōuchi Yoshitaka]] to [[Yamaguchi, Yamaguchi|Yamaguchi]] and were destroyed in the [[Tainei-ji incident]] of 1551. The current shrine was restored by [[Kuroda Nagamasa]], the first ''[[daimyō]]'' of [[Fukuoka Domain]] in 1623. Subsequent rulers of the domain continued to support the shrine to the [[Meiji Restoration|Meiji restoration]]. Under the [[Meiji government]]'s [[State Shinto]]'s system of [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|Ranked Shinto shrines]], Sumiyoshi Shrine was Ranked as a Prefectural Shrine in 1872, and promoted to a {{nihongo|Imperial shrine, 3rd Rank|官幣小社|Kanpei-shōsha}} in 1925. In 2004, [[archaeological excavation]]s began around the precincts. In a total of three excavations up to 2014, the remains of a mansion from the medieval to early modern period were discovered along with artifacts related to rituals. ==Cultural Properties== *{{nihongo|'''Honden'''|本殿||}} - The main hall of the shrine was built by Kuroda Nagamasa in 1623 during the early Edo period. It is in the ''Sumiyoshi-zukuri'' style, which is considered to be an older form of shrine architecture. It is a gabled structure and the roof is thatched with cypress bark. The pillars are painted vermilion and the wooden walls are painted white. It was designated as a National [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] in 1922.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/3464|title=住吉神社本殿|language=ja |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=December 20, 2023}} ==Gallery== Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka) It is the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of former [[Chikuzen Province]]. The main festival of the shrine is held annually on October 13.{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}} Along with the more famous [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]] in [[Osaka]] and the [[Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shimonoseki)|Sumiyoshi Jinja]] in [[Shimonoseki, Yamaguchi]], it is one of the "Three Great Sumiyoshi" shrines.{{cite encyclopedia|last=Yonei|first=Teruyoshi|title=Aramitama|url=http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=1180|encyclopedia=Encyclopedia of Shinto|publisher=Kokugakuin University|access-date=5 February 2011}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''[[kami]]'' enshrined at Sumiyoshi Jinja are: * {{nihongo|'''[[Sumiyoshi sanjin]]'''| 住吉三神|}} * {{nihongo|'''[[Empress Jingū]]'''| 神功皇后|}} * {{nihongo|'''[[Amaterasu]]'''|天照皇大神 |}} ==Origins== Per the shrine's legend (''Chikuzen Sumiyoshi Daimyojin Goengi''), the shrine is the birthplace of the Sumiyoshi cult and the origin for all Sumiyoshi shrines in the country. Unlike Hakata, which is located on sand dunes, the area surrounding the shrine grounds is located on the alluvial land of the Naka River, and topographically located on the cape of Reizeitsu, which juts out into the mouths of the Hie River and the Naka River. This was thought to be a suitable location for a place of worship for the guardian deity of navigation. Bronze spear and a bronze sword from the [[Yayoi Period]] have been excavated from the shrine grounds, and it is theorized that this area was originally a sacred place for [[Nakoku]] or the Amabe maritime tribe. ==History== The foundation of the Sumitomo Shrine in Hakozaki is unknown. It first appears in historical documentation in an entry in the ''[[Shoku Nihongi]]'' dated April 737, when it is recorded that offerings were made to "Chikushi Sumiyoshi" and to [[Ise Grand Shrine]] in response to disrespectful actions by the kingdom of [[Silla]] in the [[Korean Peninsula]]. Per a survey dated 806, 36 shrines were dedicated to Sumiyoshi in Chikuzen Province, and in 847 the monk [[Ennin]] and in 852 the monk [[Enchin]] recited Buddhist sutras at the shrine on their return from [[Tang China]]. In 878, it was placed under the direct protection of the Imperial Court after an oracle at [[ Kashii-gū]] warned of a possible attack by Silla. In the ''[[Engishiki]]'', the shrine is listed as a ''Myojin Taisha'' and in 1019, the shrine was entrusted to [[Emperor Go-Ichijō]] as a "once-in-a-generation" offering. It has been regarded as the ''ichinomiya'' of Chikuzen Province since the late [[Heian period]]. [[Takezaki Suenaga]]'s ''[[Mōko Shūrai Ekotoba]]'' depicts the vermilion torii gate of Sumiyoshi Shrine. In 1480, the ''[[renga]]'' master [[Sōgi]] visited the shrine, and wrote about the devastation of Sumiyoshi Shrine due to war in the "Tsukushi Doki". During the [[Sengoku period]], the shrine records and old documents were taken by [[Ōuchi Yoshitaka]] to [[Yamaguchi, Yamaguchi|Yamaguchi]] and were destroyed in the [[Tainei-ji incident]] of 1551. The current shrine was restored by [[Kuroda Nagamasa]], the first ''[[daimyō]]'' of [[Fukuoka Domain]] in 1623. Subsequent rulers of the domain continued to support the shrine to the [[Meiji Restoration|Meiji restoration]]. Under the [[Meiji government]]'s [[State Shinto]]'s system of [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|Ranked Shinto shrines]], Sumiyoshi Shrine was Ranked as a Prefectural Shrine in 1872, and promoted to a {{nihongo|Imperial shrine, 3rd Rank|官幣小社|Kanpei-shōsha}} in 1925. In 2004, [[archaeological excavation]]s began around the precincts. 住吉神社 | image = Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka) haiden-1.JPG | caption = Haiden of Sumiyoshi Shrine {{Infobox mapframe|tyep=shape|zoom=14|frame-width=240}} | map_type = Japan Fukuoka Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|33|35|9.26|N|130|24|49.33|E|type:landmark_region:JP|display=title, inline}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = Sumiyoshi Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = Sumiyoshi | deity = [[Sumiyoshi sanjin]] | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = 3-1-51 Sumiyoshi, Hakata-ku, Fukuoka-shi, Fukuoka-ken | website = | architecture_style = Sumiyoshi-zukuri | festival = October 13 | leadership = | footnotes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=pink|text align=center|[[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]}} }} {{nihongo|'''Sumiyoshi Shrine'''|住吉神社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] in the Sumiyoshi neighborhood of [[Hakata-ku, Fukuoka]] in [[Fukuoka Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It is the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of former [[Chikuzen Province]]. The main festival of the shrine is held annually on October 13.{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}} Along with the more famous [[Sumiyoshi-taisha]] in [[Osaka]] and the [[Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shimonoseki)|Sumiyoshi Jinja]] in [[Shimonoseki, Yamaguchi]], it is one of the "Three Great Sumiyoshi" shrines.{{cite encyclopedia|last=Yonei|first=Teruyoshi|title=Aramitama|url=http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=1180|encyclopedia=Encyclopedia of Shinto|publisher=Kokugakuin University|access-date=5 February 2011}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''[[kami]]'' enshrined at Sumiyoshi Jinja are: * {{nihongo|'''[[Sumiyoshi sanjin]]'''| 住吉三神|}} * {{nihongo|'''[[Empress Jingū]]'''| 神功皇后|}} * {{nihongo|'''[[Amaterasu]]'''|天照皇大神 |}} ==Origins== Per the shrine's legend (''Chikuzen Sumiyoshi Daimyojin Goengi''), the shrine is the birthplace of the Sumiyoshi cult and the origin for all Sumiyoshi shrines in the country. Unlike Hakata, which is located on sand dunes, the area surrounding the shrine grounds is located on the alluvial land of the Naka River, and topographically located on the cape of Reizeitsu, which juts out into the mouths of the Hie River and the Naka River. This was thought to be a suitable location for a place of worship for the guardian deity of navigation. Bronze spear and a bronze sword from the [[Yayoi Period]] have been excavated from the shrine grounds, and it is theorized that this area was originally a sacred place for [[Nakoku]] or the Amabe maritime tribe. ==History== The foundation of the Sumitomo Shrine in Hakozaki is unknown. It first appears in historical documentation in an entry in the ''[[Shoku Nihongi]]'' dated April 737, when it is recorded that offerings were made to "Chikushi Sumiyoshi" and to [[Ise Grand Shrine]] in response to disrespectful actions by the kingdom of [[Silla]] in the [[Korean Peninsula]]. Per a survey dated 806, 36 shrines were dedicated to Sumiyoshi in Chikuzen Province, and in 847 the monk [[Ennin]] and in 852 the monk [[Enchin]] recited Buddhist sutras at the shrine on their return from [[Tang China]]. In 878, it was placed under the direct protection of the Imperial Court after an oracle at [[ Kashii-gū]] warned of a possible attack by Silla. In the ''[[Engishiki]]'', the shrine is listed as a ''Myojin Taisha'' and in 1019, the shrine was entrusted to [[Emperor Go-Ichijō]] as a "once-in-a-generation" offering. It has been regarded as the ''ichinomiya'' of Chikuzen Province since the late [[Heian period]]. [[Takezaki Suenaga]]'s ''[[Mōko Shūrai Ekotoba]]'' depicts the vermilion torii gate of Sumiyoshi Shrine. In 1480, the ''[[renga]]'' master [[Sōgi]] visited the shrine, and wrote about the devastation of Sumiyoshi Shrine due to war in the "Tsukushi Doki". During the [[Sengoku period]], the shrine records and old documents were taken by [[Ōuchi Yoshitaka]] to [[Yamaguchi, Yamaguchi|Yamaguchi]] and were destroyed in the [[Tainei-ji incident]] of 1551. The current shrine was restored by [[Kuroda Nagamasa]], the first ''[[daimyō]]'' of [[Fukuoka Domain]] in 1623. Subsequent rulers of the domain continued to support the shrine to the [[Meiji Restoration|Meiji restoration]]. Under the [[Meiji government]]'s [[State Shinto]]'s system of [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|Ranked Shinto shrines]], Sumiyoshi Shrine was Ranked as a Prefectural Shrine in 1872, and promoted to a {{nihongo|Imperial shrine, 3rd Rank|官幣小社|Kanpei-shōsha}} in 1925. In 2004, [[archaeological excavation]]s began around the precincts. In a total of three excavations up to 2014, the remains of a mansion from the medieval to early modern period were discovered along with artifacts related to rituals. ==Cultural Properties== *{{nihongo|'''Honden'''|本殿||}} - The main hall of the shrine was built by Kuroda Nagamasa in 1623 during the early Edo period. It is in the ''Sumiyoshi-zukuri'' style, which is considered to be an older form of shrine architecture. It is a gabled structure and the roof is thatched with cypress bark. The pillars are painted vermilion and the wooden walls are painted white.
