また、全国的に住吉神を祀る神社に関して見た場合、『{{jalink|住吉大社神代記|Q11381815}}』や『{{jalink|延喜式|Q1342448}}』{{jalink|延喜式神名帳|Q11064932|神名帳}}（{{jalink|927年|Q30470}}成立）において{{jalink|摂津国|Q864163}}・{{jalink|播磨国|Q1047523}}・{{jalink|長門国|Q907382}}・{{jalink|筑前国|Q1047664}}・{{jalink|壱岐国|Q1052938}}・{{jalink|対馬国|Q1054861}}にそれぞれ住吉神社の記載があることから、当社含めこれらの社には朝鮮航路の要所に配置する意図があったとする説もある{{Sfn|岡田精司|2011|pp=86-109}}。この中で、住吉神は神功皇后の征討伝承と不可分であることから国家的な航海守護神に位置づけられていたとし、{{jalink|5世紀|Q8095}}の{{jalink|倭の五王|Q1152880}}の頃から{{jalink|ヤマト王権|Q2658252}}の軍事・外交に深く関わっていたとする説もある{{Sfn|岡田精司|2011|pp=86-109}}。 === 概史 === ==== 古代 ==== 『続日本紀』{{jalink|天平|Q1199879}}9年（{{jalink|737年|Q23583}}）4月乙巳朔条にて、{{jalink|伊勢神宮|Q687168}}などとともに「筑紫住吉」に{{jalink|新羅|Q28456}}の無礼の報告と奉幣がなされた{{Sfn|住吉神社（角川）|1988}}。『{{jalink|新抄格勅符抄|Q11502312}}』『新抄格勅符抄』巻10（神事諸家封戸）大同元年（806年）牒（{{Harvnb|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。によれば、{{jalink|大同 (日本)|Q1373191|大同}}元年（{{jalink|806年|Q30021}}）には「{{jalink|住吉神}}」に{{jalink|神封|Q1689534}}36戸が{{jalink|筑前国|Q1047664}}から充てられている{{Sfn|住吉神社（角川）|1988}}。また{{jalink|承和 (日本)|Q1075605|承和}}14年（{{jalink|847年|Q30354}}）には僧{{jalink|円仁|Q732282}}が、{{jalink|仁寿|Q1373077}}2年（{{jalink|852年|Q30383}}）には僧{{jalink|円珍|Q1972505}}が入唐にあたって経典の読誦を行なっている{{Sfn|住吉神社（神々）|1984}}。 {{jalink|六国史|Q1151168|国史}}では、{{jalink|天安 (日本)|Q1075611|天安}}3年（{{jalink|859年|Q23897}}）に筑前国の「住吉神」の{{jalink|神階|Q11591025}}が無位から従五位下に昇叙されたと見えるほか、{{jalink|元慶|Q747451}}2年（{{jalink|878年|Q23910}}）『日本三代実録』元慶2年（878年）12月24日条（{{Harvnb|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。には「新羅凶賊」を告げる{{jalink|香椎宮|Q631373}}の託宣を受けて朝廷の奉幣に預かっている{{Sfn|住吉神社（角川）|1988}}。 {{jalink|延長 (元号)|Q1327274|延長}}5年（{{jalink|927年|Q30470}}）成立の『{{jalink|延喜式|Q1342448}}』{{jalink|延喜式神名帳|Q11064932|神名帳}}では、筑前国{{jalink|那珂郡 (福岡県)|Q11642798|那珂郡}}に「住吉神社三座 並名神大」と記載され、3座が{{jalink|名神大社|Q9610964}}に列している{{Sfn|住吉神社（角川）|1988}}。また『住吉大社神代記』では、「筑前国那珂郡住吉社三前」や「筑前国那珂郡住吉荒魂社三前」の表記で記載されている{{Sfn|岡田精司|2011|pp=86-109}}{{Sfn|住吉神社（神々）|1984}}。{{jalink|寛仁|Q1193951}}元年（{{jalink|1019年|Q19252}}）『左経記』寛仁元年（1019年）10月2日条。には{{jalink|後一条天皇|Q374087}}の1代1度の奉幣に預かったほか、{{jalink|元永|Q1193613}}2年（{{jalink|1119年|Q19540}}）『中右記』元永2年（1119年）4月26日条。にも住吉社遷宮の日時勘申がなされており、国家神的性格は{{jalink|平安時代|Q193292}}末期にも継続する{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000|pp=576-577}}。 ==== 中世・近世 ==== {{jalink|中世|Q12554}}以降は{{jalink|建武 (日本)|Q1193970|建武}}元年（{{jalink|1334年|Q6007}}）の文書を初見として筑前国の{{jalink|一宮|Q1656379}}の位置づけにあったとされる{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000|pp=576-577}}。文献では筑前国の一宮として{{jalink|筥崎宮|Q714742}}（福岡市{{jalink|東区 (福岡市)|Q1206659|東区}}{{jalink|箱崎 (福岡市)|Q11603321|箱崎}}）も見られるが、中世以前の史料で一宮の記述が確認されているのは筑前国で住吉神社のみになる{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000|pp=576-577}}。この頃の{{jalink|竹崎季長|Q1064936}}の『{{jalink|蒙古襲来絵詞|Q3087790}}』では、住吉神社の朱塗りの鳥居が描かれている{{Sfn|住吉神社（式内社）|1978}}。また{{jalink|文明 (日本)|Q1193544|文明}}12年（{{jalink|1480年|Q6628}}）には連歌師の{{jalink|宗祇|Q923562}}が参詣しており、『筑紫道記』に戦乱による住吉神社荒廃の様子を記している{{sfn|住吉神社（平凡社）|2004}}。{{jalink|戦国時代 (日本)|Q204023|戦国時代}}には、当社に伝わる古文書を山口の{{jalink|大内義隆|Q1065163}}のもとに上進していたところ、{{jalink|天文 (元号)|Q1192853|天文}}20年（{{jalink|1551年|Q6560}}）の{{jalink|大寧寺の変|Q10856357}}に巻き込まれその一切を散逸したという{{sfn|住吉神社（平凡社）|2004}}。 [[File:Kuroda Nagamasa.jpg|thumb|160px|right|{{center|{{jalink|黒田長政|Q950496}}}}{{small|{{jalink|福岡藩|Q208766}}初代藩主。現在の本殿を再建。}}]] {{jalink|江戸時代|Q184963}}、{{jalink|福岡藩|Q208766|福岡藩主}}となった{{jalink|黒田長政|Q950496}}が{{jalink|元和 (日本)|Q635245|元和}}9年（{{jalink|1623年|Q6818}}）に白銀2,000枚を下行して社殿を再興し、そのときの本殿が現在まで使用されている{{sfn|住吉神社（平凡社）|2004}}。{{jalink|天和 (日本)|Q1145289|天和}}3年（{{jalink|1683年|Q7651}}）には3代藩主{{jalink|黒田光之|Q11678571}}が社領として30石を寄せ、{{jalink|文化 (元号)|Q1373146|文化}}13年（{{jalink|1816年|Q6953}}）には10代藩主{{jalink|黒田斉清|Q11678605}}が20石を加増したことにより計50石を有した{{sfn|住吉神社（平凡社）|2004}}。この頃の{{jalink|別当寺|Q11396755}}は松花山円福寺であった{{Sfn|住吉神社（角川）|1988}}。 ==== 近代以降 ==== {{jalink|明治維新|Q8707}}後、{{jalink|明治|Q3125096}}5年（{{jalink|1872年|Q7753}}）に{{jalink|近代社格制度|Q712534}}において{{jalink|県社}}に列し、{{jalink|大正|Q329174}}14年（{{jalink|1925年|Q18107}}）に{{jalink|近代社格制度#官社|Q712534|官幣小社}}に昇格した{{Sfn|住吉神社（角川）|1988}}。戦後は{{jalink|神社本庁|Q908077}}の{{jalink|別表神社|Q10898274}}に列している。 {{jalink|平成|Q234510}}16年（{{jalink|2004年|Q2014}}）からは境内域周辺（住吉神社遺跡）で発掘調査が開始されている{{Sfn|住吉神社遺跡第1次調査報告|2006|p=6}}。平成26年（{{jalink|2014年|Q1999}}）までの計3次の調査では、中世-近世期の屋敷地の遺構が祭祀に関わる遺物を伴い検出されるとともに[http://bunkazai.city.fukuoka.lg.jp/excavation_news/detail/18/from_sp:1 博多区住吉で中世の屋敷跡を発見! -住吉神社遺跡第3次発掘調査について-]（福岡市ホームページ）。、屋敷地の方位が現在の本殿と一致し、この方位が中世前半まで遡ることも認められた{{Sfn|住吉神社遺跡第1次調査報告|2006|p=6}}。 === 神階 === * {{jalink|天安 (日本)|Q1075611|天安}}3年（{{jalink|859年|Q23897}}）1月27日、無位から従五位下 （『{{jalink|日本三代実録|Q1052981}}』）『日本三代実録』貞観元年（859年）正月27日条（{{Harvnb|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 - 表記は「住吉神」。 === 神職・社領 === 神職は、『{{jalink|類聚符宣抄|Q11665188}}』の{{jalink|天元 (日本)|Q1327101|天元}}2年（{{jalink|979年|Q23784}}）太政官符によると大宮司があったといい、『{{jalink|吾妻鏡|Q1042324}}』には{{jalink|源頼朝|Q242800}}にも仕えた神官として佐伯氏の名が見え{{sfn|住吉神社（平凡社）|2004}}、その後は佐伯氏末裔の横田氏が代々担ったという{{Sfn|住吉神社（神々）|1984}}。社領は文献に「住吉庄」と見え、その所属は後白河院領、宣陽門院領、伏見院領、天皇家領と変遷しながら継続した{{Sfn|住吉神社（角川）|1988}}。 {{jalink|天保|Q1369045}}時代の大宮司・横田織江は、{{jalink|福岡藩|Q208766}}に禁じられた神道式祭祀の復活を願い、{{jalink|筥崎宮|Q714742}}や{{jalink|宇美八幡宮|Q924940}}の大宮司らと{{jalink|京都|Q740246}}の{{jalink|一条家|Q1535498}}に訴え出たところ、藩から帰郷命令が出て逮捕され、天保4年（1833年）、隠居と{{jalink|座敷牢|Q11486150}}での謹慎を命じられた『大三輪長兵衛の生涯』葦津泰国（葦津事務所、2008年）p42。 === 境内 === [[File:Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka), honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|本殿（重要文化財）}}{{small|社殿形式は「住吉造」である。}}]] 境内の広さは8,107坪（2.68ヘクタール）。博多が砂丘上に立地するのとは異なり、境内周辺は那珂川の沖積地に立地する。 境内社殿のうち{{jalink|神社建築#本殿|Q3080012|'''本殿'''}}は、{{jalink|江戸時代|Q184963}}前期の{{jalink|元和 (日本)|Q635245|元和}}9年（{{jalink|1623年|Q6818}}）の{{jalink|福岡藩|Q208766|福岡藩主}}{{jalink|黒田長政|Q950496}}による造営。{{jalink|神明造|Q930545}}・{{jalink|大社造|Q387874}}と並んで、古い社殿形式とされる「'''{{jalink|住吉造|Q3503635}}'''」{{Sfn|稲垣|2000|p=174}}{{Sfn|米澤|2016|pp=112-113}}を採用する。桁行（奥行）4間・梁間（間口）2間の{{jalink|切妻造|Q13308575}}で、屋根は{{jalink|檜皮葺|Q90373477}}。屋根やそれに付す{{jalink|破風|Q4881511}}・{{jalink|千木・鰹木|Q87220234|千木・堅魚木}}3本が直線的である点は、古式建築を反映する。柱は朱色、板壁は白色で彩る。{{Sfn|岡田精司|2011|pp=86-109}}。国の{{jalink|重要文化財|Q1188622}}に指定されている[http://www.fsg.pref.fukuoka.jp/bunka/contents_detail.asp?table=t6&fields=f767&id=1307-4&bunrui=kuni_yuke_kenz_juyo 住吉神社本殿]（ふくおか社会教育ネットワーク「福岡県の文化財」）。[http://bunkazai.city.fukuoka.lg.jp/cultural_properties/detail/140 住吉神社本殿]（福岡市文化財保護課「福岡市の文化財」）。。 本殿前に建てられている{{jalink|神社建築#拝殿|Q3080012|'''拝殿'''}}は、{{jalink|入母屋造|Q855025}}で、屋根は銅板葺。また境内南側にある{{jalink|住吉神社能楽殿|Q132168040|能楽殿}}（のうがくでん）は、{{jalink|警固神社|Q11632314}}（福岡市中央区天神）能楽堂の老朽化に伴い{{jalink|昭和|Q327567}}10年（{{jalink|1935年|Q18658}}）から住吉神社内での造営が計画され、昭和13年（{{jalink|1938年|Q18645}}）に完成したものになる。{{jalink|入母屋造|Q855025}}の妻入りで、屋根は波子鉄板葺。この能楽殿は日本の伝統様式と洋風の様式を一体とした近代和風建築であり、福岡市指定文化財に指定されている[http://bunkazai.city.fukuoka.lg.jp/cultural_properties/detail/158 住吉神社能楽殿]（福岡市文化財保護課「福岡市の文化財」）。境内説明板。。 そのほか、境内には神楽殿・神門などの社殿がある。 ファイル:住吉大社 本殿平面図.tif|住吉造の平面図 File:Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka) nougakuden.JPG|能楽殿（福岡市指定文化財）の入る建物 File:Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka) shinmon.JPG|神門 === 主な祭事 === ; 追儺祭 : 「ついなさい」。1月7日。皇室・国家の繁栄祈願として、鬼すべ・鷽替え（うそ替え）神事を行う[http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/winter.html 冬の祭典・行事]（公式サイト）。 ; 御田祭 : 「おんださい」。3月7日。五穀豊穣祈願として、播種神事を行う[http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/spring.html 春の祭典・行事]（公式サイト）。 ; 潮干祭 : 「しおひさい」。4月3日。航海安全・豊漁祈願として神幸（神輿渡御）を行う。かつて門前に海が広がった頃には船での神幸であったというが、現在は陸上での神幸として行う。 ; 名越大祭 : 「なごしたいさい」。7月30日から8月1日。伊弉諾尊の禊で住吉神が生まれたことに関係する神事で、穢れ祓いとして茅の輪くぐりや人形流しの神事を行う[http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/summer.html 夏の祭典・行事]（公式サイト）。 ; 例大祭 : 「'''相撲会大祭'''（すもうえたいさい）」または単に「相撲会祭」とも。10月12日から14日。住吉神社で最も重要な祭。神功皇后が朝鮮から帰国したとき、住吉神に対して神恩感謝として相撲・{{jalink|流鏑馬|Q1886157}}を奉納したことに由来するという。祭事では、稚児行列のほか・流鏑馬・少年相撲が奉納される[http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/autumn.html 秋の祭典・行事]（公式サイト）。 ; 歩射祭 : 「ほしゃさい」。11月7日。元慶2年（878年）の{{jalink|陽成天皇|Q349280}}の奉幣の際、住吉神の霊験により外賊の災いがなくなったことの謝礼として、{{jalink|大宰府|Q144845}}役人が南西（裏鬼門）方向に歩射を行なったことが由来とされる神事。国家鎮護祈願として社前で歩射を行う。 === 文化財 === === {{jalink|別表神社|Q10898274}} |創建 = 不詳（伝承上は上古） |本殿 = {{jalink|住吉造|Q3503635}} |別名 = |札所等 = 三大住吉 |例祭 = {{jalink|10月13日|Q2925}}（相撲会祭） |神事 = |地図 = {{Location map|Fukuoka city|label=住吉神社|position=bottom|width=200|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=15|float=center|caption=}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|marker=religious-shinto|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|frame-height=200}} }} {{座標一覧}} [[File:Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|鳥居}}]] '''住吉神社'''（すみよしじんじゃ）は、{{jalink|福岡県|Q123258}}{{jalink|福岡市|Q26600}}{{jalink|博多区|Q1330839}}{{jalink|住吉 (福岡市)|Q28689038|住吉}}にある{{jalink|神社|Q845945}}。{{jalink|式内社}}（{{jalink|名神大社|Q9610964}}）、{{jalink|筑前国|Q1047664}}{{jalink|一宮|Q1656379}}。{{jalink|近代社格制度|Q712534|旧社格}}は{{jalink|近代社格制度#官社|Q712534|官幣小社}}で、現在は{{jalink|神社本庁|Q908077}}の{{jalink|別表神社|Q10898274}}。 全国にある{{jalink|住吉神社|Q11381857}}の始祖とする説があるほか、大阪の{{jalink|住吉大社|Q705949}}・下関の{{jalink|住吉神社 (下関市)|Q11381858|住吉神社}}とともに「三大住吉」の1つに数えられる{{Cite book |和書 |editor=森睦彦 |title=名数数詞辞典 |publisher=東京堂出版 |year=1987 |page=135}}。 航海守護神の{{jalink|住吉三神|Q1114013}}を祀る神社である。全国には{{jalink|住吉神社|Q11381857}}が2,300社以上あり、{{jalink|大阪府|Q122723}}{{jalink|大阪市|Q35765}}{{jalink|住吉区|Q985702}}の{{jalink|住吉大社|Q705949}}が総本社とされることが多い{{Refnest|group=注釈|{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.sumiyoshitaisha.net/about/origin.html|title=住吉大社の由緒|accessdate=2021-04-25}}}}が、住吉大社に伝わる古典籍『{{jalink|住吉大社神代記|Q11381815}}』では、筑紫大神が{{jalink|神功皇后|Q232803}}に我が{{jalink|荒魂・和魂|Q495568|荒魂}}を{{jalink|下関市|Q203308|穴門山田邑}}に祀るよう宣託を下したので、{{jalink|穴門直}}の祖である{{jalink|踐立}}が{{jalink|住吉神社 (下関市)|Q11381858|住吉神社}}（{{jalink|山口県|Q127264}}{{jalink|下関市|Q203308}}）に荒魂を、和魂を{{jalink|津守氏|Q11555993|津守}}の祖である手搓（{{jalink|田裳見宿禰|Q20041346}}）が大津渟中倉之長峡の祠（住吉大社）に祀ったとあり、当社を示す筑紫大神が住吉の始源である{{Sfn|縁起|1982}}。{{jalink|ヤマト王権|Q2658252}}の国家的航海神として崇敬され、{{jalink|中世|Q12554}}からは{{jalink|筑前国|Q1047664}}の{{jalink|一宮|Q1656379}}に位置づけられたほか、領主・一般民衆からも海にまつわる神として信仰された。 === 祭神 === 祭神は次の5柱神社由緒書。。これら5柱をして「住吉五所大神」とも総称される。 ; 主祭神 :* '''{{jalink|住吉三神|Q1114013|底筒男命}}'''（そこつつのおのみこと） :* '''{{jalink|住吉三神|Q1114013|中筒男命}}'''（なかつつのおのみこと） :* '''{{jalink|住吉三神|Q1114013|表筒男命}}'''（うわつつのおのみこと） : 以上の3柱は「{{jalink|住吉三神|Q1114013}}」と総称される。 ; 配祀神 :* {{jalink|天照大神|Q455602|天照皇大神}} （あまてらすすめおおかみ） :* {{jalink|神功皇后|Q232803}} （じんぐうこうごう） === 祭神について === {{Double image stack|right|Sumiyoshi-taisha, keidai-2.jpg|Sumiyoshi-jinja (Shimonoseki) Honden.JPG|200|{{Center|上：{{jalink|住吉大社|Q705949}}（{{jalink|大阪府|Q122723}}{{jalink|大阪市|Q35765}}）
下：{{jalink|住吉神社 (下関市)|Q11381858|住吉神社}}（{{jalink|山口県|Q127264}}{{jalink|下関市|Q203308}}）}}}} 主祭神の住吉三神は、『{{jalink|古事記|Q813031}}』『{{jalink|日本書紀|Q813935}}』において2つの場面で登場する。1つはその生誕の場面で、黄泉国から帰った{{jalink|イザナギ|Q813858}}（伊奘諾尊/伊邪那岐命）が穢れ祓いのため筑紫日向の橘の小門（おど）の阿波岐原（あはきはら、檍原）で{{jalink|禊|Q1936265}}をすると、{{jalink|ワタツミ|Q1474187|綿津見三神}}（海三神）とともにこれら住吉三神が誕生したという{{Sfn|古事記|1963|pp=28-30}}{{Sfn|書紀|1967|pp=94-95}}。次いで{{jalink|神功皇后|Q232803}}の朝鮮出兵の場面で、住吉神は皇后に神憑りして神託し、皇后の{{jalink|三韓征伐|Q11249435|三韓征討}}に協力することで征討は成功する{{Sfn|古事記|1963|pp=132-134}}{{Sfn|書紀|1967|pp=330-332}}。『日本書紀』では朝鮮からの帰還に際して神託があったとし、住吉神の{{jalink|荒魂}}を祀る祠を穴門山田邑に、{{jalink|和魂}}を祀る祠を大津渟中倉長峡に設けたとする{{Sfn|書紀|1967|p=336}}（一般にはそれぞれ下関の{{jalink|住吉神社 (下関市)|Q11381858|住吉神社}}、大阪の{{jalink|住吉大社|Q705949}}に比定）{{Sfn|住吉神社（神々）|1984}}。 一方で当社縁起では、住吉神が生まれた阿波岐原を当地に比定する{{Sfn|住吉神社（式内社）|1978}}{{sfn|住吉神社（平凡社）|2004}}{{Refnest|group=注釈|住吉神社から西に約10キロメートルには日向峠、北東に約10キロメートルには古賀市青柳（阿波岐?）がある。また立花山（橘?）、その北の尾東山麓（小戸?）といった地名が関連づけられる。}}。その説の中で、『日本書紀』『日本書紀』神功皇后摂政前紀仲哀天皇9年9月己卯（10日）条。において三韓征討以前に神功皇后が{{jalink|依網男垂見|Q24899491|依網吾彦男垂見}}に対して住吉神の神主を命じたとする記事{{Sfn|書紀|1967|pp=335-336}}を当社の創建記とし、ここから全ての住吉神社の中で最も早く創建されたとする{{Sfn|住吉神社（式内社）|1978}}。 住吉三神を構成する底筒男命・中筒男命・表筒男命の「ツツノヲ」の字義については、諸説がある。ツツは夕月（ゆうづつ）のツツに通じ、夕方の月、{{jalink|宵の明星}}、星を指し、星は航海の指針に用いられることから、海神を示す説{{Sfn|川口|1993|p=148}}、「津の男」に見る説、「ツツ」を船の呪杖に見る説、船霊を納める筒に見る説、対馬の豆酘（つつ）に関連づけて「豆酘の男」に見る説、航海に従った持衰の身を「ツツシム」に見る説などである{{Sfn|住吉神社（神々）|1984}}{{Sfn|住吉三神（国史）}}{{Sfn|岡田精司|2011|pp=86-109}}。 === 歴史 === === 創建 === 社記（筑前国住吉大明神御縁起社蔵。収蔵：{{Cite book |和書 |title={{jalink|神道大系|Q11590923}} 神社編44 - 筑前・筑後・豊前・豊後国 |publisher=神道大系編纂会 |year=1982}}）では、この住吉神社が鎮座する地を住吉神の生まれた阿波岐原（あはきはら、檍原）の古跡に比定する{{sfn|住吉神社（平凡社）|2004}}。これをもって当社では、当社が上古よりの鎮座として「住吉本社」または「日本第一の住吉宮」であるとし{{Sfn|住吉神社（神々）|1984}}、全国2千数百社ある住吉神社の始源である根拠としている{{sfn|住吉神社（平凡社）|2004}}{{Sfn|住吉神社（角川）|1988}}{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000|pp=576-577}}。 中世絵図の「博多古図」には、当社の鎮座地が地形的には比恵川と{{jalink|那珂川 (九州)|Q11642765|那珂川}}の河口に突き出た冷泉津の岬の上に位置する様子が見られ、当地は航海守護神の祭祀地として適地であったと考えられている{{Sfn|住吉神社（神々）|1984}}{{sfn|住吉神社（平凡社）|2004}}。また『{{jalink|和名抄}}』では{{jalink|筑前国|Q1047664}}{{jalink|那珂郡 (福岡県)|Q11642798|那珂郡}}に{{jalink|海人部|Q55528867|海人族}}の集落に共通すると考えられる古代地名「海部郷」の記載があるほか、境内からは{{jalink|弥生時代|Q207858}}の{{jalink|銅戈|Q11650186}}・{{jalink|銅矛|Q11650189|銅鉾（銅矛）}}が出土したとも伝えられることから、当地が古くから海人族にとっての聖地であったとする説もある{{Sfn|住吉神社（神々）|1984}}。 なお『筑前国続風土記拾遺』では、当社の元地を{{jalink|現人神社|Q85882377}}（{{jalink|福岡県|Q123258}}{{jalink|那珂川市|Q1206001}}）とする{{Sfn|住吉神社（式内社）|1978}}{{Sfn|住吉神社（神々）|1984}}。この伝承では現人神社の地まで海岸線であったとし、海岸線の後退とともに現在の博多区住吉に遷座したとしている。『式内社調査報告』では、住吉神社と現人神社の中間に{{jalink|奴国|Q600473}}のものと思われる遺跡（{{jalink|須玖岡本遺跡|Q11473236}}など）が展開していたことから、{{jalink|那珂川|Q1076983}}の上流・下流に位置する神社として古代より両社の祭祀が結ばれていたとする説を挙げている{{Sfn|住吉神社（式内社）|1978}}。 また、全国的に住吉神を祀る神社に関して見た場合、『{{jalink|住吉大社神代記|Q11381815}}』や『{{jalink|延喜式|Q1342448}}』{{jalink|延喜式神名帳|Q11064932|神名帳}}（{{jalink|927年|Q30470}}成立）において{{jalink|摂津国|Q864163}}・{{jalink|播磨国|Q1047523}}・{{jalink|長門国|Q907382}}・{{jalink|筑前国|Q1047664}}・{{jalink|壱岐国|Q1052938}}・{{jalink|対馬国|Q1054861}}にそれぞれ住吉神社の記載があることから、当社含めこれらの社には朝鮮航路の要所に配置する意図があったとする説もある{{Sfn|岡田精司|2011|pp=86-109}}。この中で、住吉神は神功皇后の征討伝承と不可分であることから国家的な航海守護神に位置づけられていたとし、{{jalink|5世紀|Q8095}}の{{jalink|倭の五王|Q1152880}}の頃から{{jalink|ヤマト王権|Q2658252}}の軍事・外交に深く関わっていたとする説もある{{Sfn|岡田精司|2011|pp=86-109}}。 === 概史 === ==== 古代 ==== 『続日本紀』{{jalink|天平|Q1199879}}9年（{{jalink|737年|Q23583}}）4月乙巳朔条にて、{{jalink|伊勢神宮|Q687168}}などとともに「筑紫住吉」に{{jalink|新羅|Q28456}}の無礼の報告と奉幣がなされた{{Sfn|住吉神社（角川）|1988}}。『{{jalink|新抄格勅符抄|Q11502312}}』『新抄格勅符抄』巻10（神事諸家封戸）大同元年（806年）牒（{{Harvnb|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。によれば、{{jalink|大同 (日本)|Q1373191|大同}}元年（{{jalink|806年|Q30021}}）には「{{jalink|住吉神}}」に{{jalink|神封|Q1689534}}36戸が{{jalink|筑前国|Q1047664}}から充てられている{{Sfn|住吉神社（角川）|1988}}。また{{jalink|承和 (日本)|Q1075605|承和}}14年（{{jalink|847年|Q30354}}）には僧{{jalink|円仁|Q732282}}が、{{jalink|仁寿|Q1373077}}2年（{{jalink|852年|Q30383}}）には僧{{jalink|円珍|Q1972505}}が入唐にあたって経典の読誦を行なっている{{Sfn|住吉神社（神々）|1984}}。 {{jalink|六国史|Q1151168|国史}}では、{{jalink|天安 (日本)|Q1075611|天安}}3年（{{jalink|859年|Q23897}}）に筑前国の「住吉神」の{{jalink|神階|Q11591025}}が無位から従五位下に昇叙されたと見えるほか、{{jalink|元慶|Q747451}}2年（{{jalink|878年|Q23910}}）『日本三代実録』元慶2年（878年）12月24日条（{{Harvnb|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。には「新羅凶賊」を告げる{{jalink|香椎宮|Q631373}}の託宣を受けて朝廷の奉幣に預かっている{{Sfn|住吉神社（角川）|1988}}。 {{jalink|延長 (元号)|Q1327274|延長}}5年（{{jalink|927年|Q30470}}）成立の『{{jalink|延喜式|Q1342448}}』{{jalink|延喜式神名帳|Q11064932|神名帳}}では、筑前国{{jalink|那珂郡 (福岡県)|Q11642798|那珂郡}}に「住吉神社三座 並名神大」と記載され、3座が{{jalink|名神大社|Q9610964}}に列している{{Sfn|住吉神社（角川）|1988}}。また『住吉大社神代記』では、「筑前国那珂郡住吉社三前」や「筑前国那珂郡住吉荒魂社三前」の表記で記載されている{{Sfn|岡田精司|2011|pp=86-109}}{{Sfn|住吉神社（神々）|1984}}。{{jalink|寛仁|Q1193951}}元年（{{jalink|1019年|Q19252}}）『左経記』寛仁元年（1019年）10月2日条。には{{jalink|後一条天皇|Q374087}}の1代1度の奉幣に預かったほか、{{jalink|元永|Q1193613}}2年（{{jalink|1119年|Q19540}}）『中右記』元永2年（1119年）4月26日条。にも住吉社遷宮の日時勘申がなされており、国家神的性格は{{jalink|平安時代|Q193292}}末期にも継続する{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000|pp=576-577}}。 ==== 中世・近世 ==== {{jalink|中世|Q12554}}以降は{{jalink|建武 (日本)|Q1193970|建武}}元年（{{jalink|1334年|Q6007}}）の文書を初見として筑前国の{{jalink|一宮|Q1656379}}の位置づけにあったとされる{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000|pp=576-577}}。文献では筑前国の一宮として{{jalink|筥崎宮|Q714742}}（福岡市{{jalink|東区 (福岡市)|Q1206659|東区}}{{jalink|箱崎 (福岡市)|Q11603321|箱崎}}）も見られるが、中世以前の史料で一宮の記述が確認されているのは筑前国で住吉神社のみになる{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000|pp=576-577}}。この頃の{{jalink|竹崎季長|Q1064936}}の『{{jalink|蒙古襲来絵詞|Q3087790}}』では、住吉神社の朱塗りの鳥居が描かれている{{Sfn|住吉神社（式内社）|1978}}。また{{jalink|文明 (日本)|Q1193544|文明}}12年（{{jalink|1480年|Q6628}}）には連歌師の{{jalink|宗祇|Q923562}}が参詣しており、『筑紫道記』に戦乱による住吉神社荒廃の様子を記している{{sfn|住吉神社（平凡社）|2004}}。{{jalink|戦国時代 (日本)|Q204023|戦国時代}}には、当社に伝わる古文書を山口の{{jalink|大内義隆|Q1065163}}のもとに上進していたところ、{{jalink|天文 (元号)|Q1192853|天文}}20年（{{jalink|1551年|Q6560}}）の{{jalink|大寧寺の変|Q10856357}}に巻き込まれその一切を散逸したという{{sfn|住吉神社（平凡社）|2004}}。 [[File:Kuroda Nagamasa.jpg|thumb|160px|right|{{center|{{jalink|黒田長政|Q950496}}}}{{small|{{jalink|福岡藩|Q208766}}初代藩主。現在の本殿を再建。}}]] {{jalink|江戸時代|Q184963}}、{{jalink|福岡藩|Q208766|福岡藩主}}となった{{jalink|黒田長政|Q950496}}が{{jalink|元和 (日本)|Q635245|元和}}9年（{{jalink|1623年|Q6818}}）に白銀2,000枚を下行して社殿を再興し、そのときの本殿が現在まで使用されている{{sfn|住吉神社（平凡社）|2004}}。{{jalink|天和 (日本)|Q1145289|天和}}3年（{{jalink|1683年|Q7651}}）には3代藩主{{jalink|黒田光之|Q11678571}}が社領として30石を寄せ、{{jalink|文化 (元号)|Q1373146|文化}}13年（{{jalink|1816年|Q6953}}）には10代藩主{{jalink|黒田斉清|Q11678605}}が20石を加増したことにより計50石を有した{{sfn|住吉神社（平凡社）|2004}}。この頃の{{jalink|別当寺|Q11396755}}は松花山円福寺であった{{Sfn|住吉神社（角川）|1988}}。 ==== 近代以降 ==== {{jalink|明治維新|Q8707}}後、{{jalink|明治|Q3125096}}5年（{{jalink|1872年|Q7753}}）に{{jalink|近代社格制度|Q712534}}において{{jalink|県社}}に列し、{{jalink|大正|Q329174}}14年（{{jalink|1925年|Q18107}}）に{{jalink|近代社格制度#官社|Q712534|官幣小社}}に昇格した{{Sfn|住吉神社（角川）|1988}}。戦後は{{jalink|神社本庁|Q908077}}の{{jalink|別表神社|Q10898274}}に列している。 {{jalink|平成|Q234510}}16年（{{jalink|2004年|Q2014}}）からは境内域周辺（住吉神社遺跡）で発掘調査が開始されている{{Sfn|住吉神社遺跡第1次調査報告|2006|p=6}}。平成26年（{{jalink|2014年|Q1999}}）までの計3次の調査では、中世-近世期の屋敷地の遺構が祭祀に関わる遺物を伴い検出されるとともに[http://bunkazai.city.fukuoka.lg.jp/excavation_news/detail/18/from_sp:1 博多区住吉で中世の屋敷跡を発見! -住吉神社遺跡第3次発掘調査について-]（福岡市ホームページ）。、屋敷地の方位が現在の本殿と一致し、この方位が中世前半まで遡ることも認められた{{Sfn|住吉神社遺跡第1次調査報告|2006|p=6}}。 === 神階 === * {{jalink|天安 (日本)|Q1075611|天安}}3年（{{jalink|859年|Q23897}}）1月27日、無位から従五位下 （『{{jalink|日本三代実録|Q1052981}}』）『日本三代実録』貞観元年（859年）正月27日条（{{Harvnb|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 - 表記は「住吉神」。 === 神職・社領 === 神職は、『{{jalink|類聚符宣抄|Q11665188}}』の{{jalink|天元 (日本)|Q1327101|天元}}2年（{{jalink|979年|Q23784}}）太政官符によると大宮司があったといい、『{{jalink|吾妻鏡|Q1042324}}』には{{jalink|源頼朝|Q242800}}にも仕えた神官として佐伯氏の名が見え{{sfn|住吉神社（平凡社）|2004}}、その後は佐伯氏末裔の横田氏が代々担ったという{{Sfn|住吉神社（神々）|1984}}。社領は文献に「住吉庄」と見え、その所属は後白河院領、宣陽門院領、伏見院領、天皇家領と変遷しながら継続した{{Sfn|住吉神社（角川）|1988}}。 {{jalink|天保|Q1369045}}時代の大宮司・横田織江は、{{jalink|福岡藩|Q208766}}に禁じられた神道式祭祀の復活を願い、{{jalink|筥崎宮|Q714742}}や{{jalink|宇美八幡宮|Q924940}}の大宮司らと{{jalink|京都|Q740246}}の{{jalink|一条家|Q1535498}}に訴え出たところ、藩から帰郷命令が出て逮捕され、天保4年（1833年）、隠居と{{jalink|座敷牢|Q11486150}}での謹慎を命じられた『大三輪長兵衛の生涯』葦津泰国（葦津事務所、2008年）p42。 === 境内 === [[File:Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka), honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|本殿（重要文化財）}}{{small|社殿形式は「住吉造」である。}}]] 境内の広さは8,107坪（2.68ヘクタール）。博多が砂丘上に立地するのとは異なり、境内周辺は那珂川の沖積地に立地する。 境内社殿のうち{{jalink|神社建築#本殿|Q3080012|'''本殿'''}}は、{{jalink|江戸時代|Q184963}}前期の{{jalink|元和 (日本)|Q635245|元和}}9年（{{jalink|1623年|Q6818}}）の{{jalink|福岡藩|Q208766|福岡藩主}}{{jalink|黒田長政|Q950496}}による造営。{{jalink|神明造|Q930545}}・{{jalink|大社造|Q387874}}と並んで、古い社殿形式とされる「'''{{jalink|住吉造|Q3503635}}'''」{{Sfn|稲垣|2000|p=174}}{{Sfn|米澤|2016|pp=112-113}}を採用する。桁行（奥行）4間・梁間（間口）2間の{{jalink|切妻造|Q13308575}}で、屋根は{{jalink|檜皮葺|Q90373477}}。屋根やそれに付す{{jalink|破風|Q4881511}}・{{jalink|千木・鰹木|Q87220234|千木・堅魚木}}3本が直線的である点は、古式建築を反映する。柱は朱色、板壁は白色で彩る。{{Sfn|岡田精司|2011|pp=86-109}}。国の{{jalink|重要文化財|Q1188622}}に指定されている[http://www.fsg.pref.fukuoka.jp/bunka/contents_detail.asp?table=t6&fields=f767&id=1307-4&bunrui=kuni_yuke_kenz_juyo 住吉神社本殿]（ふくおか社会教育ネットワーク「福岡県の文化財」）。[http://bunkazai.city.fukuoka.lg.jp/cultural_properties/detail/140 住吉神社本殿]（福岡市文化財保護課「福岡市の文化財」）。。 本殿前に建てられている{{jalink|神社建築#拝殿|Q3080012|'''拝殿'''}}は、{{jalink|入母屋造|Q855025}}で、屋根は銅板葺。また境内南側にある{{jalink|住吉神社能楽殿|Q132168040|能楽殿}}（のうがくでん）は、{{jalink|警固神社|Q11632314}}（福岡市中央区天神）能楽堂の老朽化に伴い{{jalink|昭和|Q327567}}10年（{{jalink|1935年|Q18658}}）から住吉神社内での造営が計画され、昭和13年（{{jalink|1938年|Q18645}}）に完成したものになる。{{jalink|入母屋造|Q855025}}の妻入りで、屋根は波子鉄板葺。この能楽殿は日本の伝統様式と洋風の様式を一体とした近代和風建築であり、福岡市指定文化財に指定されている[http://bunkazai.city.fukuoka.lg.jp/cultural_properties/detail/158 住吉神社能楽殿]（福岡市文化財保護課「福岡市の文化財」）。境内説明板。。 そのほか、境内には神楽殿・神門などの社殿がある。 ファイル:住吉大社 本殿平面図.tif|住吉造の平面図 File:Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka) nougakuden.JPG|能楽殿（福岡市指定文化財）の入る建物 File:Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka) shinmon.JPG|神門 === 主な祭事 === ; 追儺祭 : 「ついなさい」。1月7日。皇室・国家の繁栄祈願として、鬼すべ・鷽替え（うそ替え）神事を行う[http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/winter.html 冬の祭典・行事]（公式サイト）。 ; 御田祭 : 「おんださい」。3月7日。五穀豊穣祈願として、播種神事を行う[http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/spring.html 春の祭典・行事]（公式サイト）。 ; 潮干祭 : 「しおひさい」。4月3日。航海安全・豊漁祈願として神幸（神輿渡御）を行う。かつて門前に海が広がった頃には船での神幸であったというが、現在は陸上での神幸として行う。 ; 名越大祭 : 「なごしたいさい」。7月30日から8月1日。伊弉諾尊の禊で住吉神が生まれたことに関係する神事で、穢れ祓いとして茅の輪くぐりや人形流しの神事を行う[http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/summer.html 夏の祭典・行事]（公式サイト）。 ; 例大祭 : 「'''相撲会大祭'''（すもうえたいさい）」または単に「相撲会祭」とも。10月12日から14日。住吉神社で最も重要な祭。神功皇后が朝鮮から帰国したとき、住吉神に対して神恩感謝として相撲・{{jalink|流鏑馬|Q1886157}}を奉納したことに由来するという。祭事では、稚児行列のほか・流鏑馬・少年相撲が奉納される[http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/autumn.html 秋の祭典・行事]（公式サイト）。 ; 歩射祭 : 「ほしゃさい」。11月7日。元慶2年（878年）の{{jalink|陽成天皇|Q349280}}の奉幣の際、住吉神の霊験により外賊の災いがなくなったことの謝礼として、{{jalink|大宰府|Q144845}}役人が南西（裏鬼門）方向に歩射を行なったことが由来とされる神事。国家鎮護祈願として社前で歩射を行う。 === 文化財 === === The pillars are painted vermilion and the wooden walls are painted white. {{Sfn|Seiji Okada|2011|pp=86-109}}. [http://www.fsg.pref.fukuoka.jp/bunka/contents_detail.asp?table=t6&fields=f767&id=1307-4&bunrui=kuni_yuke_kenz_juyo Sumiyoshi Shrine Main Hall] (Fukuoka Social Education Network ``Cultural Properties of Fukuoka Prefecture''). [http://bunkazai.city.fukuoka.lg.jp/cultural_properties/detail/140 Sumiyoshi Shrine Main Hall] (Fukuoka City Cultural Properties Protection Division ``Fukuoka City Cultural Properties''). .The {{jalink|Shrine architecture#haiden|Q3080012|'''haiden'''}} built in front of the main shrine is {{jalink|gambling|Q855025}} and has a copper plate roof. In addition, {{jalink|Sumiyoshi Shrine Nohgakuden|Q132168040|Nogakuden}} (Nogakuden) located on the south side of the precincts has been renovated due to the aging of {{jalink|Kego Shrine|Q11632314}} (Tenjin, Chuo-ku, Fukuoka City) Nohgakuden. ink|Showa|Q327567}} Construction within Sumiyoshi Shrine was planned in 1935 ({{jalink|1935|Q18658}}) and completed in 1938 ({{jalink|1938|Q18645}}). {{jalink|Irimoya-zukuri|Q855025}} with a gable roof and a corrugated iron plate roof. This Noh theater hall is a modern Japanese-style building that combines traditional Japanese and Western styles, and has been designated as a designated cultural property by Fukuoka City. Precinct information board. . In addition, there are shrine buildings such as a Kagura hall and a Shinto gate within the precincts. {{small|It is said that Hojo-e rituals were held here in the old days. }} File:Tenryu Ike Sumiyoshi.JPG|Tenryu Pond (Shioiri Pond) === Sessha === There are a total of 8 Setsusha shrines, 2 Setsusha shrines and 6 Setsusha shrines. === Sessha === [[File:Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka), Shiga-jinja and Funarama-jinja.JPG|thumb|230px|right|{{center|Funatama Shrine (right) and Shiga Shrine (left)}}]] * Funatama Shrine - Enshrined deity: {{jalink|Sartahiko|Q3090037|Sarutahiko no Mikoto}}. Regular festival: September 9th. * Shiga Shrine - Enshrined Deity: {{jalink|Watatsumi|Q1474187|Watatsumi Three Gods}}. Regular festival: June 1st. === Suesha === * Sukuhikona Shrine - Enshrined deity: {{jalink|Sukunabikona|Q3275687|Sukunahikona no Mikoto}}. Regular festival: June 8th. * Inari Shrine - Enshrined deity: {{jalink|Ukanomitama|Q3080728|Uga no Tamashii}}. Regular festival: October 10th. * Ebisu Shrine - Enshrined deity: {{jalink|Kotoshiro-shu|Q8009611|Kotoshiro-shu no Mikoto}}. Regular festival: January 3rd. * Sugawara Shrine (Tenmangu) - Enshrined deity: {{jalink|Michizane Sugawara|Q382005}}. Regular festival: August 25th. * Hitomaru Shrine - Enshrined deity: {{jalink|Kakimoto Hitomaro|Q380818|Kakimoto Hitomaro}}. Regular festival: March 18th. * Amatsu Shrine - Enshrined outside the west gate. Enshrined deity: {{jalink|Izanagi|Q813858|Izanagi Okami}}. Regular festival: April 22nd. Other affiliated companies include Chiyomori Shrine (Chiyo, Hakata-ku, Fukuoka City), Shiteruhime Shrine (Gion-cho, Hakata-ku, Fukuoka City), and {{jalink|Tetsudo Shrine (Fukuoka City)|Q30932529|Tetsudo Shrine}} (Hakata Station Chuo-gai, Hakata-ku, Fukuoka City, {{jalink|JR Hakata City|Q11226208}} rooftop). File:Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka), Sukunahikona-jinja.JPG|Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka), Sukunahikona-jinja Shrine File:Uga Shrine in Sumiyoshi Shrine.JPG|Inari Shrine File:Sumiyoshi Shrine_Ebisu Shrine.jpg|Ebisu ShrineFile:Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka), Sugawara-jinja and Hitomaru-jinja.JPG|Sugawara Shrine (left, Tenmangu Shrine), Hitomaru Shrine (right) File:Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka), Amatsu-jinja.JPG|Amatsu Shrine === Festival === === Annual festival ===
List of annual festivals
List of festivals held annually at Sumiyoshi Shrine [http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/index.html About festivals and events] (official website). . * January ** Saitan Festival (January 1st) ** Sumiyoshi Mikka Ebisu Shrine Annual Festival (January 3rd) **Oiina Festival (January 7th) *February **Setsubun Festival (February 3rd) ** Inari Shrine Hatsuuma Festival (February Hatsuuma Festival) ** National Foundation Memorial Festival (February 11th) * March ** Oda Festival (March 7th) ** Hitomaru Shrine Annual Festival (March 18th) *April ** Shiohi Festival (April 3rd) ** Amatsu Shrine Annual Festival (April 22nd) *　June ** Funatama Shrine Annual Festival (June 1st) ** Sukuhikona Shrine Annual Festival (June 8th) ** Great Purification Ceremony (June 30th) * July ** Nagoshi Festival (July 30th - August 1st) *August ** Sugawara Shrine Annual Festival (August 25th) *September ** Hayao Festival (September 4th) ** Shiga Shrine Annual Festival (September 9th) * October ** Inari Shrine Annual Festival (October 10th)** '''Reitaisai'' ('''Sumo Kai Taisai'''/Sumo Kai Festival) (October 12th-14th) ** Jingu Harukaishiki (October 17th) *November ** Ayusha Festival (November 7th) ** Inari Shrine Kazu Festival, Sukuhikona Shrine Annual Festival (November 8th) ** Kanpeisha Ranking Anniversary Festival (November 10th) ** New Grain Appreciation Festival (November 23rd) *December ** Great Purification Ceremony, New Year's Eve Festival (December 31st)
=== Main festivals === ;Oiina Festival : "Follow me." January 7th. As a prayer for the prosperity of the imperial family and the nation, the Onisube and Uso-kaeshi rituals are held [http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/winter.html Winter festivals and events] (official website). ; Oda Festival : "Ondasai". March 7th. A sowing ritual is held as a prayer for a rich harvest. ; Shiohi Festival : "Shiohisai". April 3rd. A mikoshi (portable shrine) is performed to pray for safe navigation and a bountiful catch. It is said that in the past, when the sea spread out in front of the gates, the shrine was celebrated by boat, but now it is performed on land. ; Nagoshi Grand Festival : “I want to relax.” July 30th to August 1st. It is a Shinto ritual related to the birth of Sumiyoshi deity during the purification of Izani no Mikoto, and rituals such as passing through grass rings and floating puppets are performed to purify impurities. ; Reitaisai: Also known as ``Sumo-kai Taisai'' or simply ``Sumo-kai Festival.'' October 12th to 14th. The most important festival at Sumiyoshi Shrine. It is said that the name originates from the fact that when Empress Jingu returned from Korea, she dedicated sumo and {{jalink|yabusame|Q1886157}} to the deity Sumiyoshi as a thank you for the blessings of the gods. At the festival, in addition to a procession of children, yabusame and youth sumo are offered. ; Shooting Festival : "Hoshasai". November 7th. This Shinto ritual is said to have its origins in the {{jalink|Dazaifu|Q144845}} official who, during the {{jalink|Emperor Yozei|Q349280}}'s offering in 878, performed a walking shot in the southwest (Urakimon) direction as a reward for the miraculous powers of the god Sumiyoshi who had ended the disaster of foreign pirates. A shooting ceremony is held in front of the shrine to pray for the protection of the nation. === Cultural assets === === Important cultural property (designated by the country) === * Main shrine (building) - {{jalink|Edo period|Q184963}} early period. Designated on April 13, 1922 (Taisho 11) === Fukuoka Prefecture designated cultural property === * Tangible cultural properties [https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~ri5t-mk/itiran/koukosiryo.html Archaeological materials list] (Fukuoka City cultural properties ). ** 6-piece copper sword (archaeological material) **: {{jalink|Bronze sword|Q11650186}} from the middle of the {{jalink|Yayoi period|Q207858}}. It is said that it was excavated from behind the shrine building, but the condition and location of the excavation are unknown. It is medium-slender, with a total length of around 34 centimeters. Designated October 29, 1958 [http://www.fsg.pref.fukuoka.jp/bunka/contents_detail.asp?table=t61&fields=f2293&id=1307-112&bunrui=kenn_yuke_biju_koko [Fukuoka Social Education Network ``Cultural Properties of Fukuoka Prefecture'']. . ** 5 copper hoko (archaeological material)**: {{jalink|bronze spear|Q11650189|bronze spear}} from the middle of the Yayoi period. It is said that it was excavated from behind the shrine building like the bronze dagger, but its condition and location are unknown. Designated October 29, 1958 [http://www.fsg.pref.fukuoka.jp/bunka/contents_detail.asp?table=t61&fields=f2293&id=1307-113&bunrui=kenn_yuke_biju_koko Dohoko] (Fukuoka Social Education Network ``Cultural Properties of Fukuoka Prefecture''). . === Cultural property designated by Fukuoka City === * Tangible Cultural Properties [https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~ri5t-mk/itiran/kenzoubutu.html List of Tangible Cultural Properties Buildings] (Fukuoka City Cultural Properties ). [https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~ri5t-mk/itiran/komonjo.html List of books, classics, and old books] (Fukuoka City Cultural Properties ). ** Nohgakuden (building) - Built in 1938. Designated on March 23, 2000. ** Karamon (building) - Built in the Edo period. Designated on March 18, 2010. ** Matsuka Wakashu Volume 5 Volume 1 (Books, Classics, Old Books) - A collection of poems from the end of the {{jalink|Kamakura period|Q236205}}. Designated on March 30, 1987. ** 27 Sumiyoshi Shrine documents (books, classics, old books) - Documents from the Kamakura period onwards. Designated on March 30, 1987. === Others === * Ancient Hakata Map - A pictorial map depicting Hakata in the medieval period. * The origin of Sumiyoshi Daimyojin - The origin of the origin established There are various theories regarding the literal meaning of ``Tsutsunowo'' for the three Sumiyoshi deities, Sokozutsu no Mikoto, Nakazutsu no no Mikoto, and Omotzutsu no Mikoto. The word tutu is related to the evening moon, and refers to the evening moon, {{jalink|evening star}}, and the stars.As stars are used as guides for navigation, there are some theories that it refers to the god of the sea, {{Sfn|Kawaguchi|1993|p=148}}, a theory that it is seen as a ``Tsu man,'' a theory that sees ``tutu'' as a ship's cursed staff, and a tube that houses a ship's spirit. There is a theory that he is seen as a ``mametsu man'' in connection with the Tsutsu of Tsushima, and a theory that he is seen as a ``Tsutushimu'', a body with a weakened body that accompanies a voyage. === History === === Founding === Shrine (Chikuzen Province Sumiyoshi Daimyojin Engi Shrine collection. According to this legend, the current location of the Jinjin Shrine was along the coastline, and as the coastline receded, it was moved to the current location of Sumiyoshi, Hakata Ward. In the "Shikinaisha Investigation Report", there are ruins thought to belong to {{jalink|Nakoku|Q600473}} (such as {{jalink|Suku Okamoto Ruins|Q11473236}}) located between Sumiyoshi Shrine and Genjin Shrine. Therefore, there is a theory that the rituals of the two shrines have been connected since ancient times as a shrine located upstream and downstream of {{jalink|Naka River|Q1076983}} {{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1978}}. {{Location map+|Japan|width=230|float=right|caption={{Center|Distribution of Sumiyoshi Shrine (limited to {{jalink|Shikiuchi}})}}|places= {{Location map~|Japan|lat_deg=34|lat_min=36|lat_sec=44.60|lon_deg=135|lon_min=29|lon_sec=37.63|position=right|mark=Blue pog.svg|marksize=8|label={{jalink|Sumiyoshi Taisha|Q705949}}}}{{Location map~|Japan|lat_deg=36|lat_min=58|lat_sec=29.08|lon_deg=140|lon_min=52|lon_sec=58.94|mark=Blue pog.svg|marksize=8}} {{Location map~|Japan|lat_deg=34|lat_min=58|lat_sec=0.38|lon_deg=135|lon_min=3|lon_sec=34.42|mark=Blue pog.svg|marksize=8}} {{Location map~|Japan|lat_deg=33|lat_min=59|lat_sec=58.75|lon_deg=130|lon_min=57|lon_sec=23.70|mark=Blue pog.svg|marksize=8}} {{Location map~|Japan|lat_deg=33|lat_min=35|lat_sec=9.26|lon_deg=130|lon_min=24|lon_sec=49.33|position=bottom|mark=Red pog.svg|marksize=8|label={{color|#FF0000|'''Sumiyoshi Shrine'''}}}}{{Location map~|Japan|lat_deg=33|lat_min=47|lat_sec=18.53|lon_deg=129|lon_min=42|lon_sec=23.43|mark=Blue pog.svg|marksize=8}} {{Location map~|Japan|lat_deg=34|lat_min=16|lat_sec=8.03|lon_deg=129|lon_min=18|lon_sec=54.18|mark=Blue pog.svg|marksize=8}} }}Also, when looking at shrines that enshrine Sumiyoshi deity nationwide, there are "{{jalink|Sumiyoshi Taisha Shindaiki|Q11381815}}" and "{{jalink|Engishiki|Q1342448}}" {{jalink|Engishiki|Q1342448}}. In the Shikigami Namecho|Q11064932|Shinmeicho}} (established in {{jalink|927|Q30470}}), {{jalink|Settsu Province|Q864163}} and {{jalink|Harima Province|Q10475 23}}・{{jalink|Nagato Province|Q907382}}・{{jalink|Chikuzen Province|Q1047664}}・{{jalink|Iki Province|Q1052938}}・{{jalink|Tsushima Province|Q1 054861}}, there are descriptions of Sumiyoshi Shrines in each of them, so there is a theory that these shrines, including ours, had the intention of locating them at key points on the Korean route {{Sfn|Seiji Okada|2011|pp=86-109}}. === Main festivals === ;Oiina Festival : "Follow me." January 7th. As a prayer for the prosperity of the imperial family and the nation, the Onisube and Uso-kaeshi rituals are held [http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/winter.html Winter festivals and events] (official website). ; Oda Festival : "Ondasai". March 7th. A sowing ritual is held as a prayer for a rich harvest. ; Shiohi Festival : "Shiohisai". April 3rd. A mikoshi (portable shrine) is performed to pray for safe navigation and a bountiful catch. It is said that in the past, when the sea spread out in front of the gates, the shrine was celebrated by boat, but now it is performed on land. ; Nagoshi Grand Festival : “I want to relax.” July 30th to August 1st. It is a Shinto ritual related to the birth of Sumiyoshi deity during the purification of Izani no Mikoto, and rituals such as passing through grass rings and floating puppets are performed to purify impurities. ; Reitaisai: Also known as ``Sumo-kai Taisai'' or simply ``Sumo-kai Festival.'' October 12th to 14th. The most important festival at Sumiyoshi Shrine. It is said that the name originates from the fact that when Empress Jingu returned from Korea, she dedicated sumo and {{jalink|yabusame|Q1886157}} to the deity Sumiyoshi as a thank you for the blessings of the gods. At the festival, in addition to a procession of children, yabusame and youth sumo are offered. ; Shooting Festival : "Hoshasai". November 7th. This Shinto ritual is said to have its origins in the {{jalink|Dazaifu|Q144845}} official who, during the {{jalink|Emperor Yozei|Q349280}}'s offering in 878, performed a walking shot in the southwest (Urakimon) direction as a reward for the miraculous powers of the god Sumiyoshi who had ended the disaster of foreign pirates. A shooting ceremony is held in front of the shrine to pray for the protection of the nation. === Cultural assets === === Important cultural property (designated by the country) === * Main shrine (building) - {{jalink|Edo period|Q184963}} early period. Unlike Hakata, which is located on sand dunes, the area around the shrine grounds is located on the alluvial land of the Naka River.Among the shrine buildings in the precincts, the {{jalink|Shrine architecture #main shrine|Q3080012|'''main shrine'''}} was built in the early {{jalink|Edo period|Q184963}} period. (Japan)|Q635245|Genna}}9 year ({{jalink|1623|Q6818}}) Built by {{jalink|Fukuoka domain|Q208766|Fukuoka feudal lord}}{{jalink|Nagamasa Kuroda|Q950496}}. Along with {{jalink|Shinmei-zukuri|Q930545}} and {{jalink|Taisha-zukuri|Q387874}}, it is said to be an old shrine style.''{{jalink |Sumiyoshizo|Q3503635}}''''' {{Sfn|Inagaki|2000|p=174}}{{Sfn|Yonezawa|2016|pp=112-113}} will be adopted. It is {{jalink|gabled construction|Q13308575}} with 4 girders (depth) and 2 beams (frontage), and the roof is {{jalink|cypress bark|Q90373477}}. The straight lines of the roof and the three {{jalink|gables|Q4881511}} and {{jalink|chigi/katsuogi|Q87220234|chigi/kataogi}} reflect the ancient architecture. The pillars are painted vermilion and the wooden walls are painted white. {{Sfn|Seiji Okada|2011|pp=86-109}}. [http://bunkazai.city.fukuoka.lg.jp/cultural_properties/detail/140 Sumiyoshi Shrine Main Hall] (Fukuoka City Cultural Properties Protection Division ``Fukuoka City Cultural Properties''). .The {{jalink|Shrine architecture#haiden|Q3080012|'''haiden'''}} built in front of the main shrine is {{jalink|gambling|Q855025}} and has a copper plate roof. In addition, {{jalink|Sumiyoshi Shrine Nohgakuden|Q132168040|Nogakuden}} (Nogakuden) located on the south side of the precincts has been renovated due to the aging of {{jalink|Kego Shrine|Q11632314}} (Tenjin, Chuo-ku, Fukuoka City) Nohgakuden. ink|Showa|Q327567}} Construction within Sumiyoshi Shrine was planned in 1935 ({{jalink|1935|Q18658}}) and completed in 1938 ({{jalink|1938|Q18645}}). {{jalink|Irimoya-zukuri|Q855025}} with a gable roof and a corrugated iron plate roof. This Noh theater hall is a modern Japanese-style building that combines traditional Japanese and Western styles, and has been designated as a designated cultural property by Fukuoka City. Precinct information board. . In addition, there are shrine buildings such as a Kagura hall and a Shinto gate within the precincts. List of annual festivals
List of festivals held annually at Sumiyoshi Shrine [http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/index.html About festivals and events] (official website). . * January ** Saitan Festival (January 1st) ** Sumiyoshi Mikka Ebisu Shrine Annual Festival (January 3rd) **Oiina Festival (January 7th) *February **Setsubun Festival (February 3rd) ** Inari Shrine Hatsuuma Festival (February Hatsuuma Festival) ** National Foundation Memorial Festival (February 11th) * March ** Oda Festival (March 7th) ** Hitomaru Shrine Annual Festival (March 18th) *April ** Shiohi Festival (April 3rd) ** Amatsu Shrine Annual Festival (April 22nd) *　June ** Funatama Shrine Annual Festival (June 1st) ** Sukuhikona Shrine Annual Festival (June 8th) ** Great Purification Ceremony (June 30th) * July ** Nagoshi Festival (July 30th - August 1st) *August ** Sugawara Shrine Annual Festival (August 25th) *September ** Hayao Festival (September 4th) ** Shiga Shrine Annual Festival (September 9th) * October ** Inari Shrine Annual Festival (October 10th)** '''Reitaisai'' ('''Sumo Kai Taisai'''/Sumo Kai Festival) (October 12th-14th) ** Jingu Harukaishiki (October 17th) *November ** Ayusha Festival (November 7th) ** Inari Shrine Kazu Festival, Sukuhikona Shrine Annual Festival (November 8th) ** Kanpeisha Ranking Anniversary Festival (November 10th) ** New Grain Appreciation Festival (November 23rd) *December ** Great Purification Ceremony, New Year's Eve Festival (December 31st)
=== Main festivals === ;Oiina Festival : "Follow me." January 7th. As a prayer for the prosperity of the imperial family and the nation, the Onisube and Uso-kaeshi rituals are held [http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/winter.html Winter festivals and events] (official website). ; Oda Festival : "Ondasai". March 7th. A sowing ritual is held as a prayer for a rich harvest. ; Shiohi Festival : "Shiohisai". April 3rd. A mikoshi (portable shrine) is performed to pray for safe navigation and a bountiful catch. It is said that in the past, when the sea spread out in front of the gates, the shrine was celebrated by boat, but now it is performed on land. ; Nagoshi Grand Festival : “I want to relax.” July 30th to August 1st. It is a Shinto ritual related to the birth of Sumiyoshi deity during the purification of Izani no Mikoto, and rituals such as passing through grass rings and floating puppets are performed to purify impurities. ; Reitaisai: Also known as ``Sumo-kai Taisai'' or simply ``Sumo-kai Festival.'' October 12th to 14th. The most important festival at Sumiyoshi Shrine. It is said that the name originates from the fact that when Empress Jingu returned from Korea, she dedicated sumo and {{jalink|yabusame|Q1886157}} to the deity Sumiyoshi as a thank you for the blessings of the gods. At the festival, in addition to a procession of children, yabusame and youth sumo are offered. ; Shooting Festival : "Hoshasai". November 7th. This Shinto ritual is said to have its origins in the {{jalink|Dazaifu|Q144845}} official who, during the {{jalink|Emperor Yozei|Q349280}}'s offering in 878, performed a walking shot in the southwest (Urakimon) direction as a reward for the miraculous powers of the god Sumiyoshi who had ended the disaster of foreign pirates. A shooting ceremony is held in front of the shrine to pray for the protection of the nation. === Cultural assets === === Important cultural property (designated by the country) === * Main shrine (building) - {{jalink|Edo period|Q184963}} early period. Designated on April 13, 1922 (Taisho 11) === Fukuoka Prefecture designated cultural property === * Tangible cultural properties [https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~ri5t-mk/itiran/koukosiryo.html Archaeological materials list] (Fukuoka City cultural properties ). ** 6-piece copper sword (archaeological material) **: {{jalink|Bronze sword|Q11650186}} from the middle of the {{jalink|Yayoi period|Q207858}}. It is said that it was excavated from behind the shrine building, but the condition and location of the excavation are unknown. It is medium-slender, with a total length of around 34 centimeters. Designated October 29, 1958 [http://www.fsg.pref.fukuoka.jp/bunka/contents_detail.asp?table=t61&fields=f2293&id=1307-112&bunrui=kenn_yuke_biju_koko [Fukuoka Social Education Network ``Cultural Properties of Fukuoka Prefecture'']. . ** 5 copper hoko (archaeological material)**: {{jalink|bronze spear|Q11650189|bronze spear}} from the middle of the Yayoi period. It is said that it was excavated from behind the shrine building like the bronze dagger, but its condition and location are unknown. Designated October 29, 1958 [http://www.fsg.pref.fukuoka.jp/bunka/contents_detail.asp?table=t61&fields=f2293&id=1307-113&bunrui=kenn_yuke_biju_koko Dohoko] (Fukuoka Social Education Network ``Cultural Properties of Fukuoka Prefecture''). . === Cultural property designated by Fukuoka City === * Tangible Cultural Properties [https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~ri5t-mk/itiran/kenzoubutu.html List of Tangible Cultural Properties Buildings] (Fukuoka City Cultural Properties ). One is the birth scene, where {{jalink|Izanagi|Q813858}} (Izanagi no Mikoto), who returned from the land of Yomi, went to Ahakihara (Enohara) in Tachibana no Odo in Tsukushi-Hyuga to purify himself of the impurities.{{jalink|Misogi|Q1936265 }} Accordingly, these three Sumiyoshi gods were born along with {{jalink|Watatsumi|Q1474187|Watatsumi three gods}} (three sea gods) {{Sfn|Kojiki|1963|pp=28-30}}{{Sfn|Shoki|1967|pp=94-95}}. Next, in the scene of {{jalink|Empress Jingu|Q232803}} dispatching troops to Korea, Sumiyoshi possesses the empress and gives oracles to her, and the empress {{jalink|Sanghan Conquest|Q1124943 5|By cooperating with the Sanhan Conquest}}, the conquest will be successful.{{Sfn|Kojiki|1963|pp=132-134}} "Nihonshoki" states that upon their return from Korea, there was an oracle, and that they built a shrine to enshrine the Sumiyoshi god {{jalink|Aratama}} in Anamon Yamada village, and a shrine to enshrine {{jalink|Watama}} in Nakakura Nagakyo, Otsunoki. Among these theories, "Nihonshoki" "Nihonshoki" includes an article dated September 10, 9th year, 9th year of Emperor Chuai's reign, in the pre-Regency period of Empress Jingu. In , an article states that Empress Jingu ordered {{jalink|Yorami Otarami|Q24899491|Yorami Agohiko Tarumi}} to be the Shinto priest of Sumiyoshi God before the Sanhan Conquest {{Sfn |Shoki|1967|pp=335-336}} is the founding record of our company, and from this it is said that it was the earliest of all Sumiyoshi Shrines to be built {{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1978}}. There are various theories regarding the literal meaning of ``Tsutsunowo'' for the three Sumiyoshi deities, Sokozutsu no Mikoto, Nakazutsu no no Mikoto, and Omotzutsu no Mikoto. The word tutu is related to the evening moon, and refers to the evening moon, {{jalink|evening star}}, and the stars.As stars are used as guides for navigation, there are some theories that it refers to the god of the sea, {{Sfn|Kawaguchi|1993|p=148}}, a theory that it is seen as a ``Tsu man,'' a theory that sees ``tutu'' as a ship's cursed staff, and a tube that houses a ship's spirit. There is a theory that he is seen as a ``mametsu man'' in connection with the Tsutsu of Tsushima, and a theory that he is seen as a ``Tsutushimu'', a body with a weakened body that accompanies a voyage. === History === === Founding === Shrine (Chikuzen Province Sumiyoshi Daimyojin Engi Shrine collection. With this, weThe company is said to be the ``Sumiyoshi Head Office'' or ``Japan's No. 1 Sumiyoshi Shrine,'' which has been the enshrined place since ancient times. In the ``Ancient Map of Hakata,'' a medieval illustrated map, the site of our company is topographically located between the Hie River and the Naka River. (Kyushu)|Q11642765|Q11642765|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Heibonsha)|2004}} It appears to be located on the cape of Reizeitsu that juts out from the mouth of the Naka River, and it is believed that this area was a suitable place for the worship of the guardian god of navigation.{{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Gods)|1984}}{{sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Heibonsha)|2004}} Also, in "{{jalink|Japanese Namesho}}", {{jalink|Chikuzen Province|Q1047664}}{{jalink|Naka County (Fukuoka Prefecture)|Q11642798|Naka District}} There is a mention of the ancient place name ``Kaifu-go'', which is thought to be common to the {{jalink|Amajinbe|Q55528867|Amajin tribe}} villages, and from the precincts there is a mention of {{jal from the {{jalink|Yayoi period|Q207858}}. ink|Bronze halberd|Q11650186}} and {{jalink|Bronze spear|Q11650189|Bronze spear}} are said to have been excavated, so there is a theory that this area has been a sacred place for the Kaijin people since ancient times.{{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Gods)|1984}}.In addition, in the "Chikuzen Kuni Zoku Fudoki Shui", the original location of our company is {{jalink|Genjin Shrine|Q85882377}} ({{jalink|Fukuoka Prefecture|Q123258}}{ {jalink|Nakagawa City|Q1206001}}). According to this legend, the current location of the Jinjin Shrine was along the coastline, and as the coastline receded, it was moved to the current location of Sumiyoshi, Hakata Ward. === Main festivals === ;Oiina Festival : "Follow me." January 7th. As a prayer for the prosperity of the imperial family and the nation, the Onisube and Uso-kaeshi rituals are held [http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/winter.html Winter festivals and events] (official website). ; Oda Festival : "Ondasai". March 7th. A sowing ritual is held as a prayer for a rich harvest. ; Shiohi Festival : "Shiohisai". April 3rd. A mikoshi (portable shrine) is performed to pray for safe navigation and a bountiful catch. It is said that in the past, when the sea spread out in front of the gates, the shrine was celebrated by boat, but now it is performed on land. ; Nagoshi Grand Festival : “I want to relax.” July 30th to August 1st. It is a Shinto ritual related to the birth of Sumiyoshi deity during the purification of Izani no Mikoto, and rituals such as passing through grass rings and floating puppets are performed to purify impurities. ; Reitaisai: Also known as ``Sumo-kai Taisai'' or simply ``Sumo-kai Festival.'' October 12th to 14th. The most important festival at Sumiyoshi Shrine. It is said that the name originates from the fact that when Empress Jingu returned from Korea, she dedicated sumo and {{jalink|yabusame|Q1886157}} to the deity Sumiyoshi as a thank you for the blessings of the gods. At the festival, in addition to a procession of children, yabusame and youth sumo are offered. ; Shooting Festival : "Hoshasai". November 7th. This Shinto ritual is said to have its origins in the {{jalink|Dazaifu|Q144845}} official who, during the {{jalink|Emperor Yozei|Q349280}}'s offering in 878, performed a walking shot in the southwest (Urakimon) direction as a reward for the miraculous powers of the god Sumiyoshi who had ended the disaster of foreign pirates. A shooting ceremony is held in front of the shrine to pray for the protection of the nation. === Cultural assets === === Important cultural property (designated by the country) === * Main shrine (building) - {{jalink|Edo period|Q184963}} early period. There are various theories regarding the literal meaning of ``Tsutsunowo'' for the three Sumiyoshi deities, Sokozutsu no Mikoto, Nakazutsu no no Mikoto, and Omotzutsu no Mikoto. The word tutu is related to the evening moon, and refers to the evening moon, {{jalink|evening star}}, and the stars.As stars are used as guides for navigation, there are some theories that it refers to the god of the sea, {{Sfn|Kawaguchi|1993|p=148}}, a theory that it is seen as a ``Tsu man,'' a theory that sees ``tutu'' as a ship's cursed staff, and a tube that houses a ship's spirit. After the war, it was listed as {{jalink|Beppyō Shrine|Q10898274}} of {{jalink|Shinja Honcho|Q908077}}.{{jalink|Heisei|Q234510}} From 2016 ({{jalink|2004|Q2014}}), excavation surveys have begun around the precincts (Sumiyoshi Shrine ruins) {{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine ruins 1st survey report|2006|p=6}}. In a total of three surveys up to 2014 ({{jalink|2014|Q1999}}), the remains of a mansion from the medieval to early modern period were discovered along with artifacts related to rituals. Medieval mansion ruins discovered in Sumiyoshi, Hakata Ward! - About the third excavation survey of Sumiyoshi Shrine ruins -] (Fukuoka City homepage). , the orientation of the mansion site coincides with the current main shrine, and it was also confirmed that this orientation dates back to the first half of the Middle Ages {{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine Ruins First Survey Report|2006|p=6}}. === God level === * {{jalink|Cheonan (Japan)|Q1075611|Cheonan}} January 27, 3rd year ({{jalink|859|Q23897}}), from no rank to junior fifth rank ("{{jalink|Japan three generation records|Q1052981}}") "Nihon Sandai Jiroku" Article dated 27th New Year, Jogan 1st year (859) (see {{Harvnb|Shinto and Shrine Historical Materials Collection}}). - The spelling is "Sumiyoshi God". === Shinto priest/sharei === Shinto priests are the {{jalink|Tengen (Japan)|Q1327101|Tengen}} 2nd year ({{jalink|979|Q23784}}) According to the Daijo Kanfu, there was a Daiguji, and "{{jalink|Azuma Kagami|Q1042324}}" states that {{jalink|Azuma Kagami|Q1042324}} The name of the Saeki clan appears as a priest who also served |Minamoto no Yoritomo|Q242800}}{{sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Heibonsha)|2004}}, and after that, the Yokota clan, a descendant of the Saeki clan, was in charge for generations {{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. The shrine's territory appears to be ``Sumiyoshi-sho'' in literature, and its affiliation continued through changes such as Goshirakawa-inryo, Senyomon-inryo, Fushimi-inryo, and Imperial family territory {{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Kadokawa)|1988}}. Orie Yokota, the chief priest of the {{jalink|Tenpo|Q1369045}} era, revived Shinto rituals that had been forbidden by the {{jalink|Fukuoka Domain|Q208766}}. Unlike Hakata, which is located on sand dunes, the area around the shrine grounds is located on the alluvial land of the Naka River.Among the shrine buildings in the precincts, the {{jalink|Shrine architecture #main shrine|Q3080012|'''main shrine'''}} was built in the early {{jalink|Edo period|Q184963}} period. === Main festivals === ;Oiina Festival : "Follow me." January 7th. As a prayer for the prosperity of the imperial family and the nation, the Onisube and Uso-kaeshi rituals are held [http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/winter.html Winter festivals and events] (official website). ; Oda Festival : "Ondasai". March 7th. A sowing ritual is held as a prayer for a rich harvest. ; Shiohi Festival : "Shiohisai". April 3rd. A mikoshi (portable shrine) is performed to pray for safe navigation and a bountiful catch. It is said that in the past, when the sea spread out in front of the gates, the shrine was celebrated by boat, but now it is performed on land. ; Nagoshi Grand Festival : “I want to relax.” July 30th to August 1st. It is a Shinto ritual related to the birth of Sumiyoshi deity during the purification of Izani no Mikoto, and rituals such as passing through grass rings and floating puppets are performed to purify impurities. ; Reitaisai: Also known as ``Sumo-kai Taisai'' or simply ``Sumo-kai Festival.'' October 12th to 14th. The most important festival at Sumiyoshi Shrine. It is said that the name originates from the fact that when Empress Jingu returned from Korea, she dedicated sumo and {{jalink|yabusame|Q1886157}} to the deity Sumiyoshi as a thank you for the blessings of the gods. At the festival, in addition to a procession of children, yabusame and youth sumo are offered. ; Shooting Festival : "Hoshasai". November 7th. This Shinto ritual is said to have its origins in the {{jalink|Dazaifu|Q144845}} official who, during the {{jalink|Emperor Yozei|Q349280}}'s offering in 878, performed a walking shot in the southwest (Urakimon) direction as a reward for the miraculous powers of the god Sumiyoshi who had ended the disaster of foreign pirates. A shooting ceremony is held in front of the shrine to pray for the protection of the nation. === Cultural assets === === Important cultural property (designated by the country) === * Main shrine (building) - {{jalink|Edo period|Q184963}} early period. Designated on April 13, 1922 (Taisho 11) === Fukuoka Prefecture designated cultural property === * Tangible cultural properties [https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~ri5t-mk/itiran/koukosiryo.html Archaeological materials list] (Fukuoka City cultural properties ). ** 6-piece copper sword (archaeological material) **: {{jalink|Bronze sword|Q11650186}} from the middle of the {{jalink|Yayoi period|Q207858}}. It is said that it was excavated from behind the shrine building, but the condition and location of the excavation are unknown. It is medium-slender, with a total length of around 34 centimeters. Designated October 29, 1958 [http://www.fsg.pref.fukuoka.jp/bunka/contents_detail.asp?table=t61&fields=f2293&id=1307-112&bunrui=kenn_yuke_biju_koko [Fukuoka Social Education Network ``Cultural Properties of Fukuoka Prefecture'']. . ** 5 copper hoko (archaeological material)**: {{jalink|bronze spear|Q11650189|bronze spear}} from the middle of the Yayoi period. It is said that it was excavated from behind the shrine building like the bronze dagger, but its condition and location are unknown. There is a theory that it is the founder of {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Shrine|Q11381857|WD=Q11381857}} located all over the country, and it is also considered one of the ``three great Sumiyoshi'' along with {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Taisha|Q705949|WD=Q705949}} in Osaka and {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shimonoseki City)|Q11381858|WD=Q11381858|lt=Sumiyoshi Shrine}} in Shimonoseki.{{Cite book |Japanese book |editor=Mutsuhiko Mori |title=Number Dictionary |publisher=Tokyodo Publishing |year=1987 |page=135}}.This is a shrine dedicated to {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Sanjin|Q1114013|WD=Q1114013}}, the guardian deities of navigation. There are over 2,300 {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Shrines|Q11381857|WD=Q11381857}} nationwide, {{ill|lt=Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|WD=Q122723}}{{ill|lt=Osaka City|Q35765|WD=Q35765}} {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi-ku|Q985702|WD=Q985702}}'s {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Taisha|Q705949|WD=Q705949}} is often considered the headquarters {{Refnest|group=Note|{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.sumiyoshitaisha.net/about/origin.html|title=The history of Sumiyoshi Taisha|accessdate=2021-04-25}}}} is described in the classic book "{{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Taisha Shindaiki|Q11381815|WD=Q11381815}}" handed down at Sumiyoshi Taisha. Tsukushi Okami gave my {{ill|lt=Aratama/Japanese Spirit|Q495568|WD=Q495568|lt=Aratama}} to {{ill|lt=Empress Jingu|Q232803|WD=Q232803}} {{ill|lt=Shimonoseki City|Q 203308|WD=Q 203308|lt=Anamon Yamada Village}} was enshrined, so {{ill||lt=Budate|UNKNOWN}}, the ancestor of {{ill||lt=Anamo Nao|UNKNOWN}}, enshrined {{jalink|Sumiyoshi Shrine}. (Shimonoseki City)|Q11381858|Sumiyoshi Shrine}} ({{ill|lt=Yamaguchi Prefecture|Q127264|WD=Q127264}}{{ill|lt=Shimonoseki City|Q203308|WD=Q203308}}) to pray for Aratama and Japanese soul.{{jalink|Mr. Tsumori|Q11555993 It is said that Teguri ({{ill|lt=Tamomi no Sukune|Q20041346|WD=Q20041346}}), the founder of |Tsumori}}, was enshrined at the shrine (Sumiyoshi Taisha) in Otsu-Nakakura-no-Nagakyo, and the Tsukushi Okami that represents our company is the origin of Sumiyoshi.{{Sfn|Engi|1982}}. He was revered as the national navigation god of {{ill|lt=Yamato Kingdom|Q2658252|WD=Q2658252}}, and from {{ill|lt=medieval times|Q12554|WD=Q12554}} was placed as {{ill|lt=Ichinomiya|Q1656379|WD=Q1656379}} of {{ill|lt=Chikuzen Province|Q1047664|WD=Q1047664}}, and was also worshiped by feudal lords and the general public as a god related to the sea. === Enshrined God === The following five deities are enshrined. . These five pillars are also collectively known as ``Sumiyoshi Gosho Okami.'' ; Main enshrined deity :* '''{{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Sankami|Q1114013|WD=Q1114013|lt=Sotsutsu no Omikoto}}''' (Sotsutsu no Onomikoto) :* '''{{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Mikami|Q1114013|WD=Q1114013|lt=Nakatsutsuo no Mikoto}}''' (Nakatsutsuo no Mikoto) :* '''{{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Mikami|Q1114013|WD=Q1114013|lt=Omotetsu Otoko no Mikoto}}''' (Uwatsutsu no Onomikoto) : The above three pillars are collectively called "{{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Sanjin|Q1114013|WD=Q1114013}}". ; Deity enshrined :* {{ill|lt=Amaterasu Omikami|Q455602|WD=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Omikami}} (Amaterasusume wolf) :* {{ill|lt=Empress Jingu|Q232803|WD=Q232803}} === About the enshrined deity === {{Double image stack|right|Sumiyoshi-taisha, keidai-2.jpg|Sumiyoshi-jinja (Shimonoseki) Honden.JPG|200|{{Center|Top: {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Taisha|Q705949|WD=Q705949}} ({{ill|lt=Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|WD=Q122723}}{{ill|lt=Osaka City|Q35765|WD=Q35765}})
Bottom: {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shimonoseki City)|Q11381858|WD=Q11381858|lt=Sumiyoshi Shrine}} ({{ill|lt=Yamaguchi Prefecture|Q127264|WD=Q127264}}{{ill|lt=Shimonoseki City|Q203308|WD=Q203308}})}}}}The main enshrined deities, the Sumiyoshi Sanjin, appear in two scenes in ``{{ill|lt=Kojiki|Q813031|WD=Q813031}}'' and ``{{ill|lt=Nihonshoki|Q813935|WD=Q813935}}.'' One is the birth scene, where {{ill|lt=Izanagi|Q813858|WD=Q813858}} (Izanagi no Mikoto), who returned from the land of Yomi, went to Ahakihara (Enohara) in Tachibana no Odo in Tsukushi-Hyuga to purify himself of the impurities.{{ill|lt=Misogi|Q1936265|WD=Q1936265}} Accordingly, these three Sumiyoshi gods were born along with {{ill|lt=Watatsumi|Q1474187|WD=Q1474187|lt=Watatsumi three gods}} (three sea gods) {{Sfn|Kojiki|1963|pp=28-30}}{{Sfn|Shoki|1967|pp=94-95}}. Other affiliated companies include Chiyomori Shrine (Chiyo, Hakata-ku, Fukuoka City), Shiteruhime Shrine (Gion-cho, Hakata-ku, Fukuoka City), and {{ill|lt=Tetsudo Shrine (Fukuoka City)|Q30932529|WD=Q30932529|lt=Tetsudo Shrine}} (Hakata Station Chuo-gai, Hakata-ku, Fukuoka City, {{ill|lt=JR Hakata City|Q11226208|WD=Q11226208}} rooftop). List of annual festivals
List of festivals held annually at Sumiyoshi Shrine [http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/index.html About festivals and events] (official website). . * January ** Saitan Festival (January 1st) ** Sumiyoshi Mikka Ebisu Shrine Annual Festival (January 3rd) **Oiina Festival (January 7th) *February **Setsubun Festival (February 3rd) ** Inari Shrine Hatsuuma Festival (February Hatsuuma Festival) ** National Foundation Memorial Festival (February 11th) * March ** Oda Festival (March 7th) ** Hitomaru Shrine Annual Festival (March 18th) *April ** Shiohi Festival (April 3rd) ** Amatsu Shrine Annual Festival (April 22nd) *　June ** Funatama Shrine Annual Festival (June 1st) ** Sukuhikona Shrine Annual Festival (June 8th) ** Great Purification Ceremony (June 30th) * July ** Nagoshi Festival (July 30th - August 1st) *August ** Sugawara Shrine Annual Festival (August 25th) *September ** Hayao Festival (September 4th) ** Shiga Shrine Annual Festival (September 9th) * October ** Inari Shrine Annual Festival (October 10th)** '''Reitaisai'' ('''Sumo Kai Taisai'''/Sumo Kai Festival) (October 12th-14th) ** Jingu Harukaishiki (October 17th) *November ** Ayusha Festival (November 7th) ** Inari Shrine Kazu Festival, Sukuhikona Shrine Annual Festival (November 8th) ** Kanpeisha Ranking Anniversary Festival (November 10th) ** New Grain Appreciation Festival (November 23rd) *December ** Great Purification Ceremony, New Year's Eve Festival (December 31st)
=== Main festivals === ;Oiina Festival : "Follow me." January 7th. As a prayer for the prosperity of the imperial family and the nation, the Onisube and Uso-kaeshi rituals are held [http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/winter.html Winter festivals and events] (official website). ; Oda Festival : "Ondasai". March 7th. A sowing ritual is held as a prayer for a rich harvest. ; Shiohi Festival : "Shiohisai". April 3rd. A mikoshi (portable shrine) is performed to pray for safe navigation and a bountiful catch. It is said that in the past, when the sea spread out in front of the gates, the shrine was celebrated by boat, but now it is performed on land. ; Nagoshi Grand Festival : “I want to relax.” July 30th to August 1st. It is a Shinto ritual related to the birth of Sumiyoshi deity during the purification of Izani no Mikoto, and rituals such as passing through grass rings and floating puppets are performed to purify impurities. ; Reitaisai: Also known as ``Sumo-kai Taisai'' or simply ``Sumo-kai Festival.'' October 12th to 14th. The most important festival at Sumiyoshi Shrine. It is said that the name originates from the fact that when Empress Jingu returned from Korea, she dedicated sumo and {{ill|lt=yabusame|Q1886157|WD=Q1886157}} to the deity Sumiyoshi as a thank you for the blessings of the gods. At the festival, in addition to a procession of children, yabusame and youth sumo are offered. ; Shooting Festival : "Hoshasai". November 7th. This Shinto ritual is said to have its origins in the {{ill|lt=Dazaifu|Q144845|WD=Q144845}} official who, during the {{ill|lt=Emperor Yozei|Q349280|WD=Q349280}}'s offering in 878, performed a walking shot in the southwest (Urakimon) direction as a reward for the miraculous powers of the god Sumiyoshi who had ended the disaster of foreign pirates. A shooting ceremony is held in front of the shrine to pray for the protection of the nation. === Cultural assets === === Important cultural property (designated by the country) === * Main shrine (building) - {{ill|lt=Edo period|Q184963|WD=Q184963}} early period. Designated on April 13, 1922 (Taisho 11) === Fukuoka Prefecture designated cultural property === * Tangible cultural properties [https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~ri5t-mk/itiran/koukosiryo.html Archaeological materials list] (Fukuoka City cultural properties ). ** 6-piece copper sword (archaeological material) **: {{ill|lt=Bronze sword|Q11650186|WD=Q11650186}} from the middle of the {{ill|lt=Yayoi period|Q207858|WD=Q207858}}. It is said that it was excavated from behind the shrine building, but the condition and location of the excavation are unknown. It is medium-slender, with a total length of around 34 centimeters. Designated October 29, 1958 [http://www.fsg.pref.fukuoka.jp/bunka/contents_detail.asp?table=t61&fields=f2293&id=1307-112&bunrui=kenn_yuke_biju_koko [Fukuoka Social Education Network ``Cultural Properties of Fukuoka Prefecture'']. . ** 5 copper hoko (archaeological material)**: {{ill|lt=bronze spear|Q11650189|WD=Q11650189|lt=bronze spear}} from the middle of the Yayoi period. It is said that it was excavated from behind the shrine building like the bronze dagger, but its condition and location are unknown. Designated October 29, 1958 [http://www.fsg.pref.fukuoka.jp/bunka/contents_detail.asp?table=t61&fields=f2293&id=1307-113&bunrui=kenn_yuke_biju_koko Dohoko] (Fukuoka Social Education Network ``Cultural Properties of Fukuoka Prefecture''). . === Cultural property designated by Fukuoka City === * Tangible Cultural Properties [https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~ri5t-mk/itiran/kenzoubutu.html List of Tangible Cultural Properties Buildings] (Fukuoka City Cultural Properties ). One is the birth scene, where {{ill|lt=Izanagi|Q813858|WD=Q813858}} (Izanagi no Mikoto), who returned from the land of Yomi, went to Ahakihara (Enohara) in Tachibana no Odo in Tsukushi-Hyuga to purify himself of the impurities.{{ill|lt=Misogi|Q1936265|WD=Q1936265}} Accordingly, these three Sumiyoshi gods were born along with {{ill|lt=Watatsumi|Q1474187|WD=Q1474187|lt=Watatsumi three gods}} (three sea gods) {{Sfn|Kojiki|1963|pp=28-30}}{{Sfn|Shoki|1967|pp=94-95}}. Next, in the scene of {{ill|lt=Empress Jingu|Q232803|WD=Q232803}} dispatching troops to Korea, Sumiyoshi possesses the empress and gives oracles to her, and the empress {{ill|lt=Sanghan Conquest|Q1124943 5|WD=Q1124943 5|lt=By cooperating with the Sanhan Conquest}}, the conquest will be successful.{{Sfn|Kojiki|1963|pp=132-134}} "Nihonshoki" states that upon their return from Korea, there was an oracle, and that they built a shrine to enshrine the Sumiyoshi god {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Aratama|UNKNOWN}} in Anamon Yamada village, and a shrine to enshrine {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Watama|UNKNOWN}} in Nakakura Nagakyo, Otsunoki. Among these theories, "Nihonshoki" "Nihonshoki" includes an article dated September 10, 9th year, 9th year of Emperor Chuai's reign, in the pre-Regency period of Empress Jingu. In , an article states that Empress Jingu ordered {{ill|lt=Yorami Otarami|Q24899491|WD=Q24899491|lt=Yorami Agohiko Tarumi}} to be the Shinto priest of Sumiyoshi God before the Sanhan Conquest {{Sfn |Shoki|1967|pp=335-336}} is the founding record of our company, and from this it is said that it was the earliest of all Sumiyoshi Shrines to be built {{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1978}}. There are various theories regarding the literal meaning of ``Tsutsunowo'' for the three Sumiyoshi deities, Sokozutsu no Mikoto, Nakazutsu no no Mikoto, and Omotzutsu no Mikoto. The word tutu is related to the evening moon, and refers to the evening moon, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=evening star|UNKNOWN}}, and the stars.As stars are used as guides for navigation, there are some theories that it refers to the god of the sea, {{Sfn|Kawaguchi|1993|p=148}}, a theory that it is seen as a ``Tsu man,'' a theory that sees ``tutu'' as a ship's cursed staff, and a tube that houses a ship's spirit. There is a theory that he is seen as a ``mametsu man'' in connection with the Tsutsu of Tsushima, and a theory that he is seen as a ``Tsutushimu'', a body with a weakened body that accompanies a voyage. === History === === Founding === Shrine (Chikuzen Province Sumiyoshi Daimyojin Engi Shrine collection. Collection: {{Cite book |Japanese book |title={{ill|lt=Shinto Taikei|Q11590923|WD=Q11590923}} Shrine Edition 44 - Chikuzen, Chikugo, Buzen, Bungo Province |publisher=Shinto Taikei Compilation Association |year=1982}}) compares the place where this Sumiyoshi Shrine is enshrined to the ancient site of Ahakihara, where the god Sumiyoshi was born.{{sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Heibonsha)|2004}}. With this, weThe company is said to be the ``Sumiyoshi Head Office'' or ``Japan's No. 1 Sumiyoshi Shrine,'' which has been the enshrined place since ancient times. It is based on the {{sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Heibonsha)|2004}}{{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Kadokawa)|1988}}{{Sfn|Ichinomiya system in medieval countries|2000|pp=576-577}}. In the ``Ancient Map of Hakata,'' a medieval illustrated map, the site of our company is topographically located between the Hie River and the Naka River. (Kyushu)|Q11642765|Q11642765|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Heibonsha)|2004}} It appears to be located on the cape of Reizeitsu that juts out from the mouth of the Naka River, and it is believed that this area was a suitable place for the worship of the guardian god of navigation.{{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Gods)|1984}}{{sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Heibonsha)|2004}} Also, in "{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Japanese Namesho|UNKNOWN}}", {{ill|lt=Chikuzen Province|Q1047664|WD=Q1047664}}{{ill|lt=Naka County (Fukuoka Prefecture)|Q11642798|WD=Q11642798|lt=Naka District}} There is a mention of the ancient place name ``Kaifu-go'', which is thought to be common to the {{ill|lt=Amajinbe|Q55528867|WD=Q55528867|lt=Amajin tribe}} villages, and from the precincts there is a mention of {{jal from the {{ill|lt=Yayoi period|Q207858|WD=Q207858}}. ink|Bronze halberd|Q11650186}} and {{ill|lt=Bronze spear|Q11650189|WD=Q11650189|lt=Bronze spear}} are said to have been excavated, so there is a theory that this area has been a sacred place for the Kaijin people since ancient times.{{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Gods)|1984}}.In addition, in the "Chikuzen Kuni Zoku Fudoki Shui", the original location of our company is {{ill|lt=Genjin Shrine|Q85882377|WD=Q85882377}} ({{ill|lt=Fukuoka Prefecture|Q123258|WD=Q123258}}{ {jalink|Nakagawa City|Q1206001}}). According to this legend, the current location of the Jinjin Shrine was along the coastline, and as the coastline receded, it was moved to the current location of Sumiyoshi, Hakata Ward. In the "Shikinaisha Investigation Report", there are ruins thought to belong to {{ill|lt=Nakoku|Q600473|WD=Q600473}} (such as {{ill|lt=Suku Okamoto Ruins|Q11473236|WD=Q11473236}}) located between Sumiyoshi Shrine and Genjin Shrine. Therefore, there is a theory that the rituals of the two shrines have been connected since ancient times as a shrine located upstream and downstream of {{ill|lt=Naka River|Q1076983|WD=Q1076983}} {{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1978}}. {{Location map+|Japan|width=230|float=right|caption={{Center|Distribution of Sumiyoshi Shrine (limited to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shikiuchi|UNKNOWN}})}}|places= {{Location map~|Japan|lat_deg=34|lat_min=36|lat_sec=44.60|lon_deg=135|lon_min=29|lon_sec=37.63|position=right|mark=Blue pog.svg|marksize=8|label={{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Taisha|Q705949|WD=Q705949}}}}{{Location map~|Japan|lat_deg=36|lat_min=58|lat_sec=29.08|lon_deg=140|lon_min=52|lon_sec=58.94|mark=Blue pog.svg|marksize=8}} {{Location map~|Japan|lat_deg=34|lat_min=58|lat_sec=0.38|lon_deg=135|lon_min=3|lon_sec=34.42|mark=Blue pog.svg|marksize=8}} {{Location map~|Japan|lat_deg=33|lat_min=59|lat_sec=58.75|lon_deg=130|lon_min=57|lon_sec=23.70|mark=Blue pog.svg|marksize=8}} {{Location map~|Japan|lat_deg=33|lat_min=35|lat_sec=9.26|lon_deg=130|lon_min=24|lon_sec=49.33|position=bottom|mark=Red pog.svg|marksize=8|label={{color|#FF0000|'''Sumiyoshi Shrine'''}}}}{{Location map~|Japan|lat_deg=33|lat_min=47|lat_sec=18.53|lon_deg=129|lon_min=42|lon_sec=23.43|mark=Blue pog.svg|marksize=8}} {{Location map~|Japan|lat_deg=34|lat_min=16|lat_sec=8.03|lon_deg=129|lon_min=18|lon_sec=54.18|mark=Blue pog.svg|marksize=8}} }}Also, when looking at shrines that enshrine Sumiyoshi deity nationwide, there are "{{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Taisha Shindaiki|Q11381815|WD=Q11381815}}" and "{{ill|lt=Engishiki|Q1342448|WD=Q1342448}}" {{ill|lt=Engishiki|Q1342448|WD=Q1342448}}. === Main festivals === ;Oiina Festival : "Follow me." January 7th. As a prayer for the prosperity of the imperial family and the nation, the Onisube and Uso-kaeshi rituals are held [http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/winter.html Winter festivals and events] (official website). ; Oda Festival : "Ondasai". March 7th. A sowing ritual is held as a prayer for a rich harvest. ; Shiohi Festival : "Shiohisai". April 3rd. A mikoshi (portable shrine) is performed to pray for safe navigation and a bountiful catch. It is said that in the past, when the sea spread out in front of the gates, the shrine was celebrated by boat, but now it is performed on land. ; Nagoshi Grand Festival : “I want to relax.” July 30th to August 1st. It is a Shinto ritual related to the birth of Sumiyoshi deity during the purification of Izani no Mikoto, and rituals such as passing through grass rings and floating puppets are performed to purify impurities. ; Reitaisai: Also known as ``Sumo-kai Taisai'' or simply ``Sumo-kai Festival.'' October 12th to 14th. The most important festival at Sumiyoshi Shrine. It is said that the name originates from the fact that when Empress Jingu returned from Korea, she dedicated sumo and {{ill|lt=yabusame|Q1886157|WD=Q1886157}} to the deity Sumiyoshi as a thank you for the blessings of the gods. At the festival, in addition to a procession of children, yabusame and youth sumo are offered. ; Shooting Festival : "Hoshasai". November 7th. This Shinto ritual is said to have its origins in the {{ill|lt=Dazaifu|Q144845|WD=Q144845}} official who, during the {{ill|lt=Emperor Yozei|Q349280|WD=Q349280}}'s offering in 878, performed a walking shot in the southwest (Urakimon) direction as a reward for the miraculous powers of the god Sumiyoshi who had ended the disaster of foreign pirates. A shooting ceremony is held in front of the shrine to pray for the protection of the nation. === Cultural assets === === Important cultural property (designated by the country) === * Main shrine (building) - {{ill|lt=Edo period|Q184963|WD=Q184963}} early period. Designated on April 13, 1922 (Taisho 11) === Fukuoka Prefecture designated cultural property === * Tangible cultural properties [https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~ri5t-mk/itiran/koukosiryo.html Archaeological materials list] (Fukuoka City cultural properties ). ** 6-piece copper sword (archaeological material) **: {{ill|lt=Bronze sword|Q11650186|WD=Q11650186}} from the middle of the {{ill|lt=Yayoi period|Q207858|WD=Q207858}}. It is said that it was excavated from behind the shrine building, but the condition and location of the excavation are unknown. It is medium-slender, with a total length of around 34 centimeters. Among these theories, "Nihonshoki" "Nihonshoki" includes an article dated September 10, 9th year, 9th year of Emperor Chuai's reign, in the pre-Regency period of Empress Jingu. In , an article states that Empress Jingu ordered {{ill|lt=Yorami Otarami|Q24899491|WD=Q24899491|lt=Yorami Agohiko Tarumi}} to be the Shinto priest of Sumiyoshi God before the Sanhan Conquest {{Sfn |Shoki|1967|pp=335-336}} is the founding record of our company, and from this it is said that it was the earliest of all Sumiyoshi Shrines to be built {{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1978}}. There are various theories regarding the literal meaning of ``Tsutsunowo'' for the three Sumiyoshi deities, Sokozutsu no Mikoto, Nakazutsu no no Mikoto, and Omotzutsu no Mikoto. The word tutu is related to the evening moon, and refers to the evening moon, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=evening star|1=UNKNOWN}}, and the stars.As stars are used as guides for navigation, there are some theories that it refers to the god of the sea, {{Sfn|Kawaguchi|1993|p=148}}, a theory that it is seen as a ``Tsu man,'' a theory that sees ``tutu'' as a ship's cursed staff, and a tube that houses a ship's spirit. There is a theory that he is seen as a ``mametsu man'' in connection with the Tsutsu of Tsushima, and a theory that he is seen as a ``Tsutushimu'', a body with a weakened body that accompanies a voyage. === History === === Founding === Shrine (Chikuzen Province Sumiyoshi Daimyojin Engi Shrine collection. According to this legend, the current location of the Jinjin Shrine was along the coastline, and as the coastline receded, it was moved to the current location of Sumiyoshi, Hakata Ward. === Main festivals === ;Oiina Festival : "Follow me." January 7th. As a prayer for the prosperity of the imperial family and the nation, the Onisube and Uso-kaeshi rituals are held [http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/winter.html Winter festivals and events] (official website). ; Oda Festival : "Ondasai". March 7th. A sowing ritual is held as a prayer for a rich harvest. ; Shiohi Festival : "Shiohisai". April 3rd. A mikoshi (portable shrine) is performed to pray for safe navigation and a bountiful catch. It is said that in the past, when the sea spread out in front of the gates, the shrine was celebrated by boat, but now it is performed on land. ; Nagoshi Grand Festival : “I want to relax.” July 30th to August 1st. It is a Shinto ritual related to the birth of Sumiyoshi deity during the purification of Izani no Mikoto, and rituals such as passing through grass rings and floating puppets are performed to purify impurities. ; Reitaisai: Also known as ``Sumo-kai Taisai'' or simply ``Sumo-kai Festival.'' October 12th to 14th. The most important festival at Sumiyoshi Shrine. It is said that the name originates from the fact that when Empress Jingu returned from Korea, she dedicated sumo and {{ill|lt=yabusame|Q1886157|WD=Q1886157}} to the deity Sumiyoshi as a thank you for the blessings of the gods. At the festival, in addition to a procession of children, yabusame and youth sumo are offered. ; Shooting Festival : "Hoshasai". November 7th. This Shinto ritual is said to have its origins in the {{ill|lt=Dazaifu|Q144845|WD=Q144845}} official who, during the {{ill|lt=Emperor Yozei|Q349280|WD=Q349280}}'s offering in 878, performed a walking shot in the southwest (Urakimon) direction as a reward for the miraculous powers of the god Sumiyoshi who had ended the disaster of foreign pirates. A shooting ceremony is held in front of the shrine to pray for the protection of the nation. === Cultural assets === === Important cultural property (designated by the country) === * Main shrine (building) - {{ill|lt=Edo period|Q184963|WD=Q184963}} early period. In , an article states that Empress Jingu ordered {{ill|lt=Yorami Otarami|Q24899491|WD=Q24899491|lt=Yorami Agohiko Tarumi}} to be the Shinto priest of Sumiyoshi God before the Sanhan Conquest {{Sfn |Shoki|1967|pp=335-336}} is the founding record of our company, and from this it is said that it was the earliest of all Sumiyoshi Shrines to be built {{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1978}}. There are various theories regarding the literal meaning of ``Tsutsunowo'' for the three Sumiyoshi deities, Sokozutsu no Mikoto, Nakazutsu no no Mikoto, and Omotzutsu no Mikoto. The word tutu is related to the evening moon, and refers to the evening moon, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=evening star|1=UNKNOWN}}, and the stars.As stars are used as guides for navigation, there are some theories that it refers to the god of the sea, {{Sfn|Kawaguchi|1993|p=148}}, a theory that it is seen as a ``Tsu man,'' a theory that sees ``tutu'' as a ship's cursed staff, and a tube that houses a ship's spirit. There is a theory that he is seen as a ``mametsu man'' in connection with the Tsutsu of Tsushima, and a theory that he is seen as a ``Tsutushimu'', a body with a weakened body that accompanies a voyage. === History === === Founding === Shrine (Chikuzen Province Sumiyoshi Daimyojin Engi Shrine collection.
