=== Main festivals === ;Oiina Festival : "Follow me." January 7th. As a prayer for the prosperity of the imperial family and the nation, the Onisube and Uso-kaeshi rituals are held [http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/winter.html Winter festivals and events] (official website). ; Oda Festival : "Ondasai". March 7th. A sowing ritual is held as a prayer for a rich harvest. ; Shiohi Festival : "Shiohisai". April 3rd. A mikoshi (portable shrine) is performed to pray for safe navigation and a bountiful catch. It is said that in the past, when the sea spread out in front of the gates, the shrine was celebrated by boat, but now it is performed on land. ; Nagoshi Grand Festival : “I want to relax.” July 30th to August 1st. It is a Shinto ritual related to the birth of Sumiyoshi deity during the purification of Izani no Mikoto, and rituals such as passing through grass rings and floating puppets are performed to purify impurities. ; Reitaisai: Also known as ``Sumo-kai Taisai'' or simply ``Sumo-kai Festival.'' October 12th to 14th. The most important festival at Sumiyoshi Shrine. It is said that the name originates from the fact that when Empress Jingu returned from Korea, she dedicated sumo and {{ill|lt=yabusame|Q1886157|WD=Q1886157|1=Yabusame}} to the deity Sumiyoshi as a thank you for the blessings of the gods. At the festival, in addition to a procession of children, yabusame and youth sumo are offered. ; Shooting Festival : "Hoshasai". November 7th. This Shinto ritual is said to have its origins in the {{ill|lt=Dazaifu|Q144845|WD=Q144845|1=Dazaifu (government)}} official who, during the {{ill|lt=Emperor Yozei|Q349280|WD=Q349280|1=Emperor Yōzei}}'s offering in 878, performed a walking shot in the southwest (Urakimon) direction as a reward for the miraculous powers of the god Sumiyoshi who had ended the disaster of foreign pirates. A shooting ceremony is held in front of the shrine to pray for the protection of the nation. === Cultural assets === === Important cultural property (designated by the country) === * Main shrine (building) - {{ill|lt=Edo period|Q184963|WD=Q184963|1=Edo period}} early period. Designated on April 13, 1922 (Taisho 11) === Fukuoka Prefecture designated cultural property === * Tangible cultural properties [https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~ri5t-mk/itiran/koukosiryo.html Archaeological materials list] (Fukuoka City cultural properties ). ** 6-piece copper sword (archaeological material) **: {{ill|lt=Bronze sword|Q11650186|WD=Q11650186|1=dōka}} from the middle of the {{ill|lt=Yayoi period|Q207858|WD=Q207858|1=Yayoi period}}. It is said that it was excavated from behind the shrine building, but the condition and location of the excavation are unknown. It is medium-slender, with a total length of around 34 centimeters. Designated October 29, 1958 [http://www.fsg.pref.fukuoka.jp/bunka/contents_detail.asp?table=t61&fields=f2293&id=1307-112&bunrui=kenn_yuke_biju_koko [Fukuoka Social Education Network ``Cultural Properties of Fukuoka Prefecture'']. . ** 5 copper hoko (archaeological material)**: {{ill|lt=bronze spear|Q11650189|WD=Q11650189|lt=bronze spear|1=dōhoko}} from the middle of the Yayoi period. It is said that it was excavated from behind the shrine building like the bronze dagger, but its condition and location are unknown. One is the birth scene, where {{ill|lt=Izanagi|Q813858|WD=Q813858|1=Izanagi}} (Izanagi no Mikoto), who returned from the land of Yomi, went to Ahakihara (Enohara) in Tachibana no Odo in Tsukushi-Hyuga to purify himself of the impurities.{{ill|lt=Misogi|Q1936265|WD=Q1936265|1=Misogi}} Accordingly, these three Sumiyoshi gods were born along with {{ill|lt=Watatsumi|Q1474187|WD=Q1474187|lt=Watatsumi three gods|1=Watatsumi}} (three sea gods) {{Sfn|Kojiki|1963|pp=28-30}}{{Sfn|Shoki|1967|pp=94-95}}. Next, in the scene of {{ill|lt=Empress Jingu|Q232803|WD=Q232803|1=Empress Jingū}} dispatching troops to Korea, Sumiyoshi possesses the empress and gives oracles to her, and the empress {{ill|lt=Sanghan Conquest|Q1124943 5|WD=Q1124943 5|lt=By cooperating with the Sanhan Conquest}}, the conquest will be successful.{{Sfn|Kojiki|1963|pp=132-134}} "Nihonshoki" states that upon their return from Korea, there was an oracle, and that they built a shrine to enshrine the Sumiyoshi god {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Aratama|1=UNKNOWN}} in Anamon Yamada village, and a shrine to enshrine {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Watama|1=UNKNOWN}} in Nakakura Nagakyo, Otsunoki. (Shimonoseki City)|Q11381858|Sumiyoshi Shrine}}, compared to {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Taisha|Q705949|WD=Q705949|1=Sumiyoshi-taisha}} in Osaka) {{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Gods)|1984}}.On the other hand, in our company's origin story, we attribute this to Awagihara, where the Sumiyoshi deity was born. }}{{Refnest|group=Notes|Approximately 10 kilometers west of Sumiyoshi Shrine is Hyuga Pass, and approximately 10 kilometers northeast is Aoyagi (Awagi?), Koga City. It is also associated with place names such as Mt. Tachibana (Tachibana?) and the foothills of Mt. Bito (Odo?) to the north. }}. Among these theories, "Nihonshoki" "Nihonshoki" includes an article dated September 10, 9th year, 9th year of Emperor Chuai's reign, in the pre-Regency period of Empress Jingu. In , an article states that Empress Jingu ordered {{ill|lt=Yorami Otarami|Q24899491|WD=Q24899491|lt=Yorami Agohiko Tarumi|1=Yosami no Otarumi}} to be the Shinto priest of Sumiyoshi God before the Sanhan Conquest {{Sfn |Shoki|1967|pp=335-336}} is the founding record of our company, and from this it is said that it was the earliest of all Sumiyoshi Shrines to be built {{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1978}}. There are various theories regarding the literal meaning of ``Tsutsunowo'' for the three Sumiyoshi deities, Sokozutsu no Mikoto, Nakazutsu no no Mikoto, and Omotzutsu no Mikoto. The word tutu is related to the evening moon, and refers to the evening moon, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=evening star|1=UNKNOWN}}, and the stars.As stars are used as guides for navigation, there are some theories that it refers to the god of the sea, {{Sfn|Kawaguchi|1993|p=148}}, a theory that it is seen as a ``Tsu man,'' a theory that sees ``tutu'' as a ship's cursed staff, and a tube that houses a ship's spirit. There is a theory that he is seen as a ``mametsu man'' in connection with the Tsutsu of Tsushima, and a theory that he is seen as a ``Tsutushimu'', a body with a weakened body that accompanies a voyage. === History === === Founding === Shrine (Chikuzen Province Sumiyoshi Daimyojin Engi Shrine collection. Collection: {{Cite book |Japanese book |title={{ill|lt=Shinto Taikei|Q11590923|WD=Q11590923|1=Shintō Taikei}} Shrine Edition 44 - Chikuzen, Chikugo, Buzen, Bungo Province |publisher=Shinto Taikei Compilation Association |year=1982}}) compares the place where this Sumiyoshi Shrine is enshrined to the ancient site of Ahakihara, where the god Sumiyoshi was born.{{sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Heibonsha)|2004}}. With this, weThe company is said to be the ``Sumiyoshi Head Office'' or ``Japan's No. 1 Sumiyoshi Shrine,'' which has been the enshrined place since ancient times. List of annual festivals
List of festivals held annually at Sumiyoshi Shrine [http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/index.html About festivals and events] (official website). . * January ** Saitan Festival (January 1st) ** Sumiyoshi Mikka Ebisu Shrine Annual Festival (January 3rd) **Oiina Festival (January 7th) *February **Setsubun Festival (February 3rd) ** Inari Shrine Hatsuuma Festival (February Hatsuuma Festival) ** National Foundation Memorial Festival (February 11th) * March ** Oda Festival (March 7th) ** Hitomaru Shrine Annual Festival (March 18th) *April ** Shiohi Festival (April 3rd) ** Amatsu Shrine Annual Festival (April 22nd) *　June ** Funatama Shrine Annual Festival (June 1st) ** Sukuhikona Shrine Annual Festival (June 8th) ** Great Purification Ceremony (June 30th) * July ** Nagoshi Festival (July 30th - August 1st) *August ** Sugawara Shrine Annual Festival (August 25th) *September ** Hayao Festival (September 4th) ** Shiga Shrine Annual Festival (September 9th) * October ** Inari Shrine Annual Festival (October 10th)** '''Reitaisai'' ('''Sumo Kai Taisai'''/Sumo Kai Festival) (October 12th-14th) ** Jingu Harukaishiki (October 17th) *November ** Ayusha Festival (November 7th) ** Inari Shrine Kazu Festival, Sukuhikona Shrine Annual Festival (November 8th) ** Kanpeisha Ranking Anniversary Festival (November 10th) ** New Grain Appreciation Festival (November 23rd) *December ** Great Purification Ceremony, New Year's Eve Festival (December 31st)
=== Main festivals === ;Oiina Festival : "Follow me." January 7th. As a prayer for the prosperity of the imperial family and the nation, the Onisube and Uso-kaeshi rituals are held [http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/winter.html Winter festivals and events] (official website). ; Oda Festival : "Ondasai". March 7th. A sowing ritual is held as a prayer for a rich harvest. ; Shiohi Festival : "Shiohisai". April 3rd. A mikoshi (portable shrine) is performed to pray for safe navigation and a bountiful catch. It is said that in the past, when the sea spread out in front of the gates, the shrine was celebrated by boat, but now it is performed on land. ; Nagoshi Grand Festival : “I want to relax.” July 30th to August 1st. It is a Shinto ritual related to the birth of Sumiyoshi deity during the purification of Izani no Mikoto, and rituals such as passing through grass rings and floating puppets are performed to purify impurities. ; Reitaisai: Also known as ``Sumo-kai Taisai'' or simply ``Sumo-kai Festival.'' October 12th to 14th. The most important festival at Sumiyoshi Shrine. It is said that the name originates from the fact that when Empress Jingu returned from Korea, she dedicated sumo and {{ill|lt=yabusame|Q1886157|WD=Q1886157|1=Yabusame}} to the deity Sumiyoshi as a thank you for the blessings of the gods. At the festival, in addition to a procession of children, yabusame and youth sumo are offered. ; Shooting Festival : "Hoshasai". November 7th. This Shinto ritual is said to have its origins in the {{ill|lt=Dazaifu|Q144845|WD=Q144845|1=Dazaifu (government)}} official who, during the {{ill|lt=Emperor Yozei|Q349280|WD=Q349280|1=Emperor Yōzei}}'s offering in 878, performed a walking shot in the southwest (Urakimon) direction as a reward for the miraculous powers of the god Sumiyoshi who had ended the disaster of foreign pirates. A shooting ceremony is held in front of the shrine to pray for the protection of the nation. === Cultural assets === === Important cultural property (designated by the country) === * Main shrine (building) - {{ill|lt=Edo period|Q184963|WD=Q184963|1=Edo period}} early period. Designated on April 13, 1922 (Taisho 11) === Fukuoka Prefecture designated cultural property === * Tangible cultural properties [https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~ri5t-mk/itiran/koukosiryo.html Archaeological materials list] (Fukuoka City cultural properties ). ** 6-piece copper sword (archaeological material) **: {{ill|lt=Bronze sword|Q11650186|WD=Q11650186|1=dōka}} from the middle of the {{ill|lt=Yayoi period|Q207858|WD=Q207858|1=Yayoi period}}. It is said that it was excavated from behind the shrine building, but the condition and location of the excavation are unknown. It is medium-slender, with a total length of around 34 centimeters. Designated October 29, 1958 [http://www.fsg.pref.fukuoka.jp/bunka/contents_detail.asp?table=t61&fields=f2293&id=1307-112&bunrui=kenn_yuke_biju_koko [Fukuoka Social Education Network ``Cultural Properties of Fukuoka Prefecture'']. . ** 5 copper hoko (archaeological material)**: {{ill|lt=bronze spear|Q11650189|WD=Q11650189|lt=bronze spear|1=dōhoko}} from the middle of the Yayoi period. It is said that it was excavated from behind the shrine building like the bronze dagger, but its condition and location are unknown. There is a theory that it is the founder of {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Shrine|Q11381857|WD=Q11381857|1=Sumiyoshi Shrine}} located all over the country, and it is also considered one of the ``three great Sumiyoshi'' along with {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Taisha|Q705949|WD=Q705949|1=Sumiyoshi-taisha}} in Osaka and {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shimonoseki City)|Q11381858|WD=Q11381858|lt=Sumiyoshi Shrine|1=Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shimonoseki)}} in Shimonoseki.{{Cite book |Japanese book |editor=Mutsuhiko Mori |title=Number Dictionary |publisher=Tokyodo Publishing |year=1987 |page=135}}.This is a shrine dedicated to {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Sanjin|Q1114013|WD=Q1114013|1=Sumiyoshi sanjin}}, the guardian deities of navigation. There are over 2,300 {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Shrines|Q11381857|WD=Q11381857|1=Sumiyoshi Shrine}} nationwide, {{ill|lt=Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|WD=Q122723|1=Osaka Prefecture}}{{ill|lt=Osaka City|Q35765|WD=Q35765|1=Osaka}} {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi-ku|Q985702|WD=Q985702|1=Sumiyoshi-ku, Osaka}}'s {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Taisha|Q705949|WD=Q705949|1=Sumiyoshi-taisha}} is often considered the headquarters {{Refnest|group=Note|{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.sumiyoshitaisha.net/about/origin.html|title=The history of Sumiyoshi Taisha|accessdate=2021-04-25}}}} is described in the classic book "{{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Taisha Shindaiki|Q11381815|WD=Q11381815|1=Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine Chronicles}}" handed down at Sumiyoshi Taisha. Tsukushi Okami gave my {{ill|lt=Aratama/Japanese Spirit|Q495568|WD=Q495568|lt=Aratama|1=Mitama}} to {{ill|lt=Empress Jingu|Q232803|WD=Q232803|1=Empress Jingū}} {{ill|lt=Shimonoseki City|Q 203308|WD=Q 203308|lt=Anamon Yamada Village}} was enshrined, so {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Budate|1=UNKNOWN}}, the ancestor of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Anamo Nao|1=UNKNOWN}}, enshrined {{jalink|Sumiyoshi Shrine}. (Shimonoseki City)|Q11381858|Sumiyoshi Shrine}} ({{ill|lt=Yamaguchi Prefecture|Q127264|WD=Q127264|1=Yamaguchi Prefecture}}{{ill|lt=Shimonoseki City|Q203308|WD=Q203308|1=Shimonoseki}}) to pray for Aratama and Japanese soul.{{jalink|Mr. Tsumori|Q11555993 It is said that Teguri ({{ill|lt=Tamomi no Sukune|Q20041346|WD=Q20041346|1=Tamomi no Sukune}}), the founder of |Tsumori}}, was enshrined at the shrine (Sumiyoshi Taisha) in Otsu-Nakakura-no-Nagakyo, and the Tsukushi Okami that represents our company is the origin of Sumiyoshi.{{Sfn|Engi|1982}}. He was revered as the national navigation god of {{ill|lt=Yamato Kingdom|Q2658252|WD=Q2658252|1=Yamato Kingship}}, and from {{ill|lt=medieval times|Q12554|WD=Q12554|1=Middle Ages}} was placed as {{ill|lt=Ichinomiya|Q1656379|WD=Q1656379|1=Ichinomiya}} of {{ill|lt=Chikuzen Province|Q1047664|WD=Q1047664|1=Chikuzen Province}}, and was also worshiped by feudal lords and the general public as a god related to the sea. === Enshrined God === The following five deities are enshrined. . These five pillars are also collectively known as ``Sumiyoshi Gosho Okami.'' ; Main enshrined deity :* '''{{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Sankami|Q1114013|WD=Q1114013|lt=Sotsutsu no Omikoto|1=Sumiyoshi sanjin}}''' (Sotsutsu no Onomikoto) :* '''{{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Mikami|Q1114013|WD=Q1114013|lt=Nakatsutsuo no Mikoto|1=Sumiyoshi sanjin}}''' (Nakatsutsuo no Mikoto) :* '''{{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Mikami|Q1114013|WD=Q1114013|lt=Omotetsu Otoko no Mikoto|1=Sumiyoshi sanjin}}''' (Uwatsutsu no Onomikoto) : The above three pillars are collectively called "{{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Sanjin|Q1114013|WD=Q1114013|1=Sumiyoshi sanjin}}". ; Deity enshrined :* {{ill|lt=Amaterasu Omikami|Q455602|WD=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Omikami|1=Amaterasu}} (Amaterasusume wolf) :* {{ill|lt=Empress Jingu|Q232803|WD=Q232803|1=Empress Jingū}} === About the enshrined deity === {{Double image stack|right|Sumiyoshi-taisha, keidai-2.jpg|Sumiyoshi-jinja (Shimonoseki) Honden.JPG|200|{{Center|Top: {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Taisha|Q705949|WD=Q705949|1=Sumiyoshi-taisha}} ({{ill|lt=Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|WD=Q122723|1=Osaka Prefecture}}{{ill|lt=Osaka City|Q35765|WD=Q35765|1=Osaka}})
Bottom: {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shimonoseki City)|Q11381858|WD=Q11381858|lt=Sumiyoshi Shrine|1=Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shimonoseki)}} ({{ill|lt=Yamaguchi Prefecture|Q127264|WD=Q127264|1=Yamaguchi Prefecture}}{{ill|lt=Shimonoseki City|Q203308|WD=Q203308|1=Shimonoseki}})}}}}The main enshrined deities, the Sumiyoshi Sanjin, appear in two scenes in ``{{ill|lt=Kojiki|Q813031|WD=Q813031|1=Kojiki}}'' and ``{{ill|lt=Nihonshoki|Q813935|WD=Q813935|1=Nihon Shoki}}.'' One is the birth scene, where {{ill|lt=Izanagi|Q813858|WD=Q813858|1=Izanagi}} (Izanagi no Mikoto), who returned from the land of Yomi, went to Ahakihara (Enohara) in Tachibana no Odo in Tsukushi-Hyuga to purify himself of the impurities.{{ill|lt=Misogi|Q1936265|WD=Q1936265|1=Misogi}} Accordingly, these three Sumiyoshi gods were born along with {{ill|lt=Watatsumi|Q1474187|WD=Q1474187|lt=Watatsumi three gods|1=Watatsumi}} (three sea gods) {{Sfn|Kojiki|1963|pp=28-30}}{{Sfn|Shoki|1967|pp=94-95}}. Next, in the scene of {{ill|lt=Empress Jingu|Q232803|WD=Q232803|1=Empress Jingū}} dispatching troops to Korea, Sumiyoshi possesses the empress and gives oracles to her, and the empress {{ill|lt=Sanghan Conquest|Q1124943 5|WD=Q1124943 5|lt=By cooperating with the Sanhan Conquest}}, the conquest will be successful.{{Sfn|Kojiki|1963|pp=132-134}} "Nihonshoki" states that upon their return from Korea, there was an oracle, and that they built a shrine to enshrine the Sumiyoshi god {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Aratama|1=UNKNOWN}} in Anamon Yamada village, and a shrine to enshrine {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Watama|1=UNKNOWN}} in Nakakura Nagakyo, Otsunoki. (Shimonoseki City)|Q11381858|Sumiyoshi Shrine}}, compared to {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Taisha|Q705949|WD=Q705949|1=Sumiyoshi-taisha}} in Osaka) {{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Gods)|1984}}.On the other hand, in our company's origin story, we attribute this to Awagihara, where the Sumiyoshi deity was born. }}{{Refnest|group=Notes|Approximately 10 kilometers west of Sumiyoshi Shrine is Hyuga Pass, and approximately 10 kilometers northeast is Aoyagi (Awagi?), Koga City. It is also associated with place names such as Mt. Tachibana (Tachibana?) and the foothills of Mt. Bito (Odo?) to the north. }}. Among these theories, "Nihonshoki" "Nihonshoki" includes an article dated September 10, 9th year, 9th year of Emperor Chuai's reign, in the pre-Regency period of Empress Jingu. In , an article states that Empress Jingu ordered {{ill|lt=Yorami Otarami|Q24899491|WD=Q24899491|lt=Yorami Agohiko Tarumi|1=Yosami no Otarumi}} to be the Shinto priest of Sumiyoshi God before the Sanhan Conquest {{Sfn |Shoki|1967|pp=335-336}} is the founding record of our company, and from this it is said that it was the earliest of all Sumiyoshi Shrines to be built {{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1978}}. There are various theories regarding the literal meaning of ``Tsutsunowo'' for the three Sumiyoshi deities, Sokozutsu no Mikoto, Nakazutsu no no Mikoto, and Omotzutsu no Mikoto. The word tutu is related to the evening moon, and refers to the evening moon, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=evening star|1=UNKNOWN}}, and the stars.As stars are used as guides for navigation, there are some theories that it refers to the god of the sea, {{Sfn|Kawaguchi|1993|p=148}}, a theory that it is seen as a ``Tsu man,'' a theory that sees ``tutu'' as a ship's cursed staff, and a tube that houses a ship's spirit. List of annual festivals
List of festivals held annually at Sumiyoshi Shrine [http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/index.html About festivals and events] (official website). . * January ** Saitan Festival (January 1st) ** Sumiyoshi Mikka Ebisu Shrine Annual Festival (January 3rd) **Oiina Festival (January 7th) *February **Setsubun Festival (February 3rd) ** Inari Shrine Hatsuuma Festival (February Hatsuuma Festival) ** National Foundation Memorial Festival (February 11th) * March ** Oda Festival (March 7th) ** Hitomaru Shrine Annual Festival (March 18th) *April ** Shiohi Festival (April 3rd) ** Amatsu Shrine Annual Festival (April 22nd) *　June ** Funatama Shrine Annual Festival (June 1st) ** Sukuhikona Shrine Annual Festival (June 8th) ** Great Purification Ceremony (June 30th) * July ** Nagoshi Festival (July 30th - August 1st) *August ** Sugawara Shrine Annual Festival (August 25th) *September ** Hayao Festival (September 4th) ** Shiga Shrine Annual Festival (September 9th) * October ** Inari Shrine Annual Festival (October 10th)** '''Reitaisai'' ('''Sumo Kai Taisai'''/Sumo Kai Festival) (October 12th-14th) ** Jingu Harukaishiki (October 17th) *November ** Ayusha Festival (November 7th) ** Inari Shrine Kazu Festival, Sukuhikona Shrine Annual Festival (November 8th) ** Kanpeisha Ranking Anniversary Festival (November 10th) ** New Grain Appreciation Festival (November 23rd) *December ** Great Purification Ceremony, New Year's Eve Festival (December 31st)
=== Main festivals === ;Oiina Festival : "Follow me." January 7th. As a prayer for the prosperity of the imperial family and the nation, the Onisube and Uso-kaeshi rituals are held [http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/winter.html Winter festivals and events] (official website). ; Oda Festival : "Ondasai". March 7th. A sowing ritual is held as a prayer for a rich harvest. ; Shiohi Festival : "Shiohisai". April 3rd. A mikoshi (portable shrine) is performed to pray for safe navigation and a bountiful catch. It is said that in the past, when the sea spread out in front of the gates, the shrine was celebrated by boat, but now it is performed on land. ; Nagoshi Grand Festival : “I want to relax.” July 30th to August 1st. It is a Shinto ritual related to the birth of Sumiyoshi deity during the purification of Izani no Mikoto, and rituals such as passing through grass rings and floating puppets are performed to purify impurities. ; Reitaisai: Also known as ``Sumo-kai Taisai'' or simply ``Sumo-kai Festival.'' October 12th to 14th. The most important festival at Sumiyoshi Shrine. It is said that the name originates from the fact that when Empress Jingu returned from Korea, she dedicated sumo and {{ill|lt=yabusame|Q1886157|WD=Q1886157|1=Yabusame}} to the deity Sumiyoshi as a thank you for the blessings of the gods. At the festival, in addition to a procession of children, yabusame and youth sumo are offered. ; Shooting Festival : "Hoshasai". November 7th. This Shinto ritual is said to have its origins in the {{ill|lt=Dazaifu|Q144845|WD=Q144845|1=Dazaifu (government)}} official who, during the {{ill|lt=Emperor Yozei|Q349280|WD=Q349280|1=Emperor Yōzei}}'s offering in 878, performed a walking shot in the southwest (Urakimon) direction as a reward for the miraculous powers of the god Sumiyoshi who had ended the disaster of foreign pirates. A shooting ceremony is held in front of the shrine to pray for the protection of the nation. === Cultural assets === === Important cultural property (designated by the country) === * Main shrine (building) - {{ill|lt=Edo period|Q184963|WD=Q184963|1=Edo period}} early period. Designated on April 13, 1922 (Taisho 11) === Fukuoka Prefecture designated cultural property === * Tangible cultural properties [https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~ri5t-mk/itiran/koukosiryo.html Archaeological materials list] (Fukuoka City cultural properties ). ** 6-piece copper sword (archaeological material) **: {{ill|lt=Bronze sword|Q11650186|WD=Q11650186|1=dōka}} from the middle of the {{ill|lt=Yayoi period|Q207858|WD=Q207858|1=Yayoi period}}. It is said that it was excavated from behind the shrine building, but the condition and location of the excavation are unknown. It is medium-slender, with a total length of around 34 centimeters. Designated October 29, 1958 [http://www.fsg.pref.fukuoka.jp/bunka/contents_detail.asp?table=t61&fields=f2293&id=1307-112&bunrui=kenn_yuke_biju_koko [Fukuoka Social Education Network ``Cultural Properties of Fukuoka Prefecture'']. . ** 5 copper hoko (archaeological material)**: {{ill|lt=bronze spear|Q11650189|WD=Q11650189|lt=bronze spear|1=dōhoko}} from the middle of the Yayoi period. It is said that it was excavated from behind the shrine building like the bronze dagger, but its condition and location are unknown. There is a theory that it is the founder of {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Shrine|Q11381857|WD=Q11381857|1=Sumiyoshi Shrine}} located all over the country, and it is also considered one of the ``three great Sumiyoshi'' along with {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Taisha|Q705949|WD=Q705949|1=Sumiyoshi-taisha}} in Osaka and {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shimonoseki City)|Q11381858|WD=Q11381858|lt=Sumiyoshi Shrine|1=Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shimonoseki)}} in Shimonoseki.{{Cite book |Japanese book |editor=Mutsuhiko Mori |title=Number Dictionary |publisher=Tokyodo Publishing |year=1987 |page=135}}.This is a shrine dedicated to {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Sanjin|Q1114013|WD=Q1114013|1=Sumiyoshi sanjin}}, the guardian deities of navigation. There are over 2,300 {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Shrines|Q11381857|WD=Q11381857|1=Sumiyoshi Shrine}} nationwide, {{ill|lt=Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|WD=Q122723|1=Osaka Prefecture}}{{ill|lt=Osaka City|Q35765|WD=Q35765|1=Osaka}} {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi-ku|Q985702|WD=Q985702|1=Sumiyoshi-ku, Osaka}}'s {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Taisha|Q705949|WD=Q705949|1=Sumiyoshi-taisha}} is often considered the headquarters {{Refnest|group=Note|{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.sumiyoshitaisha.net/about/origin.html|title=The history of Sumiyoshi Taisha|accessdate=2021-04-25}}}} is described in the classic book "{{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Taisha Shindaiki|Q11381815|WD=Q11381815|1=Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine Chronicles}}" handed down at Sumiyoshi Taisha. Tsukushi Okami gave my {{ill|lt=Aratama/Japanese Spirit|Q495568|WD=Q495568|lt=Aratama|1=Mitama}} to {{ill|lt=Empress Jingu|Q232803|WD=Q232803|1=Empress Jingū}} {{ill|lt=Shimonoseki City|Q 203308|WD=Q 203308|lt=Anamon Yamada Village}} was enshrined, so {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Budate|1=UNKNOWN}}, the ancestor of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Anamo Nao|1=UNKNOWN}}, enshrined {{jalink|Sumiyoshi Shrine}. (Shimonoseki City)|Q11381858|Sumiyoshi Shrine}} ({{ill|lt=Yamaguchi Prefecture|Q127264|WD=Q127264|1=Yamaguchi Prefecture}}{{ill|lt=Shimonoseki City|Q203308|WD=Q203308|1=Shimonoseki}}) to pray for Aratama and Japanese soul.{{jalink|Mr. Tsumori|Q11555993 It is said that Teguri ({{ill|lt=Tamomi no Sukune|Q20041346|WD=Q20041346|1=Tamomi no Sukune}}), the founder of |Tsumori}}, was enshrined at the shrine (Sumiyoshi Taisha) in Otsu-Nakakura-no-Nagakyo, and the Tsukushi Okami that represents our company is the origin of Sumiyoshi.{{Sfn|Engi|1982}}. He was revered as the national navigation god of {{ill|lt=Yamato Kingdom|Q2658252|WD=Q2658252|1=Yamato Kingship}}, and from {{ill|lt=medieval times|Q12554|WD=Q12554|1=Middle Ages}} was placed as {{ill|lt=Ichinomiya|Q1656379|WD=Q1656379|1=Ichinomiya}} of {{ill|lt=Chikuzen Province|Q1047664|WD=Q1047664|1=Chikuzen Province}}, and was also worshiped by feudal lords and the general public as a god related to the sea. === Enshrined God === The following five deities are enshrined. . These five pillars are also collectively known as ``Sumiyoshi Gosho Okami.'' ; Main enshrined deity :* '''{{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Sankami|Q1114013|WD=Q1114013|lt=Sotsutsu no Omikoto|1=Sumiyoshi sanjin}}''' (Sotsutsu no Onomikoto) :* '''{{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Mikami|Q1114013|WD=Q1114013|lt=Nakatsutsuo no Mikoto|1=Sumiyoshi sanjin}}''' (Nakatsutsuo no Mikoto) :* '''{{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Mikami|Q1114013|WD=Q1114013|lt=Omotetsu Otoko no Mikoto|1=Sumiyoshi sanjin}}''' (Uwatsutsu no Onomikoto) : The above three pillars are collectively called "{{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Sanjin|Q1114013|WD=Q1114013|1=Sumiyoshi sanjin}}". ; Deity enshrined :* {{ill|lt=Amaterasu Omikami|Q455602|WD=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Omikami|1=Amaterasu}} (Amaterasusume wolf) :* {{ill|lt=Empress Jingu|Q232803|WD=Q232803|1=Empress Jingū}} === About the enshrined deity === {{Double image stack|right|Sumiyoshi-taisha, keidai-2.jpg|Sumiyoshi-jinja (Shimonoseki) Honden.JPG|200|{{Center|Top: {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Taisha|Q705949|WD=Q705949|1=Sumiyoshi-taisha}} ({{ill|lt=Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|WD=Q122723|1=Osaka Prefecture}}{{ill|lt=Osaka City|Q35765|WD=Q35765|1=Osaka}})
Bottom: {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shimonoseki City)|Q11381858|WD=Q11381858|lt=Sumiyoshi Shrine|1=Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shimonoseki)}} ({{ill|lt=Yamaguchi Prefecture|Q127264|WD=Q127264|1=Yamaguchi Prefecture}}{{ill|lt=Shimonoseki City|Q203308|WD=Q203308|1=Shimonoseki}})}}}}The main enshrined deities, the Sumiyoshi Sanjin, appear in two scenes in ``{{ill|lt=Kojiki|Q813031|WD=Q813031|1=Kojiki}}'' and ``{{ill|lt=Nihonshoki|Q813935|WD=Q813935|1=Nihon Shoki}}.'' One is the birth scene, where {{ill|lt=Izanagi|Q813858|WD=Q813858|1=Izanagi}} (Izanagi no Mikoto), who returned from the land of Yomi, went to Ahakihara (Enohara) in Tachibana no Odo in Tsukushi-Hyuga to purify himself of the impurities.{{ill|lt=Misogi|Q1936265|WD=Q1936265|1=Misogi}} Accordingly, these three Sumiyoshi gods were born along with {{ill|lt=Watatsumi|Q1474187|WD=Q1474187|lt=Watatsumi three gods|1=Watatsumi}} (three sea gods) {{Sfn|Kojiki|1963|pp=28-30}}{{Sfn|Shoki|1967|pp=94-95}}. Next, in the scene of {{ill|lt=Empress Jingu|Q232803|WD=Q232803|1=Empress Jingū}} dispatching troops to Korea, Sumiyoshi possesses the empress and gives oracles to her, and the empress {{ill|lt=Sanghan Conquest|Q1124943 5|WD=Q1124943 5|lt=By cooperating with the Sanhan Conquest}}, the conquest will be successful.{{Sfn|Kojiki|1963|pp=132-134}} "Nihonshoki" states that upon their return from Korea, there was an oracle, and that they built a shrine to enshrine the Sumiyoshi god {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Aratama|1=UNKNOWN}} in Anamon Yamada village, and a shrine to enshrine {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Watama|1=UNKNOWN}} in Nakakura Nagakyo, Otsunoki. List of annual festivals
List of festivals held annually at Sumiyoshi Shrine [http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/index.html About festivals and events] (official website). . * January ** Saitan Festival (January 1st) ** Sumiyoshi Mikka Ebisu Shrine Annual Festival (January 3rd) **Oiina Festival (January 7th) *February **Setsubun Festival (February 3rd) ** Inari Shrine Hatsuuma Festival (February Hatsuuma Festival) ** National Foundation Memorial Festival (February 11th) * March ** Oda Festival (March 7th) ** Hitomaru Shrine Annual Festival (March 18th) *April ** Shiohi Festival (April 3rd) ** Amatsu Shrine Annual Festival (April 22nd) *　June ** Funatama Shrine Annual Festival (June 1st) ** Sukuhikona Shrine Annual Festival (June 8th) ** Great Purification Ceremony (June 30th) * July ** Nagoshi Festival (July 30th - August 1st) *August ** Sugawara Shrine Annual Festival (August 25th) *September ** Hayao Festival (September 4th) ** Shiga Shrine Annual Festival (September 9th) * October ** Inari Shrine Annual Festival (October 10th)** '''Reitaisai'' ('''Sumo Kai Taisai'''/Sumo Kai Festival) (October 12th-14th) ** Jingu Harukaishiki (October 17th) *November ** Ayusha Festival (November 7th) ** Inari Shrine Kazu Festival, Sukuhikona Shrine Annual Festival (November 8th) ** Kanpeisha Ranking Anniversary Festival (November 10th) ** New Grain Appreciation Festival (November 23rd) *December ** Great Purification Ceremony, New Year's Eve Festival (December 31st)
=== Main festivals === ;Oiina Festival : "Follow me." January 7th. As a prayer for the prosperity of the imperial family and the nation, the Onisube and Uso-kaeshi rituals are held [http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/winter.html Winter festivals and events] (official website). ; Oda Festival : "Ondasai". March 7th. A sowing ritual is held as a prayer for a rich harvest. ; Shiohi Festival : "Shiohisai". April 3rd. A mikoshi (portable shrine) is performed to pray for safe navigation and a bountiful catch. It is said that in the past, when the sea spread out in front of the gates, the shrine was celebrated by boat, but now it is performed on land. ; Nagoshi Grand Festival : “I want to relax.” July 30th to August 1st. It is a Shinto ritual related to the birth of Sumiyoshi deity during the purification of Izani no Mikoto, and rituals such as passing through grass rings and floating puppets are performed to purify impurities. ; Reitaisai: Also known as ``Sumo-kai Taisai'' or simply ``Sumo-kai Festival.'' October 12th to 14th. The most important festival at Sumiyoshi Shrine. It is said that the name originates from the fact that when Empress Jingu returned from Korea, she dedicated sumo and {{ill|lt=yabusame|Q1886157|WD=Q1886157|1=Yabusame}} to the deity Sumiyoshi as a thank you for the blessings of the gods. At the festival, in addition to a procession of children, yabusame and youth sumo are offered. ; Shooting Festival : "Hoshasai". November 7th. This Shinto ritual is said to have its origins in the {{ill|lt=Dazaifu|Q144845|WD=Q144845|1=Dazaifu (government)}} official who, during the {{ill|lt=Emperor Yozei|Q349280|WD=Q349280|1=Emperor Yōzei}}'s offering in 878, performed a walking shot in the southwest (Urakimon) direction as a reward for the miraculous powers of the god Sumiyoshi who had ended the disaster of foreign pirates. A shooting ceremony is held in front of the shrine to pray for the protection of the nation. === Cultural assets === === Important cultural property (designated by the country) === * Main shrine (building) - {{ill|lt=Edo period|Q184963|WD=Q184963|1=Edo period}} early period. Designated on April 13, 1922 (Taisho 11) === Fukuoka Prefecture designated cultural property === * Tangible cultural properties [https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~ri5t-mk/itiran/koukosiryo.html Archaeological materials list] (Fukuoka City cultural properties ). ** 6-piece copper sword (archaeological material) **: {{ill|lt=Bronze sword|Q11650186|WD=Q11650186|1=dōka}} from the middle of the {{ill|lt=Yayoi period|Q207858|WD=Q207858|1=Yayoi period}}. It is said that it was excavated from behind the shrine building, but the condition and location of the excavation are unknown. It is medium-slender, with a total length of around 34 centimeters. Designated October 29, 1958 [http://www.fsg.pref.fukuoka.jp/bunka/contents_detail.asp?table=t61&fields=f2293&id=1307-112&bunrui=kenn_yuke_biju_koko [Fukuoka Social Education Network ``Cultural Properties of Fukuoka Prefecture'']. . ** 5 copper hoko (archaeological material)**: {{ill|lt=bronze spear|Q11650189|WD=Q11650189|lt=bronze spear|1=dōhoko}} from the middle of the Yayoi period. It is said that it was excavated from behind the shrine building like the bronze dagger, but its condition and location are unknown. There is a theory that it is the founder of {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Shrine|Q11381857|WD=Q11381857|1=Sumiyoshi Shrine}} located all over the country, and it is also considered one of the ``three great Sumiyoshi'' along with {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Taisha|Q705949|WD=Q705949|1=Sumiyoshi-taisha}} in Osaka and {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shimonoseki City)|Q11381858|WD=Q11381858|lt=Sumiyoshi Shrine|1=Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shimonoseki)}} in Shimonoseki.{{Cite book |Japanese book |editor=Mutsuhiko Mori |title=Number Dictionary |publisher=Tokyodo Publishing |year=1987 |page=135}}.This is a shrine dedicated to {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Sanjin|Q1114013|WD=Q1114013|1=Sumiyoshi sanjin}}, the guardian deities of navigation. There are over 2,300 {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Shrines|Q11381857|WD=Q11381857|1=Sumiyoshi Shrine}} nationwide, {{ill|lt=Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|WD=Q122723|1=Osaka Prefecture}}{{ill|lt=Osaka City|Q35765|WD=Q35765|1=Osaka}} {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi-ku|Q985702|WD=Q985702|1=Sumiyoshi-ku, Osaka}}'s {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Taisha|Q705949|WD=Q705949|1=Sumiyoshi-taisha}} is often considered the headquarters {{Refnest|group=Note|{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.sumiyoshitaisha.net/about/origin.html|title=The history of Sumiyoshi Taisha|accessdate=2021-04-25}}}} is described in the classic book "{{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Taisha Shindaiki|Q11381815|WD=Q11381815|1=Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine Chronicles}}" handed down at Sumiyoshi Taisha. Tsukushi Okami gave my {{ill|lt=Aratama/Japanese Spirit|Q495568|WD=Q495568|lt=Aratama|1=Mitama}} to {{ill|lt=Empress Jingu|Q232803|WD=Q232803|1=Empress Jingū}} {{ill|lt=Shimonoseki City|Q 203308|WD=Q 203308|lt=Anamon Yamada Village}} was enshrined, so {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Budate|1=UNKNOWN}}, the ancestor of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Anamo Nao|1=UNKNOWN}}, enshrined {{jalink|Sumiyoshi Shrine}. (Shimonoseki City)|Q11381858|Sumiyoshi Shrine}} ({{ill|lt=Yamaguchi Prefecture|Q127264|WD=Q127264|1=Yamaguchi Prefecture}}{{ill|lt=Shimonoseki City|Q203308|WD=Q203308|1=Shimonoseki}}) to pray for Aratama and Japanese soul.{{jalink|Mr. Tsumori|Q11555993 It is said that Teguri ({{ill|lt=Tamomi no Sukune|Q20041346|WD=Q20041346|1=Tamomi no Sukune}}), the founder of |Tsumori}}, was enshrined at the shrine (Sumiyoshi Taisha) in Otsu-Nakakura-no-Nagakyo, and the Tsukushi Okami that represents our company is the origin of Sumiyoshi.{{Sfn|Engi|1982}}. He was revered as the national navigation god of {{ill|lt=Yamato Kingdom|Q2658252|WD=Q2658252|1=Yamato Kingship}}, and from {{ill|lt=medieval times|Q12554|WD=Q12554|1=Middle Ages}} was placed as {{ill|lt=Ichinomiya|Q1656379|WD=Q1656379|1=Ichinomiya}} of {{ill|lt=Chikuzen Province|Q1047664|WD=Q1047664|1=Chikuzen Province}}, and was also worshiped by feudal lords and the general public as a god related to the sea. === Enshrined God === The following five deities are enshrined. . The shrine's territory appears to be ``Sumiyoshi-sho'' in literature, and its affiliation continued through changes such as Goshirakawa-inryo, Senyomon-inryo, Fushimi-inryo, and Imperial family territory {{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Kadokawa)|1988}}. Orie Yokota, the chief priest of the {{ill|lt=Tenpo|Q1369045|WD=Q1369045|1=Tenpō}} era, revived Shinto rituals that had been forbidden by the {{ill|lt=Fukuoka Domain|Q208766|WD=Q208766|1=Fukuoka Domain}}. Wish, {{ill|lt=Hakozaki Shrine|Q714742|WD=Q714742|1=Hakozaki Shrine}} and the chief priests of {{ill|lt=Umi Hachimangu|Q924940|WD=Q924940|1=Umi Hachiman-gū}} and {{jalink|Kyoto|Q740 When he complained to the {{ill|lt=Ichijo family|Q1535498|WD=Q1535498|1=Ichijō family}} of 246}}, he was arrested and ordered to return home by the domain, and in 1833, he retired and {{ja link|Zashiki prison|Q11486150}}The Life of Chobei Omiwa, Yasukuni Ashitsu (Ashitsu Office, 2008) p42. === Precincts === [[File:Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka), honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Main shrine (Important cultural property)}}{{small|The style of the shrine building is "Sumiyoshi-zukuri". }}]] The area of the precincts is 8,107 tsubo (2.68 hectares) . Unlike Hakata, which is located on sand dunes, the area around the shrine grounds is located on the alluvial land of the Naka River.Among the shrine buildings in the precincts, the {{ill|lt=Shrine architecture #main shrine|Q3080012|WD=Q3080012|lt='''main shrine'''|1=Shinto architecture}} was built in the early {{ill|lt=Edo period|Q184963|WD=Q184963|1=Edo period}} period. (Japan)|Q635245|Genna}}9 year ({{ill|lt=1623|Q6818|WD=Q6818|1=1623}}) Built by {{ill|lt=Fukuoka domain|Q208766|WD=Q208766|lt=Fukuoka feudal lord|1=Fukuoka Domain}}{{ill|lt=Nagamasa Kuroda|Q950496|WD=Q950496|1=Kuroda Nagamasa}}. Along with {{ill|lt=Shinmei-zukuri|Q930545|WD=Q930545|1=Shinmei-zukuri}} and {{ill|lt=Taisha-zukuri|Q387874|WD=Q387874|1=Taisha-zukuri}}, it is said to be an old shrine style.''{{jalink |Sumiyoshizo|Q3503635}}''''' {{Sfn|Inagaki|2000|p=174}}{{Sfn|Yonezawa|2016|pp=112-113}} will be adopted. It is {{ill|lt=gabled construction|Q13308575|WD=Q13308575|1=Kirizuma-style}} with 4 girders (depth) and 2 beams (frontage), and the roof is {{ill|lt=cypress bark|Q90373477|WD=Q90373477|1=cypress bark roof}}. The straight lines of the roof and the three {{ill|lt=gables|Q4881511|WD=Q4881511|1=Bargeboard}} and {{ill|lt=chigi/katsuogi|Q87220234|WD=Q87220234|lt=chigi/kataogi|1=chigi and katsuogi}} reflect the ancient architecture. The pillars are painted vermilion and the wooden walls are painted white. {{Sfn|Seiji Okada|2011|pp=86-109}}. [http://www.fsg.pref.fukuoka.jp/bunka/contents_detail.asp?table=t6&fields=f767&id=1307-4&bunrui=kuni_yuke_kenz_juyo Sumiyoshi Shrine Main Hall] (Fukuoka Social Education Network ``Cultural Properties of Fukuoka Prefecture''). [http://bunkazai.city.fukuoka.lg.jp/cultural_properties/detail/140 Sumiyoshi Shrine Main Hall] (Fukuoka City Cultural Properties Protection Division ``Fukuoka City Cultural Properties''). .The {{ill|lt=Shrine architecture#haiden|Q3080012|WD=Q3080012|lt='''haiden'''|1=Shinto architecture}} built in front of the main shrine is {{ill|lt=gambling|Q855025|WD=Q855025|1=East Asian hip-and-gable roof}} and has a copper plate roof. In addition, {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Shrine Nohgakuden|Q132168040|WD=Q132168040|lt=Nogakuden|1=Nōgakuden, Sumiyoshi Jinja}} (Nogakuden) located on the south side of the precincts has been renovated due to the aging of {{ill|lt=Kego Shrine|Q11632314|WD=Q11632314|1=Kego Shrine}} (Tenjin, Chuo-ku, Fukuoka City) Nohgakuden. ink|Showa|Q327567}} Construction within Sumiyoshi Shrine was planned in 1935 ({{ill|lt=1935|Q18658|WD=Q18658|1=1935}}) and completed in 1938 ({{ill|lt=1938|Q18645|WD=Q18645|1=1938}}). {{ill|lt=Irimoya-zukuri|Q855025|WD=Q855025|1=East Asian hip-and-gable roof}} with a gable roof and a corrugated iron plate roof. This Noh theater hall is a modern Japanese-style building that combines traditional Japanese and Western styles, and has been designated as a designated cultural property by Fukuoka City. Precinct information board. . In addition, there are shrine buildings such as a Kagura hall and a Shinto gate within the precincts. {{small|It is said that Hojo-e rituals were held here in the old days. }} File:Tenryu Ike Sumiyoshi.JPG|Tenryu Pond (Shioiri Pond) === Sessha === There are a total of 8 Setsusha shrines, 2 Setsusha shrines and 6 Setsusha shrines. === Sessha === [[File:Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka), Shiga-jinja and Funarama-jinja.JPG|thumb|230px|right|{{center|Funatama Shrine (right) and Shiga Shrine (left)}}]] * Funatama Shrine - Enshrined deity: {{ill|lt=Sartahiko|Q3090037|WD=Q3090037|lt=Sarutahiko no Mikoto|1=Sarutahiko Ōkami}}. Regular festival: September 9th. * Shiga Shrine - Enshrined Deity: {{ill|lt=Watatsumi|Q1474187|WD=Q1474187|lt=Watatsumi Three Gods|1=Watatsumi}}. Regular festival: June 1st. === Suesha === * Sukuhikona Shrine - Enshrined deity: {{ill|lt=Sukunabikona|Q3275687|WD=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona no Mikoto|1=Sukunabikona}}. Regular festival: June 8th. * Inari Shrine - Enshrined deity: {{ill|WD=Q3080728|lt=Ukanomitama|Q3080728|WD=Q3080728|lt=Uga no Tamashii|1=Ukanomitama}}. Regular festival: October 10th. * Ebisu Shrine - Enshrined deity: {{ill|lt=Kotoshiro-shu|Q8009611|WD=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshiro-shu no Mikoto|1=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto}}. Regular festival: January 3rd. * Sugawara Shrine (Tenmangu) - Enshrined deity: {{ill|lt=Michizane Sugawara|Q382005|WD=Q382005|1=Sugawara no Michizane}}. Regular festival: August 25th. * Hitomaru Shrine - Enshrined deity: {{ill|lt=Kakimoto Hitomaro|Q380818|WD=Q380818|lt=Kakimoto Hitomaro|1=Kakinomoto no Hitomaro}}. Regular festival: March 18th. * Amatsu Shrine - Enshrined outside the west gate. Enshrined deity: {{ill|lt=Izanagi|Q813858|WD=Q813858|lt=Izanagi Okami|1=Izanagi}}. Regular festival: April 22nd. Other affiliated companies include Chiyomori Shrine (Chiyo, Hakata-ku, Fukuoka City), Shiteruhime Shrine (Gion-cho, Hakata-ku, Fukuoka City), and {{ill|lt=Tetsudo Shrine (Fukuoka City)|Q30932529|WD=Q30932529|lt=Tetsudo Shrine|1=Tetsudō Shrine}} (Hakata Station Chuo-gai, Hakata-ku, Fukuoka City, {{ill|lt=JR Hakata City|Q11226208|WD=Q11226208|1=JR Hakata City}} rooftop). File:Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka), Sukunahikona-jinja.JPG|Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka), Sukunahikona-jinja Shrine File:Uga Shrine in Sumiyoshi Shrine.JPG|Inari Shrine File:Sumiyoshi Shrine_Ebisu Shrine.jpg|Ebisu ShrineFile:Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka), Sugawara-jinja and Hitomaru-jinja.JPG|Sugawara Shrine (left, Tenmangu Shrine), Hitomaru Shrine (right) File:Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka), Amatsu-jinja.JPG|Amatsu Shrine === Festival === === Annual festival ===
List of annual festivals
List of festivals held annually at Sumiyoshi Shrine [http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/index.html About festivals and events] (official website). . * January ** Saitan Festival (January 1st) ** Sumiyoshi Mikka Ebisu Shrine Annual Festival (January 3rd) **Oiina Festival (January 7th) *February **Setsubun Festival (February 3rd) ** Inari Shrine Hatsuuma Festival (February Hatsuuma Festival) ** National Foundation Memorial Festival (February 11th) * March ** Oda Festival (March 7th) ** Hitomaru Shrine Annual Festival (March 18th) *April ** Shiohi Festival (April 3rd) ** Amatsu Shrine Annual Festival (April 22nd) *　June ** Funatama Shrine Annual Festival (June 1st) ** Sukuhikona Shrine Annual Festival (June 8th) ** Great Purification Ceremony (June 30th) * July ** Nagoshi Festival (July 30th - August 1st) *August ** Sugawara Shrine Annual Festival (August 25th) *September ** Hayao Festival (September 4th) ** Shiga Shrine Annual Festival (September 9th) * October ** Inari Shrine Annual Festival (October 10th)** '''Reitaisai'' ('''Sumo Kai Taisai'''/Sumo Kai Festival) (October 12th-14th) ** Jingu Harukaishiki (October 17th) *November ** Ayusha Festival (November 7th) ** Inari Shrine Kazu Festival, Sukuhikona Shrine Annual Festival (November 8th) ** Kanpeisha Ranking Anniversary Festival (November 10th) ** New Grain Appreciation Festival (November 23rd) *December ** Great Purification Ceremony, New Year's Eve Festival (December 31st)
=== Main festivals === ;Oiina Festival : "Follow me." January 7th. As a prayer for the prosperity of the imperial family and the nation, the Onisube and Uso-kaeshi rituals are held [http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/winter.html Winter festivals and events] (official website). ; Oda Festival : "Ondasai". March 7th. A sowing ritual is held as a prayer for a rich harvest. ; Shiohi Festival : "Shiohisai". April 3rd. A mikoshi (portable shrine) is performed to pray for safe navigation and a bountiful catch. It is said that in the past, when the sea spread out in front of the gates, the shrine was celebrated by boat, but now it is performed on land. ; Nagoshi Grand Festival : “I want to relax.” July 30th to August 1st. It is a Shinto ritual related to the birth of Sumiyoshi deity during the purification of Izani no Mikoto, and rituals such as passing through grass rings and floating puppets are performed to purify impurities. ; Reitaisai: Also known as ``Sumo-kai Taisai'' or simply ``Sumo-kai Festival.'' October 12th to 14th. The most important festival at Sumiyoshi Shrine. It is said that the name originates from the fact that when Empress Jingu returned from Korea, she dedicated sumo and {{ill|lt=yabusame|Q1886157|WD=Q1886157|1=Yabusame}} to the deity Sumiyoshi as a thank you for the blessings of the gods. At the festival, in addition to a procession of children, yabusame and youth sumo are offered. ; Shooting Festival : "Hoshasai". November 7th. This Shinto ritual is said to have its origins in the {{ill|lt=Dazaifu|Q144845|WD=Q144845|1=Dazaifu (government)}} official who, during the {{ill|lt=Emperor Yozei|Q349280|WD=Q349280|1=Emperor Yōzei}}'s offering in 878, performed a walking shot in the southwest (Urakimon) direction as a reward for the miraculous powers of the god Sumiyoshi who had ended the disaster of foreign pirates. A shooting ceremony is held in front of the shrine to pray for the protection of the nation. === Cultural assets === === Important cultural property (designated by the country) === * Main shrine (building) - {{ill|lt=Edo period|Q184963|WD=Q184963|1=Edo period}} early period. Designated on April 13, 1922 (Taisho 11) === Fukuoka Prefecture designated cultural property === * Tangible cultural properties [https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~ri5t-mk/itiran/koukosiryo.html Archaeological materials list] (Fukuoka City cultural properties ). ** 6-piece copper sword (archaeological material) **: {{ill|lt=Bronze sword|Q11650186|WD=Q11650186|1=dōka}} from the middle of the {{ill|lt=Yayoi period|Q207858|WD=Q207858|1=Yayoi period}}. It is said that it was excavated from behind the shrine building, but the condition and location of the excavation are unknown. It is medium-slender, with a total length of around 34 centimeters. Designated October 29, 1958 [http://www.fsg.pref.fukuoka.jp/bunka/contents_detail.asp?table=t61&fields=f2293&id=1307-112&bunrui=kenn_yuke_biju_koko [Fukuoka Social Education Network ``Cultural Properties of Fukuoka Prefecture'']. . ** 5 copper hoko (archaeological material)**: {{ill|lt=bronze spear|Q11650189|WD=Q11650189|lt=bronze spear|1=dōhoko}} from the middle of the Yayoi period. It is said that it was excavated from behind the shrine building like the bronze dagger, but its condition and location are unknown. Designated October 29, 1958 [http://www.fsg.pref.fukuoka.jp/bunka/contents_detail.asp?table=t61&fields=f2293&id=1307-113&bunrui=kenn_yuke_biju_koko Dohoko] (Fukuoka Social Education Network ``Cultural Properties of Fukuoka Prefecture''). . === Cultural property designated by Fukuoka City === * Tangible Cultural Properties [https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~ri5t-mk/itiran/kenzoubutu.html List of Tangible Cultural Properties Buildings] (Fukuoka City Cultural Properties ). [https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~ri5t-mk/itiran/komonjo.html List of books, classics, and old books] (Fukuoka City Cultural Properties ). ** Nohgakuden (building) - Built in 1938. Designated on March 23, 2000. ** Karamon (building) - Built in the Edo period. Designated on March 18, 2010. ** Matsuka Wakashu Volume 5 Volume 1 (Books, Classics, Old Books) - A collection of poems from the end of the {{ill|lt=Kamakura period|Q236205|WD=Q236205|1=Kamakura period}}. Designated on March 30, 1987. ** 27 Sumiyoshi Shrine documents (books, classics, old books) - Documents from the Kamakura period onwards. There is a theory that it is the founder of {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Shrine|Q11381857|WD=Q11381857|1=Sumiyoshi Shrine}} located all over the country, and it is also considered one of the ``three great Sumiyoshi'' along with {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Taisha|Q705949|WD=Q705949|1=Sumiyoshi-taisha}} in Osaka and {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shimonoseki City)|Q11381858|WD=Q11381858|lt=Sumiyoshi Shrine|1=Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shimonoseki)}} in Shimonoseki.{{Cite book |Japanese book |editor=Mutsuhiko Mori |title=Number Dictionary |publisher=Tokyodo Publishing |year=1987 |page=135}}.This is a shrine dedicated to {{ill|lt=Sumiyoshi Sanjin|Q1114013|WD=Q1114013|1=Sumiyoshi sanjin}}, the guardian deities of navigation. There are various theories regarding the literal meaning of ``Tsutsunowo'' for the three Sumiyoshi deities, Sokozutsu no Mikoto, Nakazutsu no no Mikoto, and Omotzutsu no Mikoto. The word tutu is related to the evening moon, and refers to the evening moon, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=evening star|1=UNKNOWN}}, and the stars.As stars are used as guides for navigation, there are some theories that it refers to the god of the sea, {{Sfn|Kawaguchi|1993|p=148}}, a theory that it is seen as a ``Tsu man,'' a theory that sees ``tutu'' as a ship's cursed staff, and a tube that houses a ship's spirit. At this time, {{ill|lt=Bettoji|Q11396755|WD=Q11396755|1=Bettō-ji}} was Shokazan Enpukuji {{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Kadokawa)|1988}}. ==== Modern times and later ==== After {{ill|lt=Meiji Restoration|Q8707|WD=Q8707|1=Meiji Restoration}}, in {{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}}5 ({{ill|lt=1872|Q7753|WD=Q7753|1=1872}}), {{ill|lt=modern company rank system|Q712534|WD=Q712534|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} was established. and was promoted to {{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Kadokawa)|1988}} in {{ill|lt=Taisho|Q329174|WD=Q329174|1=Taishō era}}14 ({{ill|lt=1925|Q18107|WD=Q18107|1=1925}}). After the war, it was listed as {{ill|lt=Beppyō Shrine|Q10898274|WD=Q10898274|1=Beppyo shrine}} of {{ill|lt=Shinja Honcho|Q908077|WD=Q908077|1=Association of Shinto Shrines}}.{{ill|lt=Heisei|Q234510|WD=Q234510|1=Heisei era}} From 2016 ({{ill|lt=2004|Q2014|WD=Q2014|1=2004}}), excavation surveys have begun around the precincts (Sumiyoshi Shrine ruins) {{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine ruins 1st survey report|2006|p=6}}. In a total of three surveys up to 2014 ({{ill|lt=2014|Q1999|WD=Q1999|1=2014}}), the remains of a mansion from the medieval to early modern period were discovered along with artifacts related to rituals. The shrine's territory appears to be ``Sumiyoshi-sho'' in literature, and its affiliation continued through changes such as Goshirakawa-inryo, Senyomon-inryo, Fushimi-inryo, and Imperial family territory {{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Kadokawa)|1988}}. === Main festivals === ;Oiina Festival : "Follow me." January 7th. As a prayer for the prosperity of the imperial family and the nation, the Onisube and Uso-kaeshi rituals are held [http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/winter.html Winter festivals and events] (official website). ; Oda Festival : "Ondasai". March 7th. A sowing ritual is held as a prayer for a rich harvest. ; Shiohi Festival : "Shiohisai". April 3rd. A mikoshi (portable shrine) is performed to pray for safe navigation and a bountiful catch. It is said that in the past, when the sea spread out in front of the gates, the shrine was celebrated by boat, but now it is performed on land. ; Nagoshi Grand Festival : “I want to relax.” July 30th to August 1st. It is a Shinto ritual related to the birth of Sumiyoshi deity during the purification of Izani no Mikoto, and rituals such as passing through grass rings and floating puppets are performed to purify impurities. ; Reitaisai: Also known as ``Sumo-kai Taisai'' or simply ``Sumo-kai Festival.'' October 12th to 14th. The most important festival at Sumiyoshi Shrine. It is said that the name originates from the fact that when Empress Jingu returned from Korea, she dedicated sumo and {{ill|lt=yabusame|Q1886157|WD=Q1886157|1=Yabusame}} to the deity Sumiyoshi as a thank you for the blessings of the gods. At the festival, in addition to a procession of children, yabusame and youth sumo are offered. ; Shooting Festival : "Hoshasai". November 7th. This Shinto ritual is said to have its origins in the {{ill|lt=Dazaifu|Q144845|WD=Q144845|1=Dazaifu (government)}} official who, during the {{ill|lt=Emperor Yozei|Q349280|WD=Q349280|1=Emperor Yōzei}}'s offering in 878, performed a walking shot in the southwest (Urakimon) direction as a reward for the miraculous powers of the god Sumiyoshi who had ended the disaster of foreign pirates. A shooting ceremony is held in front of the shrine to pray for the protection of the nation. === Cultural assets === === Important cultural property (designated by the country) === * Main shrine (building) - {{ill|lt=Edo period|Q184963|WD=Q184963|1=Edo period}} early period. There are various theories regarding the literal meaning of ``Tsutsunowo'' for the three Sumiyoshi deities, Sokozutsu no Mikoto, Nakazutsu no no Mikoto, and Omotzutsu no Mikoto. The word tutu is related to the evening moon, and refers to the evening moon, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=evening star|1=UNKNOWN}}, and the stars.As stars are used as guides for navigation, there are some theories that it refers to the god of the sea, {{Sfn|Kawaguchi|1993|p=148}}, a theory that it is seen as a ``Tsu man,'' a theory that sees ``tutu'' as a ship's cursed staff, and a tube that houses a ship's spirit. There is a theory that he is seen as a ``mametsu man'' in connection with the Tsutsu of Tsushima, and a theory that he is seen as a ``Tsutushimu'', a body with a weakened body that accompanies a voyage. === History === === Founding === Shrine (Chikuzen Province Sumiyoshi Daimyojin Engi Shrine collection. === Main festivals === ;Oiina Festival : "Follow me." January 7th. As a prayer for the prosperity of the imperial family and the nation, the Onisube and Uso-kaeshi rituals are held [http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/winter.html Winter festivals and events] (official website). ; Oda Festival : "Ondasai". March 7th. A sowing ritual is held as a prayer for a rich harvest. ; Shiohi Festival : "Shiohisai". April 3rd. A mikoshi (portable shrine) is performed to pray for safe navigation and a bountiful catch. It is said that in the past, when the sea spread out in front of the gates, the shrine was celebrated by boat, but now it is performed on land. ; Nagoshi Grand Festival : “I want to relax.” July 30th to August 1st. It is a Shinto ritual related to the birth of Sumiyoshi deity during the purification of Izani no Mikoto, and rituals such as passing through grass rings and floating puppets are performed to purify impurities. ; Reitaisai: Also known as ``Sumo-kai Taisai'' or simply ``Sumo-kai Festival.'' October 12th to 14th. The most important festival at Sumiyoshi Shrine. It is said that the name originates from the fact that when Empress Jingu returned from Korea, she dedicated sumo and {{ill|lt=yabusame|Q1886157|WD=Q1886157|1=Yabusame}} to the deity Sumiyoshi as a thank you for the blessings of the gods. At the festival, in addition to a procession of children, yabusame and youth sumo are offered. ; Shooting Festival : "Hoshasai". November 7th. This Shinto ritual is said to have its origins in the {{ill|lt=Dazaifu|Q144845|WD=Q144845|1=Dazaifu (government)}} official who, during the {{ill|lt=Emperor Yozei|Q349280|WD=Q349280|1=Emperor Yōzei}}'s offering in 878, performed a walking shot in the southwest (Urakimon) direction as a reward for the miraculous powers of the god Sumiyoshi who had ended the disaster of foreign pirates. A shooting ceremony is held in front of the shrine to pray for the protection of the nation. === Cultural assets === === Important cultural property (designated by the country) === * Main shrine (building) - {{ill|lt=Edo period|Q184963|WD=Q184963|1=Edo period}} early period. There are various theories regarding the literal meaning of ``Tsutsunowo'' for the three Sumiyoshi deities, Sokozutsu no Mikoto, Nakazutsu no no Mikoto, and Omotzutsu no Mikoto. The word tutu is related to the evening moon, and refers to the evening moon, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=evening star|1=UNKNOWN}}, and the stars.As stars are used as guides for navigation, there are some theories that it refers to the god of the sea, {{Sfn|Kawaguchi|1993|p=148}}, a theory that it is seen as a ``Tsu man,'' a theory that sees ``tutu'' as a ship's cursed staff, and a tube that houses a ship's spirit. There is a theory that he is seen as a ``mametsu man'' in connection with the Tsutsu of Tsushima, and a theory that he is seen as a ``Tsutushimu'', a body with a weakened body that accompanies a voyage. === History === === Founding === Shrine (Chikuzen Province Sumiyoshi Daimyojin Engi Shrine collection. === Main festivals === ;Oiina Festival : "Follow me." January 7th. As a prayer for the prosperity of the imperial family and the nation, the Onisube and Uso-kaeshi rituals are held [http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/winter.html Winter festivals and events] (official website). ; Oda Festival : "Ondasai". March 7th. A sowing ritual is held as a prayer for a rich harvest. ; Shiohi Festival : "Shiohisai". April 3rd. A mikoshi (portable shrine) is performed to pray for safe navigation and a bountiful catch. It is said that in the past, when the sea spread out in front of the gates, the shrine was celebrated by boat, but now it is performed on land. ; Nagoshi Grand Festival : “I want to relax.” July 30th to August 1st. It is a Shinto ritual related to the birth of Sumiyoshi deity during the purification of Izani no Mikoto, and rituals such as passing through grass rings and floating puppets are performed to purify impurities. ; Reitaisai: Also known as ``Sumo-kai Taisai'' or simply ``Sumo-kai Festival.'' October 12th to 14th. The most important festival at Sumiyoshi Shrine. It is said that the name originates from the fact that when Empress Jingu returned from Korea, she dedicated sumo and {{ill|lt=yabusame|Q1886157|WD=Q1886157|1=Yabusame}} to the deity Sumiyoshi as a thank you for the blessings of the gods. At the festival, in addition to a procession of children, yabusame and youth sumo are offered. ; Shooting Festival : "Hoshasai". November 7th. This Shinto ritual is said to have its origins in the {{ill|lt=Dazaifu|Q144845|WD=Q144845|1=Dazaifu (government)}} official who, during the {{ill|lt=Emperor Yozei|Q349280|WD=Q349280|1=Emperor Yōzei}}'s offering in 878, performed a walking shot in the southwest (Urakimon) direction as a reward for the miraculous powers of the god Sumiyoshi who had ended the disaster of foreign pirates. A shooting ceremony is held in front of the shrine to pray for the protection of the nation. === Cultural assets === === Important cultural property (designated by the country) === * Main shrine (building) - {{ill|lt=Edo period|Q184963|WD=Q184963|1=Edo period}} early period. Among these theories, "Nihonshoki" "Nihonshoki" includes an article dated September 10, 9th year, 9th year of Emperor Chuai's reign, in the pre-Regency period of Empress Jingu. In , an article states that Empress Jingu ordered {{ill|lt=Yorami Otarami|Q24899491|WD=Q24899491|lt=Yorami Agohiko Tarumi|1=Yosami no Otarumi}} to be the Shinto priest of Sumiyoshi God before the Sanhan Conquest {{Sfn |Shoki|1967|pp=335-336}} is the founding record of our company, and from this it is said that it was the earliest of all Sumiyoshi Shrines to be built {{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1978}}. There are various theories regarding the literal meaning of ``Tsutsunowo'' for the three Sumiyoshi deities, Sokozutsu no Mikoto, Nakazutsu no no Mikoto, and Omotzutsu no Mikoto. The word tutu is related to the evening moon, and refers to the evening moon, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=evening star|1=UNKNOWN}}, and the stars.As stars are used as guides for navigation, there are some theories that it refers to the god of the sea, {{Sfn|Kawaguchi|1993|p=148}}, a theory that it is seen as a ``Tsu man,'' a theory that sees ``tutu'' as a ship's cursed staff, and a tube that houses a ship's spirit. There is a theory that he is seen as a ``mametsu man'' in connection with the Tsutsu of Tsushima, and a theory that he is seen as a ``Tsutushimu'', a body with a weakened body that accompanies a voyage. === History === === Founding === Shrine (Chikuzen Province Sumiyoshi Daimyojin Engi Shrine collection. According to this legend, the current location of the Jinjin Shrine was along the coastline, and as the coastline receded, it was moved to the current location of Sumiyoshi, Hakata Ward. In the "Shikinaisha Investigation Report", there are ruins thought to belong to {{ill|lt=Nakoku|Q600473|WD=Q600473|1=Nakoku}} (such as {{ill|lt=Suku Okamoto Ruins|Q11473236|WD=Q11473236|1=Suguokamoto Site}}) located between Sumiyoshi Shrine and Genjin Shrine. In the Shikigami Namecho|Q11064932|Shinmeicho}} (established in {{ill|lt=927|Q30470|WD=Q30470|1=927}}), {{ill|lt=Settsu Province|Q864163|WD=Q864163|1=Settsu Province}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Harima Province|1=UNKNOWN}}・{{ill|lt=Nagato Province|Q907382|WD=Q907382|1=Nagato Province}}・{{ill|lt=Chikuzen Province|Q1047664|WD=Q1047664|1=Chikuzen Province}}・{{ill|lt=Iki Province|Q1052938|WD=Q1052938|1=Iki Province}}・{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tsushima Province|1=UNKNOWN}}, there are descriptions of Sumiyoshi Shrines in each of them, so there is a theory that these shrines, including ours, had the intention of locating them at key points on the Korean route {{Sfn|Seiji Okada|2011|pp=86-109}}. === Main festivals === ;Oiina Festival : "Follow me." January 7th. As a prayer for the prosperity of the imperial family and the nation, the Onisube and Uso-kaeshi rituals are held [http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/winter.html Winter festivals and events] (official website). ; Oda Festival : "Ondasai". March 7th. A sowing ritual is held as a prayer for a rich harvest. ; Shiohi Festival : "Shiohisai". April 3rd. A mikoshi (portable shrine) is performed to pray for safe navigation and a bountiful catch. It is said that in the past, when the sea spread out in front of the gates, the shrine was celebrated by boat, but now it is performed on land. ; Nagoshi Grand Festival : “I want to relax.” July 30th to August 1st. It is a Shinto ritual related to the birth of Sumiyoshi deity during the purification of Izani no Mikoto, and rituals such as passing through grass rings and floating puppets are performed to purify impurities. ; Reitaisai: Also known as ``Sumo-kai Taisai'' or simply ``Sumo-kai Festival.'' October 12th to 14th. The most important festival at Sumiyoshi Shrine. It is said that the name originates from the fact that when Empress Jingu returned from Korea, she dedicated sumo and {{ill|lt=yabusame|Q1886157|WD=Q1886157|1=Yabusame}} to the deity Sumiyoshi as a thank you for the blessings of the gods. At the festival, in addition to a procession of children, yabusame and youth sumo are offered. ; Shooting Festival : "Hoshasai". November 7th. This Shinto ritual is said to have its origins in the {{ill|lt=Dazaifu|Q144845|WD=Q144845|1=Dazaifu (government)}} official who, during the {{ill|lt=Emperor Yozei|Q349280|WD=Q349280|1=Emperor Yōzei}}'s offering in 878, performed a walking shot in the southwest (Urakimon) direction as a reward for the miraculous powers of the god Sumiyoshi who had ended the disaster of foreign pirates. A shooting ceremony is held in front of the shrine to pray for the protection of the nation. === Cultural assets === === Important cultural property (designated by the country) === * Main shrine (building) - {{ill|lt=Edo period|Q184963|WD=Q184963|1=Edo period}} early period.
